0.content:
Albedo's Campsite (also: Albedo's camp, Albedo's outpost): Albedo's Campsite is a small laboratory outpost inside a cave in Dragonspine, used by the alchemist Albedo. It lies on the path from the Entombed City's Ancient Palace to its Outskirts.

It is a working field lab rather than a home: a place for research, cooking and alchemy, kept warm against Dragonspine's cold.

Places: At the cave mouth two lit torches warm anyone who approaches, and a cooking pot stands beside them. Inside are two workstations, four shelves stacked with research materials, and a crafting bench for alchemy. Barrels and crates are scattered around.

A record board is covered in his experimental reports. In-game flavour text jokes that the amount of incomprehensible content on it has grown again, and that the Traveler's help to him is what matters.

People: Albedo is the person tied to the place; his own entry carries his biography. The camp itself has no resident NPC in the sources read.

History: The wiki's galleries show the camp before the Princeps Cretaceus Chapter and again during the limited-time event quest "The Snowy Past", when an easel and equipment have been knocked over. Treat the event details as limited-time material.

Atmosphere: A cramped, warm cave of notes, glassware and alchemical clutter against the snow outside, with the hum of ongoing research. Good for quiet working conversations.

1.content: Albedo's Campsite is the cave laboratory in Dragonspine he uses for research, between the Entombed City's Ancient Palace and Outskirts. It has torches, a cooking pot, shelves of materials, workstations, an alchemy bench and a record board of his reports.

2.content:
Anemo Archon Statue (also: Statue of Barbatos, Barbatos Statue, Statue of the Anemo Archon): The Anemo Archon Statue is the large stone likeness of Barbatos, the Anemo Archon, standing in the plaza in front of Favonius Cathedral in Mondstadt City. It shows a hooded figure with two wings and hands cupped together.

Words are carved into its pedestal: "The Gateway of Celestia" (in the Teyvat script). It is the city's most recognisable shrine to the god of freedom, and the open plaza around it is a busy public square.

Appearance: The figure is hooded and winged, with its hands held together in a cup. The inscription "The Gateway of Celestia" runs along the base. Canon gives no dimensions, material or sculptor.

The statue is the visual centrepiece of the plaza, so festival decorations are arranged around it. The wiki's galleries show the plaza dressed for the Windblume Festival and for the Weinlesefest event of version 3.1.

People: By day the plaza is where a few townsfolk gather, among them a Knight of Favonius on duty (Aramis), the sister Grace, the informant Vile, the bard Six-Fingered Jose and the travelling scholar Sayid. Treat them as ordinary regulars rather than permanent fixtures.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact: sitting on the statue's cupped hands earns the achievement "Beloved of the Anemo Archon", and a hoop-running minigame around the plaza edge rewards a Luxurious Chest.

Atmosphere: A wide, open stone square with the cathedral behind it and the wind never quite still, matching Mondstadt's image as the city of freedom. Because the statue depicts the god who deliberately does not rule, it works as a place for quiet reflection or a public meeting spot rather than a seat of authority.

The inscription about the "Gateway of Celestia" is a good hook for a curious character to ask about, but canon gives no explanation, so do not supply one as fact.

3.comment: Anemo Archon Statue: Anemo Archon Statue inscription
3.content: The base of the Anemo Archon Statue in Mondstadt City is carved with the line "The Gateway of Celestia". Canon records the text but does not explain it.

4.content:
Angel's Share (also: Angels Share): Angel's Share is a tavern in Mondstadt City, established and funded by the long-standing Dawn Winery. Charles is its bartender, and the winery's owner Diluc sometimes takes a shift himself. It is the traditional home of Mondstadt's wine trade and has a friendly rival in the Cat's Tail.

The name is brewers' slang. Charles explains that some liquor is absorbed by barrels and some evaporates during distilling, and the makers call that lost share "the angels' share." The tavern sells drinks, not meals: visitors buy drink-based items from Charles, and its house special is the Dawn Winery's apple cider.

People: Charles works most nights and says he cares little for alcohol itself, it is simply his job. Occasionally Diluc, the winery's owner, tends the bar and gives him the night off, which Charles is grateful for. Regulars include the Knight of Favonius Bruce, the Adventurers' Guild branch master Cyrus, the adventurer Jack, Quinn, and by day Nelson and Payne. The bard Six-Fingered Jose performs here at night.

Patton is listed among the staff. In one official social-media post, a song Jose sings here mocks Diluc as "like a fine wine with too much ice", after which Charles throws the bard out. Charles is dry and measured: during the Stormterror crisis he said he was not worried, that people who numbed themselves with drink were frightened, and that the "Knight Who Emerges At Night" would not stand idle.

Atmosphere: A warm, busy, adult tavern in the city's heart: a counter and two floors, regulars who return night after night, a bard in the corner, and a bartender who keeps order quietly. The tavern does not accept credit or tabs. Mondstadt's famous love of wine is on display here; the menu also lists juices and cider.

Dawn Winery recruitment notices hang here, appealing to skilled fighters to defend the vineyard from boars. A job board carries posts almost exclusively from the Adventurers' Guild's Mondstadt branch. Charles voices an old-fashioned view: life is not all sweet fruit juice, it needs some bitter alcohol too.

History: The Dawn Winery opened the tavern and for a time held a near-monopoly on Mondstadt's wine trade. That ended when Diona became bartender at the Cat's Tail, which overnight became a serious challenger, though Angel's Share is still said to sell more. Elzer, the winery's long-serving butler, tried to hire Diona away to Angel's Share and was bitten for his trouble.

Margaret, owner of the Cat's Tail, noted that the Stormterror attacks cut the supplies of Angel's Share's popular drinks, but also that the tavern is supplied directly by the Dawn Winery, which gives it a decisive advantage. Charles said the tavern's variety of wines dropped during that period. Diluc stopped importing the strong Snezhnayan spirit Fire-Water because it did not suit local tastes, leaving one bottle from the original batch on display.

Quests: Scenes in Diluc's Noctua Chapter story quest "Darknight Hero's Alibi" take place at the tavern, where Diluc and the Knight Huffman wait on events. In the world quest "Equivalent Exchange" the Traveler fetches an unusual cocktail ingredient for Charles, who makes a special beverage from it.

Charles's favourite recommendations: Death After Noon, which he says is Captain Kaeya's favourite, and the Dawn Winery's apple cider. He offers a first cocktail free to new visitors.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tavern is open and operating; nothing in later content changes it.

5.content: Charles is the bartender employed by the Dawn Winery for more than a decade. He wears an amulet on a necklace, has a mustache and beard, and speaks with a calm, practical wit. He describes himself as uninterested in alcohol, comparing himself to Diona, who hates it. He answers to "Master Diluc" when talking about the owner.

6.comment: Angel's Share: The Origin of the Name
6.content: In the wine trade, the "angels' share" is the portion of liquor that soaks into the barrel wood and evaporates during distillation. Charles says brewers use the phrase for this loss, which is where the tavern's name comes from. The in-game map description confirms the tavern was established and funded by the Dawn Winery.

7.content: During the limited-time event Of Drink A-Dreaming (2.5), Luka, a worker at Angel's Share whom Charles credits with a talent for recruiting, ran "Bartender Academy Week", inviting the Traveler to try the job. The academy was originally meant to teach every kind of drink, but after an attendee mixed a drink from three hard liquors the sessions were restricted to non-alcoholic drinks. This was an event only; it is not a standing feature of the tavern.

8.content:
Apathic Interval (also: Interval of No Thought): The Apathic Interval is the first stage of being "uplifted" into the Temple of Space, the floating hall above Windrest Peak. Individuals chosen from vanished eras are cast here and must reach a state of complete emptiness, giving up every desire through Maranasati meditation, before they may enter the temple proper. Depending on the person this can take a few years or several centuries. The change is deep: it alters personality and leaves a person unable to obtain a Vision.

Asmoday made the Interval with the rest of the temple, and her Watchers Nihilita and Melanta could move through it freely when they brought people in. Its loading-screen text reads: existence is not, yet the world manifests; emptiness is full, yet cannot be stayed.

Geography: A set of platforms floating above a sea of red cubes called the Unbroken Sea. The cubes can be crossed only with the help of the juvenile Watcher Dex. The Interval was unlocked by the quest Lion's Celerity and can be revisited through a Teleport Waypoint.

Maranasati Caskets, cube-like guardians, occupy the platforms and attack any approaching life, imprisoning them in cages. The Interval is a separate stage in the Temple of Space and is not part of any of the exhibition halls.

People: Those who endured the Interval include the temple's Uplifted residents. Istoria spent centuries here, giving up his pursuit of truth and his longing for his loved ones. Calcerius of Remuria lost his faith in Phobos there. Venipi of King Deshret's time spent perhaps under a hundred years. Daozi says that after the Interval, none of them could receive a Vision. Watchers brought people in; after Asmoday vanished Ronova's Caskets took over its guard.

Yu Huangyi, speaking from the Mahavaipulya Chamber, says the Interval's torment and tempering eroded will and desire, which suited an ancient art of cutting away the "Three Deadly Selves", though a single good idea could revive a creative spark.

Culture: The Interval is the temple's rite of passage, a purely mental discipline: relinquish every desire by meditating and mastering your own thoughts. Success makes a person quiet and receptive, and those who passed treat it as a shared hardship.

History: Created by Asmoday. After she disappeared, Ronova installed the Maranasati Caskets to guard the area. The temple later announced that its uplifting had ended, so no new arrivals are expected. In 6.5, during Lion's Celerity, the Melanta-driven crisis cast the Traveler, Istoria, Zeitlind and Dex into the Interval; they escaped by destroying the Caskets with Dex and collecting Deathmuse Shards, without forgoing their desires.

In the Caskets' weak-spot fights Dex can seize the exposed core and strike the Casket down. After returning to the temple the group were puzzled that Paimon had not been pulled in with them.

Dangers: Maranasati Caskets and the Domain Keepers they summon; the Unbroken Sea, which cannot be crossed without Dex; and the Interval's pressure on identity.

Gameplay note: the Caskets cannot be damaged directly until their weak spot is exposed.

Atmosphere: Blank, silent and weightless: no landscape worth the name, only platforms over a red sea, the sense that wanting anything is the only thing that costs you here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 6.5 (and unchanged through 7.1) the Interval is still guarded by Caskets but no new people are being uplifted.

The Traveler's party escaped without sacrificing their desires; the system itself is intact, since Asmoday remains absent and Ronova's Caskets were not repealed.

9.content: Ronova created the Maranasati Caskets to guard the Apathic Interval. They attack approaching life forms and lock them in cages. They come in several forms; some summon Domain Keepers, some slam the ground or roll along a fixed path. Dex can grip an exposed weak spot and tear them apart, and each defeated Casket yields a Deathmuse Shard that he absorbs. The name echoes the Buddhist practice of mindfulness of death.

10.content:
Arcadia (also: Great Arcadia): Arcadia, also called Great Arcadia, was a civilization in Mondstadt's vast oak forests, between what are now Windrest Peak, Windrise and Windwail Highland. A part of Teyvat's unified civilization, it was a holy city of plenty, favoured by heaven, that worshipped Istaroth and Asmoday and later the Three Moons. It was entombed in endless winter when the War of Funerary Flame came.

Its survivors fled south and found shelter under Decarabian.

Geography: Arcadia was made of several city-states; a holy city was the capital, and one of the city-states, Elysium, was built north of it at Windrest Peak. Vast oakwoods that could weather storms and harsh winters surrounded it.

The Temple of Space was constructed near Elysium and the Thousand Winds Temple was dedicated to Istaroth.

Government: A high priest led the city, authorised by a divine envoy who gave them the Golden Bough of Nemorensis. The Gunnhildr Clan controlled Elysium and are described as scions of the hallowed line.

Religion: The Arcadians worshipped Istaroth, Master of Time, and Asmoday, Master of Space, building the Thousand Winds Temple for the first and the Temple of Space for the second; the two temples were once connected. Divine envoys did not answer people's questions, so the Arcadians turned to the Three Moons, gathering golden boughs from oak groves as moon offerings. They especially revered Canon, original goddess of the Frost Moon, as Prusmene.

The Golden Bough of Nemorensis was said to restore the city's glory. The wiki links the golden boughs to Moonlit Offering relics; the Frost Moon's worship in Arcadia is referred to in the quest The Unmanned Vessel (II).

History: Arcadia was called the eternal holy city, a land without sorrow where hunger was unknown. Prosperity kindled questioning, which stirred the gods' wrath. A disaster lifted the Temple of Space into the heavens, leaving Istaroth's temple behind on the ground. Then the War of Funerary Flame ended Eternity; Arcadia was entombed beneath an endless winter. The Knight of the Golden Bough, Gunnhildr, sought the Golden Bough in the frozen north to save it, found it withered, and led surviving Arcadians south to shelter under Decarabian.

The knight crossed the wastes to a grove that had survived the calamity, with a white tree no priest or envoy tended. The Jack Frost King, a self-proclaimed fae king bound by an old command, tested visitors with riddles; the knight defeated him in a duel, but the Bough had long withered. The Jack Frost King never grasped the loss and kept guarding the tree. The wiki links the withering to the spread of the Holy Soil of Primordial Ice.

Culture: Oak groves were sacred, and golden boughs were gathered for moon offerings. The city saw itself as eternal, and its holy status rested on divine envoys that said nothing when people asked questions.

People: The Gunnhildr Clan, scions of Arcadia's hallowed line, ruled Elysium; the Knight of the Golden Bough, Gunnhildr, led its survivors away.

Atmosphere: Holy oak groves and the stillness of a snow-buried ruin; the sense of a once-lavish holy city whose promise of eternity failed.

Quests: The world quest Secret Pirate Treasure has Kaeya send the Traveler into what he calls the 'Lost Arcadian Ruins' to lure Treasure Hoarders; it was a ruse, not a real treasure hunt. Arcadia is also mentioned by Mary-Ann in Rowboat's Wake.

Status as of 7.1: Long lost as a civilization; ruins and records only as of 7.1.

key: Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind
11.comment: Arcadia: Elysium and the Gunnhildr Clan
11.content: Elysium was an Arcadian city-state north of the holy city, at Windrest Peak, controlled by the Gunnhildr Clan, and hosted the Temple of Space. It is named in the text of the domain Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind.

12.comment: Arcadia: Knight of the Golden Bough
12.content: Gunnhildr, the Knight of the Golden Bough, journeyed across the frozen wastes in search of the legendary Golden Bough to restore Arcadia. The Jack Frost King, guarding a grove that had survived, tested the knight with riddles and trials until a duel decided it. The Bough had withered; the knight gave up on Arcadia, gathered the survivors and led them south to the high tower where a wicked dragon had been cast down, seeking refuge under Decarabian.

13.content:
Brightcrown Canyon: Brightcrown Canyon is a rocky canyon in the Brightcrown Mountains, on Mondstadt's north-western side. At its north-eastern end lies the eastern entrance to Stormterror's Lair, the ruined capital of the old storm god Decarabian. Hilichurls roam its ancient mechanical guards and ruins.

The canyon is part of the approach to Old Mondstadt. Anemo Rings are found along it, and a bard named Davy sits near the ruins overlooking Cider Lake.

Geography: A valley at the north-west coast of Cider Lake, flanked by ruins and walled by cliffs. Features include an Anemo Ring, Rock Piles, Ruins Torches and Seelie; calla lilies and small lamp grass grow here. The canyon's north-eastern part opens into Stormterror's Lair.

A worn path leads between the old city and a boar habitat, which the wiki takes as a sign the city's people hunted here.

Places: Its main landmark is the eastern gate to the ancient ring-shaped city that held Decarabian's tower. The Travel Guide describes the pass as still guarded by ancient mechanisms, without the soldiers who once held it for the King of Gales.

Part of the ruins was destroyed in a failed experiment by the witch Alice, who tried to control a Ruin Guard with a hilichurl strapped to it; the guard fell apart.

People: Davy, a bard in the standard Mondstadt bard outfit, stands outside the ruins above Cider Lake for inspiration. He is the ex-husband of the bard Myweiss, once billed with her as Mr. and Mrs. Lovebard, and is bitter about love.

Davy points travellers to crystal ore he noticed while seeking inspiration, and plans a ballad he calls the Manacles of Matrimony.

History: These ruins belong to Decarabian's walled capital, which rebels brought down around 2,600 years ago. The ancient mechanisms guarding the pass are remains of that age.

In the Prologue the lair beyond was where Dvalin was found; the canyon is the way in from the east.

Atmosphere: Weathered stone, wind and the creak of old machinery; empty, but not safe.

Dangers: Hilichurls, Samachurls, Mitachurls (Blazing Axe), Fatui Electro Cicin Mages, slimes of every element, and Ruin Guards.

Travel: Found on the north-west shore of Cider Lake, with the Brightcrown Mountains beyond.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing new is recorded; still ruined and dangerous.

14.comment: Brightcrown Canyon: Alice's Ruin Guard Experiment
14.content: In her travel diary, Alice records trying to command a Ruin Guard with a hilichurl and wrecking half the canyon's ruins.

15.content:
Brightcrown Mountains: The Brightcrown Mountains are the rugged northwestern part of Mondstadt. They hold Brightcrown Canyon and, at the heart of the range, the ruins of Old Mondstadt, the walled city of Decarabian, God of Storms. During the Prologue the ruins were Stormterror's Lair, the sleeping place of the dragon Dvalin.

Mondstadters do not live here. Hilichurls, slimes and Fatui skirmishers are the usual company in the canyon and ruins, and the bard Davy is met in the canyon, and the wind currents that help gliders also make the old city dangerous.

Geography: Cliffs, canyons and wind-scoured ruins. Brightcrown Canyon runs through the range and its northeastern end leads to the eastern entrance of Stormterror's Lair. The lair itself is the former capital, with Decarabian's Tower rising in the middle. A Boar Habitat in the mountains is notable for its many forest boars.

The canyon's northeastern end holds the eastern entrance to the lair. Broken arcades, stone stairs and wind currents link the levels of the old city up to the summit of the tower. No battle music plays in Stormterror's Lair, a gameplay detail rather than lore.

Places: Brightcrown Canyon; Stormterror's Lair (Old Mondstadt) with its entrance, and Decarabian's Tower at its centre; the Boar Habitat.

The tower's second-highest floor holds the "first Field Tiller", an inert Khaenri'ahn war machine; its top floor is where the God of Storms is implied to have personally lived, and the Confront Stormterror domain is entered there. The lowest floor of the tower is treated by the game as out of bounds, and Paimon warns the player away.

History: Old Mondstadt was Decarabian's capital until the rebellion about 2,600 years ago, when he was slain and Barbatos took his place; the people then moved to the island in Cider Lake. Five hundred years ago the dragon Dvalin, victorious but badly hurt by the corrupted Durin, fell asleep in the ruined capital. Mondstadt forgot him, feared him on waking and called him Stormterror, which is where the lair's name comes from.

The Abyss Order exploited the pain from the poisonous blood Durin left in Dvalin, which is the situation the Traveler found in the Prologue. A damaged Field Tiller, the first Ruin Guard prototype, once arrived here after a fight with Boreas in Wolvendom; for about a year it fired on anyone approaching the city, which Mondstadters took as a last fury of the dead Decarabian.

Dangers: Hilichurls and their samachurls, slimes and Fatui skirmishers; Eye of the Storm, mitachurl and Ruin Guard elite enemies in the lair; steep drops and strong air currents.

Atmosphere: Desolate and windy. Official viewpoint text describes murmuring winds shrouding a desolate city and telling a story no mortal now remembers, that of the nameless wind sprite who was the tower's master's downfall.

Travel: Local specialties include calla lily, windwheel aster and small lamp grass. Atop a rock formation in the southwest of the lair stands an unexplained camp with a sword stuck in the ground in front of a tent; its origin and purpose are not explained.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruins are quiet. The storm barrier from the Prologue is gone.

Dvalin was freed from the Abyss Order's hold long ago and is honoured again; the lair is no longer a site of crisis.

16.comment: Brightcrown Mountains: Stormterror's Lair and Decarabian's Tower
16.content:
Stormterror's Lair is what the Prologue called the ruins of Old Mondstadt. A storm barrier sealed it until the Archon Quest dispelled it. Decarabian's Tower stands in the middle of the ruined city and is climbed by wind current; its upper floors contain the first Field Tiller and the domain where Stormterror is confronted.

Official viewpoint text calls it the "Abandoned Capital of Howling Winds" and speaks of a nameless wind sprite and a chorus that made the tower quail, an allusion to the rebellion that ended Decarabian's rule.

17.content:
Cage of Suchness (also: Atrium of Suchness): The Cage of Suchness is the highest point of the Temple of Space, the floating hall above Windrest Peak in Mondstadt. It was the home of the god Asmoday and her two Watchers, Nihilita and Melanta, and from here they oversaw the temple. It lies beyond the Corridor of Nothingness and can be reached only by laying down all of one's memories. After Asmoday's disappearance it became the seat of the Watcher Melanta, who ruled the temple's inhabitants harshly until the Traveler defeated him there.

The room is cut off from the rest of the temple, so nothing short of the Path to the Heavens leads in or out. Wiki shorthand for the Temple of Space as a whole is "Segment-Domain Tau"; the Cage is its innermost, most private part.

Geography: The Cage sits at the very top of the temple, separated from the exhibition halls and the Pillar Hall Central Zone by the Corridor of Nothingness. The map shows it with a side chamber as a second level. The only approach is the Path to the Heavens, which runs through the Corridor.

Quest text sometimes calls the room the Atrium of Suchness. In the room the Traveler can find a damaged coffin and a note left by a visitor who claims to have escaped a containment vessel (see uncertainties).

People: Asmoday, Ruler of Space, lived here with her Watchers in the temple's early age; she is gone. Nihilita opened his eye after her disappearance, abandoned his duties and left, so only Melanta remained. Melanta used the Cage as his seat while he condemned Nihilita as a traitor and enforced the founding rules; his longing for Asmoday and his fear of her laws being corrupted drove him to cruelty.

Raumhilda, a traveller who had met Nihilita at Windrest Peak, reached the Cage once by sacrificing her memories to build the Path to the Heavens, and confronted Melanta there. They did not reach an accord. She promised that her younger sister Zeitlind would one day return and defeat him, and Melanta in a rage destroyed half the Corridor and severed the path.

Governance: Under Asmoday the temple's purpose was preservation alone: nothing new, no innovation, nothing taken out into the world. Under Melanta that became rigid enforcement, with punishment for anyone who blurred the lines. Those who wished to leave had to win an audience with Asmoday by offering up every memory and every scrap of wisdom, so that no knowledge of the temple could return to the mortal world.

History: The Cage was created with the rest of the temple by Asmoday. After she vanished and Nihilita left, Melanta took control, punished the Mahavaipulya Chamber, Luyang Academy and Desert Pavilion for changes that other Shades had allowed, and exiled a resident called "Maukie" for defiling the laws of space. In 6.5, during The Final Judgment, the Traveler and Zeitlind reached the Cage by offering Zeitlind's memories on top of Raumhilda's remnants, and the Traveler defeated Melanta in battle.

Melanta admitted afterwards that every creation became free the moment Asmoday disappeared. He also said his own actions, including severing the Path to the Heavens, set off his self-destruction; he confessed envy of Nihilita's freedom and a wish for Asmoday's approval, and his final words were directed at Nihilita. On the way, the Traveler relives the shared fantasies of the two sisters while drifting through the Corridor.

Atmosphere: A scene here is quiet, bare and heavily symbolic: a place that holds the weight of an absent god, with no wind, no sense of time and no bustle. It should feel like a stage after the play has ended.

Status as of 7.1: As of 6.5 and still at 7.1, Melanta is gone and the Cage is empty.

Melanta self-destructed after the battle with the Traveler, freeing the temple from his influence. Asmoday remains absent, and Nihilita was last seen outside the temple, at Windrest Peak. The Cage holds a damaged coffin whose text links it to the Traveler's sibling. No later canon through 7.1 has revisited the Cage.

18.content: Melanta, the Watcher who stayed, became the temple's tyrant in Asmoday's absence. He punished the inhabitants of the exhibition halls: those in the Mahavaipulya Chamber were pressed between pages, those of Luyang Academy turned to ink blots in paintings, and those of the Desert Pavilion turned to sand. When Domain Keepers began to fall onto Windrest Peak the temple's laws were visibly failing. The Traveler fought him in the Cage and he destroyed himself afterwards.

19.content:
Cape Oath: Cape Oath is a headland at the south-eastern corner of Mondstadt's surroundings, bordering Galesong Hill. A local legend says two lovers swore an oath to each other here, and young couples still come for the sunrise and sunset. A time tunnel on the cape leads to Musk Reef, the island that holds the entrance to the Spiral Abyss.

The drop in the terrain makes it easy to see Windrise, which sits facing the sea. Lovers treat Cape Oath as a favoured Windblume date spot.

Geography: A cape of grass and cliff edge looking over the sea, forming one side of the bay with Falcon Coast. Dandelion seeds grow in large numbers. The time tunnel does not appear on the world map but appears on the minimap close to it.

Reaching the tunnel means gathering the seelie around the Electro Slimes to raise a wind current that carries a glider up to it. Electro Hypostasis is found in the area as a boss; a Wooden Shieldwall Mitachurl, Fatui Cryogunners and Anemoboxers are among the foes.

Places: The Time Tunnel leads one way to Musk Reef, which holds the Spiral Abyss portal. Stepping through it earns the 'Initiating Warp Drive!' achievement.

Windrise lies within sight and Falcon Coast along the shore.

History: No narrative history is given for the cape beyond the lovers' legend. Musk Reef, its destination, was once the summit of a great mountain called Pilos Peak.

Before Barbatos reshaped Mondstadt about 2,600 years ago, Pilos Peak stood as a mountain on the continent. The adventurer Leonard failed to climb it, as his journal Of Mountains and Seas records. When Barbatos blew the snow away, the peak was swept from its place and the melted ice made the sea, leaving the island of Musk Reef.

Atmosphere: Open sky, sea air and wide views over the water; a romantic spot, especially at sunrise and sunset.

Dangers: Few: slimes and hilichurls, with Fatui scouts and the Electro Hypostasis nearby.

Travel: In the south-east corner of Mondstadt's surroundings; the time tunnel shows on the minimap on approach.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 unchanged.

20.comment: Cape Oath: Time Tunnel to Musk Reef
20.content: A one-way time tunnel at Cape Oath carries travellers to Musk Reef, where the Spiral Abyss portal stands. The island was once the summit Pilos Peak.

21.content:
Cecilia Garden (also: Cecilia Garden domain): Cecilia Garden is a Forgery domain near Wolvendom in Windwail Highland, Mondstadt. The entrance text says Cecilia flowers, which grow only on high cliffs, once bloomed here in greenhouses, and that the ancient civilisation that enjoyed their scent was lost along with the sea of white flowers. It is an ancient sacrificial altar flooded with Hydro energy, and clearing it yields weapon ascension materials.

A locked Anemo monument and four Seelie Courts stand outside the entrance and must be restored before the trial opens. The ruins' ornament resembles that of Stormterror's Lair.

Geography: The entrance lies in Windwail Highland by the forest of Wolvendom. Inside is a damp ancient altar chamber charged with Hydro energy.

Unlocking it means freeing the Seelie around the entrance monument. Unlike most domain doors it carries no Solomon's knot above its doorway.

History: Canon gives only the entrance blurb: a lost ancient civilisation grew Cecilia in greenhouses here, and both the people and the sea of white flowers vanished. The text does not name the civilisation. Venti calls Cecilia his favourite flower, and the Nameless Bard of Decarabian's age wore a stylised Cecilia, which hints at, but does not prove, a link to Old Mondstadt.

Dangers: The trial pits the Traveler against Hydro slimes, Hilichurls, Hydro Samachurls and, at the top level, Fatui Pyro Agents. The ley line disorder boosts Electro damage, so Electro wielders are favoured.

Atmosphere: Damp stone, ancient carved ornament, and the faint melancholy of a flower garden whose gardeners are gone.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the domain is open and unchanged since 1.0; nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content alters it.

22.content:
Cider Lake: Cider Lake is the large freshwater lake in Starfell Valley that holds the island on which Mondstadt City stands. Its water is crystal clear, cool and never freezes, and its headwaters are credited with Mondstadt's famous ciders and wines. It has become a symbol of the nation.

Official text says the lake looks unchanged for eons, so clear you can see the bottom, and is pleasant to drink.

Geography: Mondstadt City stands on a large island in the lake behind a stone wall. Wolvendom's shore, where Ross the Quick stands by a waypoint, faces the lake, and the bard Davy overlooks it from the ruins at Brightcrown Canyon. An Anemo Elemental Monument and fishing spots are found along the lake.

The Traveler says the lake's never-freezing waters are used to make drinks such as apple cider.

History: No origin is given; the lake is described as ancient and unchanged.

Atmosphere: Cool, clear water, windmills on the island and breezes across the surface.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 unchanged.

23.content: A sweet 'Cider Lake' drink with a little alcohol exists in Mondstadt; 'Sweet Cider Lake' is a juice-and-milk drink from the Of Drink A-Dreaming event.

24.content:
Dadaupa Gorge: Dadaupa Gorge is a rugged area of Galesong Hill in Mondstadt, home to three hilichurl tribes: the Meaty, the Sleeper and the Eclipse. At its centre lies the Forgotten Sword Cemetery, which witnessed the ancient battle against the monsters of Khaenri'ah.

The name Dadaupa means 'large mountain' in Hilichurlian, according to the Handy Handbook of Hilichurlian. Official text calls the place dangerous for the number of hilichurls and its Mitachurls and Samachurls.

Geography: A gorge with many hilichurl camps and three Elemental Monuments (Cryo, Electro and Pyro). The quest page describes the Sword Cemetery as standing in the middle of a large lake in the gorge. Calla lilies and dandelion seeds grow. Ruin Torches and Seelie can be found.

The three tribes are placed around the cemetery: the Meaty to the north, the Sleeper to the south and the Eclipse in the east valley.

Places: The Forgotten Sword Cemetery is protected by three layers of seal that can be broken by activating the monuments at the camps. The Temple of the Lion, an old temple to the Lion of the South, is also listed here by the wiki.

The cemetery's graves are marked with swords; Dr. Livingstone says the seals were set by survivors using elemental powers so their fallen comrades could rest. The Temple of the Lion is abandoned; folklore holds the dandelions on Mondstadt's winds symbolise the Lion of the South's blessing.

People: Dr. Livingstone, an adventurer who looks like a scholar and works with Dr. Edith, researches the cemetery. She gives the world quest Break the Sword Cemetery Seal.

After the Traveler breaks the seals, she stays to keep studying the many mysteries that remain at the cemetery.

History: The cemetery marks an ancient battlefield against Khaenri'ah's monsters; canon gives no further detail.

The account of survivors raising the triple seal comes from Dr. Livingstone's explanation in the world quest.

Atmosphere: Hilichurl fires and drum noise among steep rock, with a hush around the swords.

Dangers: Heavy hilichurl presence, including Mitachurls and Samachurls, Fatui skirmishers, Cryo Abyss Mages and slimes. Treat hilichurl camps as hostile.

Quests: Break the Sword Cemetery Seal (world quest), which unlocks a random Dr. Livingstone's Transport Request.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 hilichurls still hold the gorge and the cemetery remains studied.

25.content: A battlefield in Dadaupa Gorge guarded by three seals, said to mark the battle against Khaenri'ah's monsters. Breaking the seals means defeating the three hilichurl camps around it, after which a treasure is found at its centre.

26.content:
Dawn Winery (also: Dawn Winery estate, Manor of Daybreak): The Dawn Winery is the chief winery of Mondstadt, on a hill in Windwail Highland southwest of the capital. It specialises in dandelion wine and is the estate of the Ragnvindr family, which has owned it for about a thousand years. Its owner is Diluc Ragnvindr, who inherited it four years before the Prologue when his father Crepus died. A game viewpoint describes it as a pilgrimage site for anyone who loves the bottle.

Elzer, who handles its affairs and chairs the Mondstadt Wine Guild, says the winery is so successful that it effectively stands for Mondstadt's whole wine industry. Diluc also runs the Angel's Share tavern in the city, which belongs to the same business.

Geography: The estate lies in the south-western reaches of Mondstadt, between Springvale and the Stone Gate to Liyue. A two-storey manor stands on a small hill; the vineyard circles it in several rows, with a few storage sheds and single-storey buildings nearby. A lake southwest of the manor supplies the winery's water. Local specialties around it include calla lilies, Philanemo mushrooms and windwheel asters.

The official map description calls it an estate in the land southwest of the city that has handed down Mondstadt's traditional wines and ciders for generations. Each year's output is split: part is sold in Mondstadt and the rest goes out along the trade route south of the city. A Statue of the Seven stands in the area.

Places: The manor is the heart of the estate, and a game viewpoint is named for it ("Manor of Daybreak"). Inside, an owl statue carries an inscription urging the watcher of the night to remember the splendour of the dawn, and those who contend with evildoers to keep to righteousness. A signboard behind the manor marks an employee resting area.

Books found in and around the manor include parts of the series "A Drunkard's Tale", and volume 4 of the "Heart of Clear Springs" collection lies on a table by the stairs. The winery sign is written in Teyvat script and carries the name, a welcome and two short sayings (see uncertainties for the motto).

People: Diluc Ragnvindr is the owner. Elzer, executive chairman of the Mondstadt Wine Guild, handles the winery's affairs. Adelinde is the head housemaid, with the maids Hillie and Moco; Connor is the winemaker, Ernest the warehouse manager, Tunner a farmer. The late Crepus Ragnvindr, Diluc's father, owned the estate before him.

Delivery staff named in quests include Fritz, Ben and Magar, and a worker called Hartman. Staff of the Angel's Share tavern include the bartender Charles, the caller Patton and the winemaker Georg, with Luka also listed.

History: The Ragnvindr family has held the winery at least since Ragnvindr himself, about a thousand years ago. Crepus Ragnvindr died four years before the game begins and Diluc inherited the estate (see the Mondstadt entry for the disputed details of Crepus' death).

During the limited-time event Wishful Drops (1.4) the water sources near the winery turned bitter, which Katheryne warned could ruin Mondstadt's wine industry within a few years. Connor sent the Traveler to follow the water northwest; the cause was the young Oceanid Endora and the Oceanid Rhodeia's anger, not the water's composition.

Atmosphere: Fragrant with grapes and wine, orderly and hardworking, with signboards advertising seasonal juice and staff who treat the estate as a proud household.

Status as of 7.1: In operation as of 7.1, owned by Diluc.

Nothing in the pages read shows the estate changing hands or being damaged after the Prologue. Diluc has declined the Knights' invitation to return (see the Mondstadt entry).

27.comment: Dawn Winery: Dawn Winery motto and sign
27.content: Diluc's first Character Story gives the winery motto as "Shine True". His fifth story glosses it as: evil cannot go unpunished, never settle for mediocrity, never forget that the dawn will one day come. The in-game sign reads differently (a line about the flow of daylight, and "Forget not whence thou came"), so keep the two accounts separate.

28.comment: Dawn Winery: Wishful Drops and the bitter water
28.content: In the 1.4 event Wishful Drops, water sources on the Mondstadt-Liyue border turned bitter without warning, including the water near the winery. Connor explained that no ordinary purification removed the bitterness, so the water could not be used for wine. The Traveler traced it to the Oceanids: the young Oceanid Endora had come to Mondstadt, Rhodeia mistook her for a threat, and the clash soured the waters. Springvale's spring alone stayed sweet.

29.content:
Dawn Winery Manor (also: Manor of Daybreak, Diluc Manor): The Dawn Winery Manor is the central house of the Dawn Winery in Mondstadt's Windwail Highland, the Ragnvindr family estate that Diluc now owns. Its housemaids and butler run the winery's day-to-day affairs. Its name is unofficial: the manga calls it Diluc Manor, and the game's own text calls it the Manor of Daybreak.

The winery around it is Mondstadt's chief winery and specialises in dandelion wine, and has belonged to the Ragnvindrs for roughly a thousand years.

People: Adelinde is a polite young housemaid who spends most of her time cleaning rooms; she knows the history between Diluc and Kaeya. Elzer served the winery under Crepus, the man he says was like a father to him, and took on most of the winery's affairs after Crepus died and Diluc left Mondstadt; he is also Executive Chairman of the Mondstadt Wine Guild. Hillie and Moco are maids who trade gossip: in one exchange they share a rumour of a hidden room at the far end of the second-floor corridor, which one of them says she noticed while waxing floors.

Elzer is among the few who know that Diluc is the rumoured "Darknight Hero".

Atmosphere: A grand, quiet house surrounded by vineyards, with an owl statue at its door. The inscription on the statue is a prayer to the "watcher of the night" not to forget the splendour of the dawn and not to sway from the path of righteousness. Inside is a strange vase that looks completely out of place.

Books kept in and around the manor include volumes of A Drunkard's Tale, Ballads of the Squire, Biography of Gunnhildr, Heart of Clear Springs, The Fox in the Dandelion Sea and Vera's Melancholy.

History: In the manga, the vase was a gift from Kaeya, which he used to discreetly return Diluc's Vision after Diluc came back to Mondstadt. In the quest "A Child's Secret", Kaeya asks Diluc what happened to the vase and Diluc claims not to remember; Reckless Pallad says he saw one in Diluc's home.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the manor remains the winery's home and offices; no change in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content is recorded on the wiki.

30.comment: Dawn Winery Manor: Owl Statue Inscription
30.content: An owl statue at the manor carries two lines: one calling on the watcher of the night to remember the splendour of the dawn, and one urging those who struggle with evildoers not to stray from righteousness.

31.content:
Decarabian's Mondstadt (also: Old Mondstadt, Decarabian's City): Decarabian's Mondstadt, usually called Old Mondstadt, was the original home of Mondstadt's people: a walled capital built in a deep valley by the God of Storms, Decarabian, who ruled from a great tower. His people rebelled and killed him about 2,600 years ago, after which the new Anemo Archon Barbatos led them to Cider Lake. The valley is now the ruin-filled area called Stormterror's Lair.

Texts describe the city as a "dream of prosperity" created wholly by Decarabian's divine might. To his people it was a prison of wind.

Geography: The capital lay in an extremely deep valley that may be partly artificial, in the area now called Stormterror's Lair in the Brightcrown Mountains. Tall bridges are a signature of the city and its surroundings.

Ruins in Decarabian's style show that his realm spread across the Brightcrown Mountains and Windwail Highland, with ruin clusters in Brightcrown Canyon (leading into the city) and around Cecilia Garden, and as far south as the waypoint between Liyue and Dawn Winery. Architecture inside the lair suggests the city once opened to the northeast and northwest; a mountain now blocks the northeast gateway and the northwest waterway is dammed. How far north or west the realm reached is not known. The Wolvendom part of Windwail Highland has none of these ruins.

Places: Decarabian's Tower stood at the middle of the capital and was his seat. The residential quarter is still clearly marked out in the ruins.

Culture: Decarabian micromanaged the capital, even deciding where each resident lived, and banned certain tunes and chords because they might signal dissent. His ruins show a distinct style: plant-like margent ornaments and a curled-ended cross (a cercelée) instead of the Celtic knots and triquetra found on other Teyvat ruins. The stonework has survived 2,600 years in good condition.

Decarabian honestly believed his rule was loving and that his subjects bowed in adoration. His people bowed because the harsh winds forced them to, and the rebels used the windblume flower as a secret sign of solidarity.

History: During the Archon War the land was a frozen waste under Boreas, the wolf-god of the north, and Decarabian raised an impenetrable storm wall around his capital to shut out the cold. His subjects came to see themselves as locked in. About 2,600 years ago they rose in rebellion and slew him; the wall fell, and for the first time they saw the sky beyond it. A wind spirit among the rebels ascended as Barbatos, cleared the snow, and led the survivors to found the new city on Cider Lake, leaving the old capital empty.

The rebels, led by the Nameless Bard, the wind spirit, Decarabian's former lover Amos, the knight Gunnhildr and a wandering red-haired warrior, won at a cost: Amos and the Nameless Bard died. Decarabian's death blew apart part of his tower. The Gunnhildr Clan had left the city some years earlier, found shelter through a weak wind spirit's help, and rejoined the revolt. Mondstadt's later histories call this era the Age of Kings, naming Boreas and Decarabian the Kings of Ice and Frost.

Atmosphere: Silent, wind-scoured stone in a deep valley: tall arched bridges, broken pillars, plant-patterned carvings and strong air currents. It feels like a once-controlled city left to the weather.

Dangers: Hilichurls, slimes, Fatui, an Eye of the Storm and Ruin Guards roam the lair, and its wind currents and heights are hazardous.

Status as of 7.1: Abandoned ruins as of 7.1.

The storm barrier fell with Decarabian, and during the Prologue the ruins were sealed by a storm barrier of Dvalin's lair until Venti dispelled it, after which Dvalin was freed from the Abyss Order's hold. The area is open to travellers.

32.comment: Decarabian's Mondstadt: Decarabian's Wind Wall and Rebellion
32.content: Decarabian walled his city in gales that even Boreas could not scratch, because blizzards covered the land. The wall barred exit and entry, and his people felt imprisoned despite the warmth inside. The rebellion's symbol was the windblume. When Decarabian fell the wall dispelled and revealed clear blue sky.

33.content: Ruins in Decarabian's style are recognisable by margent plant motifs and the curled-ended cross, and they lack the triquetra. They appear in Brightcrown Canyon, around Cecilia Garden, and at the southern waypoint of Windwail Highland. A Field Tiller sitting in the tower once fired on visitors, a year-long episode remembered as the "Tyrant's Final Fury".

34.content:
Decarabian's Tower (also: Tower of Decarabian): Decarabian's Tower is the great ruined tower at the middle of Old Mondstadt, from which the God of Storms Decarabian ruled and watched over his people. His death blew away part of it. Centuries later the wounded dragon Dvalin laired in the ruin, and the Traveler climbs it in the Prologue.

The tower is also the place where a prototype Ruin Guard, the first Field Tiller, still stands inactive.

Geography: The tower stands in a very deep valley and reaches far down below the aboveground floors. The bottommost reachable floor is blocked off by an out-of-bounds barrier. The top resembles an observatory. Wind currents lift visitors from floor to floor.

The second-highest floor holds the inactive Field Tiller; the top floor has a Light Actuator and the entrance to the Confront Stormterror domain, whose text implies this was Decarabian's own residence. Climbing a broken pillar from the roof reaches the tower's very top.

History: Decarabian took the tower and built his capital around it after a wicked dragon had been cast down on that spot. From its heights he looked down on subjects who, in his mind, adored him. About 2,600 years ago the rebels killed him, and the blast of his death destroyed part of the tower. His storm barrier dropped with him and his people left for Cider Lake.

A prototype Field Tiller built in Khaenri'ah, damaged in a fight with Boreas' spirit, took shelter in the tower and fired on any approach for roughly a year, a period called the "Tyrant's Final Fury" until its power ran out. Five hundred years ago the dragon Dvalin, wounded and poisoned by Durin, used the tower as his lair.

Dangers: Gales, vertical drops and the tower's guards. The Confront Stormterror domain at the top is a boss encounter; the Prologue confrontation with Dvalin took place around it, freeing him from the Abyss Order's control.

Atmosphere: A hollow spire in a windswept valley: broken arches, drifting air currents and a sense of old authority gone silent.

Status as of 7.1: A ruin, open to climb as of 7.1.

35.content: The Field Tiller on the tower's upper deck is the first Ruin Guard ever made, a prototype far stronger than later units, built by Khaenri'ah. It is inactive in the present.

key: Pavilion of Scorching Sands and Blazing Sun
36.content:
Desert Pavilion (also: Pavilion of Scorching Sands and Blazing Sun, Desert Pavilion: Mirage): The Desert Pavilion is the Temple of Space's exhibition area for sculpture and architecture, built in the style of the desert temples of Sumeru. Its loading-screen text says that though every grand tower in the world will crumble into sand, towers built upon sand remain here forever. It was reconstructed from memory by the temple's Uplifted residents. Under the Watcher Melanta's rule its people were punished by being turned into sand statues, until the Traveler freed them in 6.5.

Death does not exist in the Temple of Space, so the sand statues are alive and can be restored. A mirror version of the area exists on the map as "Desert Pavilion: Mirage", an upside-down copy.

Geography: A multi-level complex of Sumeru-style architecture with pillars, torches, rock walls and elevators between levels, set around a central area. Parts of it are built on quicksand: with Dex's help the player can raise and remove sand structures to build cover or reach new places. The area is opened by the quest Unofficial Chronicle of the Desert Pavilion.

Sumeru-style features here include Dendrograna, Primal Beams, Primal Embers and Torches, Tri-Yana Seeds and Valaya. Enemies include Suppression and Patrol Type Segment-Domain Keepers, Domain Keepers, and a local legend, the Punisher of Gomorrah.

People: Venipi, who comes from the time of King Deshret's divine form, once worked on the king's mausoleum; he was plucked from the desert and spent less than a hundred years in the Apathic Interval. Vitruvius designed the main layout and pathways and was the first the party saw turned to sand. Kshama is another resident freed from sand, from the Dendro Archon's age. Makani Khagan, Mardava and Nagahvaya are also listed there.

Venipi supplied the patternwork and motifs from King Deshret's time; he keeps a coin the king gave him as a lucky charm and a reminder of his old life, and refused to hand it to Paimon as a reward. Vitruvius, in his own account, had spent millennia working out an epitaph, asking that his love in Patraipolis be told something. Residents say that everyone in the temple is friends, regardless of status in their former lives.

History: After Asmoday vanished, the other Shades let minor changes into the temple. Venipi says the deity's sisters asked him to rebuild desert buildings from memory, and with everyone's help the Pavilion was made. Later Melanta, mad with longing for Asmoday, sought to restore the temple to its original order and punished the Pavilion's people by turning them to sand, exiling the resident "Maukie" for defiling the laws of space.

In 6.5 the Traveler, Paimon, Zeitlind and Dex explored the Pavilion in Unofficial Chronicle of the Desert Pavilion, fighting Suppression Type Keepers, rescuing Venipi, Vitruvius and Kshama, and defeating the Punisher of Gomorrah (Afar's Avian), a boss that had hidden its form. Defeating it collapsed the upside-down mirage of the Pavilion and brought the real one, and all its inhabitants, back to life. Afterwards Zeitlind found an amethyst brooch of her sister's displayed there, one of the items lost from her suitcase.

Dangers: Suppression Type Keepers, which can turn people into sand, Patrol Type Keepers, Domain Keepers and the Punisher of Gomorrah; quicksand that must be handled with Dex's help.

Atmosphere: Sun-bleached stone and heat, with eerie lifelike sand figures frozen in flight from an unseen disaster, together with the friendly bickering of the people who built it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 6.5 (unchanged through 7.1) the sand curse is lifted and the residents are restored.

No later release through 7.1 was found to revisit the Pavilion. Its inhabitants remain in the Temple of Space, but 'Maukie', exiled by Melanta, was not among those restored here.

37.comment: Desert Pavilion: The Punisher of Gomorrah
37.content: The only known way to stop people being turned to sand was to defeat the Punisher of Gomorrah, which had hidden its form. The Traveler found and defeated it, in two waves of Domain Keepers and then the Punisher itself. After that the Pavilion's sand statues could be restored.

38.content: Venipi (of King Deshret's era) and Vitruvius (the Pavilion's layout designer) are friends and tease each other. Vitruvius turned to sand mid-sentence while stating his planned epitaph. Kshama, from the Dendro Archon's age, was rescued from three Suppression Keepers.

39.content:
Devil's Cut (also: Devils Cut, The Devil's Cut): Devil's Cut is the tavern of Dornman Port, in Windrest Peak (opened in 6.5). Its owner is Groovy. The name pairs with Mondstadt City's Angel's Share, and the two taverns are counterparts. The port tavern serves sailors, merchants and locals.

Angel's Share takes its name from brewers' slang for liquor lost to evaporation; by the same real-world slang, the devil's cut is the portion a barrel absorbs. Angel's Share belongs to the Dawn Winery; no source ties Devil's Cut to the winery.

People: Groovy has blond hair in a ponytail, a mustache and beard, blue eyes and a brown and purple blazer. He greets visitors cheerfully, offers fruit juice to those who do not drink, and notes that the merchant Matthaus has just unloaded a batch of Snezhnayan Fire-Water, which tempts even him. He says "Hey, feeling down? Try a cup of this".

Odolf is a businessman who recently travelled to Snezhnaya and returned shortly before the Traveler meets him. He sits at the tavern after the world quest "Winds Beneath the Tower of Silence" and says Mondstadt's beer still tastes best. He found Snezhnaya freezing cold and envied the fluffy fae guides there. He once dreamed of joining the Knights but took over his father's stall at the Guild instead.

Quests: The world quest "Winds Beneath the Tower of Silence" begins when the Traveler approaches a group of locals gathered in front of the tavern, and leads to the old lighthouse. Its story: Odolf, disliking the grave-keeper Winslow, had planted a lure to attract elemental creatures to the lighthouse mechanism; while he was in Snezhnaya it drew an Eye of the Storm, which frightened Winslow into paranoia. Afterwards Odolf admits what he did, though not proudly: he thought it would blow over.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tavern is open and unchanged; nothing in 6.x-7.1 content after its debut alters it.

40.content: Groovy is the owner of Devil's Cut and an open-world NPC in Dornman Port. Canon gives no backstory, only his friendly patter, his fondness for strong spirits from Snezhnaya and his habit of offering juice to non-drinkers.

key: The Harbor Where a Thousand Winds Converge
41.content:
Dornman Port (also: The Harbor Where a Thousand Winds Converge): Dornman Port is the busy port town of northern Mondstadt, on Windrest Peak north of Cider Lake. Its loading screen calls it a bustling harbor and one of the continent's major trade hubs, welcoming merchant ships from many nations. In the aristocratic era it was the fief of the Gunnhildr Clan. Mondstadt knights are stationed here, and the port has no church.

It is known for cargo shipping and flower cultivation. Legally docking requires a valid entry permit. The area opened in game with Windrest Peak in version 6.5.

Geography: The port sits on the water in the far north of Mondstadt, where the weather is clearer and more varied than in the south. It has a western bridge, a bazaar, a central square, the Knights of Favonius base, and outskirts. The Old Sanatorium Site lies on a hill above, and the Knights of Favonius Ruins lie beneath the old lighthouse. Nearby is Millhaven.

Henry Morton says it is too far to charter a boat to the Nameless Island from here. Ruins just north of the port hold a time-trial challenge, and the Open-Eyed boss roams Windrest Peak.

Places: The Knights of Favonius base, an unofficial name, is the Ranged Company's centre in Windrest Peak, with members of the Logistics, Combined Arms, Support and Investigation companies. The Devil's Cut tavern, owned by Groovy, mirrors the capital's Angel's Share in name. Fragrant Whispers is a flower shop run by Alodia. The bazaar, a "Taste of the North" venue and a windmill are also noted.

The Knights of Favonius Ruins are catacombs beneath the city where the knights who defended the port during the Cataclysm lie. The Old Sanatorium Site is a demolished sanatorium built on the ruins left when the Temple of Space was lifted into the sky.

People: Lohen, Vice Captain of the Ranged Company, has been stationed here and teases locals and troublemakers alike. Knights at the base include the gunsmiths Herstal and Koch and snipers Gunther and Ursula. Hannelore and Philomena (a nun) are also local. Groovy runs the Devil's Cut, Alodia the flower shop, and Insigne, Lietzberg and Patricia work in the bazaar.

Beidou's crew (The Crux) has docked here. Frederica Gunnhildr was sent back by Grand Master Varka to help defend it. Mona was born here, to parents who had moved in from elsewhere, and found Barbeloth before settling in the capital.

Governance: Local order is kept by the Knights of Favonius from the base. In aristocratic times the Gunnhildr Clan held the fief; after Vennessa's rebellion they led the push to abolish hereditary fiefs and likely handed theirs to the people.

The Reconnaissance Company under Eula patrols the long trade road between the port and Mondstadt City, especially during Weinlesefest.

History: In the age of Great Arcadia the area belonged to the city-state Elysium under the Gunnhildr Clan, who after its fall took refuge in Decarabian's city. After Barbatos scattered the snow they returned north. The port is said to be named after the Thorn King, a possible clan ancestor. They founded Mondstadt's first sanctuary to Barbatos here.

In the tyrannical age the Gunnhildrs broke with the Imunlaukr Clan by seizing the bishop sent from the capital, throwing him from the sanctuary's high tower and tearing it down, so the port has had no church since. The Gunnhildrs sided with the people in Vennessa's rebellion and were spared exile. In the Cataclysm 500 years ago the port nearly fell and many knights died defending it.

Quests: The Windrest Peak story quests, including Winds Beneath the Tower of Silence, take place around the port and the Knights' ruins. In Alchemical Ascension (limited-time event) Eula and Beidou traveled from the port to the alchemy showcase after a smuggling crackdown.

Dangers: Smuggling is a recurring problem. Eula's company once tracked a dangerous Abyss Order cargo here that was bound for Liyue Harbor; Yanfei, a consultant on the merchant vessel, was imperilled until Eula rescued her.

Travel: The port is a hub for sea travel. A route to Port Ormos in Sumeru has opened and a local trading company plans to export fruit, though one reply doubts the fruit would survive the trip.

Atmosphere: Salt air and flower scent, sailors, merchants and bards in the square, knights keeping a watchful eye, and a lively, cosmopolitan mood quite unlike the capital's slow pace. Lohen jokes that even the Treasure Hoarders avoid the place since he arrived.

Status as of 7.1: A thriving trade port with a Knights of Favonius base as of 7.1.

Varka ordered several returning knights to the port to help defend it (in-game mail, 2025). No Dornman Port content from 7.0-7.1 was found.

42.content: Three loading-screen accounts compete: a madman in a crown of thorns from Windrest Peak preaching apocalypse; a Thorn King god whose people called themselves Dornman before Barbatos defeated him; or a Gunnhildr ancestor named the Thorn King. Researchers reject the first. Keep it unresolved.

key: Winds Beneath the Tower of Silence
43.comment: Dornman Port: The Port in the Cataclysm
43.content: Five hundred years ago the port stood on the brink of destruction as a front against the monsters of the Abyss, and the fallen knights' graves lie beneath the city in the Knights of Favonius Ruins.

44.content:
Dragonspine (also: Vindagnyr): Dragonspine is a huge snow-covered mountain in Mondstadt, one of the most dangerous places in the nation: its snow never melts and its cold kills the unprepared. It was once called Vindagnyr, a green mountain where the ancient kingdom of Sal Vindagnyr flourished until a Celestial Nail, the Skyfrost Nail, fell on it and buried it in endless winter. About five hundred years ago the Abyssal dragon Durin fell dead here after his battle with Dvalin, giving the mountain its present name. The alchemist Albedo keeps a research camp on its slopes.

Durin's poisonous blood seeped into the mountain's ley lines, producing the warm, toxic red crystals called Scarlet Quartz and reviving the shattered sacred tree of Sal Vindagnyr as the Frostbearing Tree. Few adventurers attempt the mountain; those who do rest at a camp at its foot.

Geography: A single vast massif beyond Windwail Highland, near the border with Liyue, whose sharp summit (its design modelled on the Matterhorn) can be seen from much of northern Liyue. Its subareas are the Snow-Covered Path (the lower approach and the Frostbearing Tree), Entombed City - Outskirts and Entombed City - Ancient Palace (the buried ruins of Sal Vindagnyr), Starglow Cavern (a great cave at the mountain's heart), Wyrmrest Valley (Durin's bones and heart) and the Skyfrost Nail at the summit. A river and small islands lie on its northern side.

The whole mountain lies under a "Subzero Climate": cold builds up steadily, faster in snowstorms, in certain parts of the mountain and in icy water, and only fires, torches and other heat sources, or Scarlet Quartz, hold it off. Blocks of patterned "Ancient Rime" that ordinary fire cannot melt choke many paths; only Scarlet Quartz breaks them. Blue plants that glow in the dark (called Starglow) grow around the Rime and through Starglow Cavern, a peculiarity the Celestial Nail's power is believed to cause. In Wyrmrest Valley Durin's life force has dyed the snow red.

Places: - Dragonspine Adventurer Camp: a rest stop on the outskirts, on the path from Dadaupa Gorge, built by the cook Harris; the weaponsmith Orban, the researcher Stevens and the adventurer Iris work there.
- Albedo's Campsite: a small cave laboratory between the Ancient Palace and the Outskirts, with torches, a cooking pot, worktables, shelves of research material and an alchemy bench.
- Frostbearing Tree: the revived sacred tree of Sal Vindagnyr, crimson-marked instead of blue.
- Wyrmrest Valley: Durin's skull, ribcage and still-warm heart.
- Entombed City: the buried palace and outskirts of Sal Vindagnyr, including the Mural Room where Imunlaukr left his greatsword.
- Skyfrost Nail and the Peak of Vindagnyr: the summit, where the restored Nail hovers above the old ritual site.

People: No one lives on Dragonspine permanently. Albedo, the Knights of Favonius' Chief Alchemist, works there for long stretches, often joined by his assistant Sucrose or the alchemist Timaeus. The adventurer camp hosts adventurers and researchers, and the Knights post a guard who keeps inexperienced climbers from heading for the summit. Researchers such as the environmentalist Esther survey the slopes, and Fatui squads lurk in Wyrmrest Valley.

History: Several thousand years ago refugees fleeing "a land of snow and strife" found a lush green mountain, raised a monument on it and founded Sal Vindagnyr, which prospered under heavenly blessing around a great white tree. Then the Skyfrost Nail fell from the heavens onto the summit's ritual site; snowstorms buried the kingdom, the Nail split into three, a fragment shattered the sacred tree, and the people died. Five hundred years ago, during the cataclysm, Barbatos and Dvalin lured the rampaging dragon Durin over the mountain and Dvalin killed him; Durin's body fell into what is now Wyrmrest Valley, and the mountain became Dragonspine.

About a thousand years ago, at the end of the aristocratic era, Mondstadt's nobles sent an expedition to uncover the mountain's secrets; it was destroyed from within by Eberhart and none of its members came home. In the Traveler's time no one had reached the summit until the Traveler freed the three Nail shards from their ice (In the Mountains, 1.2) and the restored Nail rose above the peak. Albedo's dealings with Durin's legacy run through the mountain's later story: the cursed sword Festering Desire (1.2 event), his failed predecessor Subject Two (2.3 event) and the draining of Durin's heart in Paralogism (5.6).

Atmosphere: Silence, wind and deep snow; breath fogging, ice cracking underfoot and the constant worry of the cold. Broken ancient stonework juts out of drifts, giant bones curve above a scarlet valley, and blue Starglow light fills the caves. A crackling campfire is the most welcome sight on the mountain.

Dangers: The cold itself is the chief killer; snowstorms, falling icicles, rockfalls and icy water make it worse. Cryo slimes, Cryo hilichurl tribes and their Lawachurl chieftains, Abyss Mages, dormant Ruin Guards and Ruin Graders, a Cryo Hypostasis and the boar known as The Great Snowboar King roam the slopes, and Fatui agents come for Durin's relics. Durin's blood is highly toxic to ordinary people.

Travel: The usual approach is from Windwail Highland through Dadaupa Gorge to the Adventurer Camp at the foot of the mountain. Climbers should bring hot food and the means to light fires; Pyro users, campfires, torches and Scarlet Quartz are what make the ascent survivable. The summit path was sealed by Ancient Rime until the Skyfrost Nail's shards were freed.

Quests: - Princeps Cretaceus Chapter (Albedo, 1.2): Albedo's experiments on the Traveler at his Dragonspine camp.
- In the Mountains (1.2): Iris asks the Traveler to investigate the strange ice; the Nail's shards are freed and the summit opens.
- The Festering Fang (1.2): the smith Orban forges a spear from Durin's tooth while the Fatui eye Durin's heart.
- A Land Entombed (1.2): the journals of the lost aristocratic expedition.
- Lost in the Snow and the Snowy Silhouette quests (1.2 onward): the search for Joel's father.
- Hidden objectives: Ancient Carvings, the three boxes of Sal Vindagnyr, the Ragged Records and the Ruin Guards' coded records.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Dragonspine is still frozen and hazardous. Durin's heart has been inert since Albedo drained it during Paralogism, and Durin's name now belongs to the gentle young man created in his place. After the 7.1 Archon Quest the Skyfrost Nail began showing a strange change, and Albedo is watching it from the summit.

The drained heart can no longer empower dragon teeth, though it still gives off warmth; the Adventurer Camp has an alchemy bench that does the job instead. The change in the Nail began when Ronova destroyed the Celestial Nail at Hyperborea with Eitr, after which every other Nail showed a strange sign in the sky. Albedo, who thought the Nail's purpose had ended with Sal Vindagnyr's destruction, now doubts that and is studying how the change affects the mountain's ecosystem.

45.content:
Sal Vindagnyr was the kingdom on Vindagnyr in the era of the unified civilization. Its chief priest Varuch's daughter, the princess, was born beneath the sacred white tree and could foresee the future, painting what she saw as frescoes; she once dreamed of a black dragon filling the land with scarlet poison. After the Skyfrost Nail fell, she gave the Starsilver greatsword to Imunlaukr, an outlander hero, who left to seek a way to break the ice. Varuch climbed the summit to seek guidance and did not return; the princess tried to graft a branch of the shattered tree on a small island and died in the snow; the scribe Ukko buried her, cursed the heavens and the absent Imunlaukr, and wrote the last carvings.

Ukko's last words wished that a "new nation without gods" (Khaenri'ah, then in its infancy) might have the strength to stand against the world. Imunlaukr returned to find everyone dead, left the greatsword among the frescoes and went to seek war; his descendants became the Imunlaukr Clan of Mondstadt.

46.content: The Skyfrost Nail is the Celestial Nail cast down by the heavens onto Vindagnyr's summit ritual site, turning a green mountain into an eternal winter; the damage to the ley lines is implied to be the cause of the abnormal cold. Carvings record that the Nail split in three; its shards froze a spot deep in Starglow Cavern, an underground chamber near the Outskirts and the sacred tree. During In the Mountains the Traveler thawed the shards with Scarlet Quartz, they rejoined the main body, and the restored Nail rose to hover above the Peak of Vindagnyr.

47.content: The Frostbearing Tree is the sacred white tree of Sal Vindagnyr, a withered Irminsul-type tree shattered and frozen when the Skyfrost Nail fell. Durin's blood seeping into the ley lines brought it back to a hungry half-life, marking it red rather than blue. Once freed from its Ancient Rime, it absorbs Crimson Agate (crystals of Durin's life force fused with the mountain's energy) and grows, finally bearing a single crimson, icy "fruit", the catalyst Frostbearer, in memory of the kingdom's dead, meant for one who will bring justice to a poisoned world.

48.comment: Dragonspine: Wyrmrest Valley and Durin's Heart
48.content:
Wyrmrest Valley holds the black dragon Durin's skull, ribcage and heart. Created by the alchemist Rhinedottir in Khaenri'ah, Durin rampaged through Mondstadt during the cataclysm until Dvalin pierced his neck over the mountain. His heart went on beating, dyeing the snow red, and its life force could empower dragon teeth; Fatui squads camped nearby to exploit it, and the smith Orban used it to forge the Dragonspine Spear. Scarlet Quartz is a gemstone formed from his decaying remains.

In Paralogism (5.6) Albedo, fearing that the slowly reviving heart would bring disaster, drew its vital energy with reagents won from the Hexenzirkel and used it to turn Mini Durin, the kindly dragon from the storybook world Simulanka, into a human who took the old Durin's place. The heart is now a silent stone that still radiates warmth.

49.content: About a thousand years ago, late in the aristocratic era, Mondstadt's nobles sent a team of young aristocrats to investigate Dragonspine. Eberhart, an illegitimate son of Landrich who secretly plotted against the aristocracy, laid traps that whittled the team down, then attacked his half-brother Ingbert and Luther himself; Ingbert died, Luther was mortally wounded, and Eberhart escaped by boat, gravely hurt, expecting his ally Priscilla to light a warning beacon at Stormbearer Point if the plot were discovered. The aristocracy did uncover it. Stevens at the Adventurer Camp pieces this together from the team's journals; Eberhart's ultimate fate is unrecorded.

50.comment: Dragonspine: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon
50.content: During this 1.2 limited-time event, Sucrose asked the Traveler to uncover Albedo's "secret": Festering Desire, a sword recovered from Treasure Hoarders whose vanished smith had coated its blade with powder made from Durin's remains, cursing it. Albedo had the Traveler, who can purify Abyssal corruption, test it in battle on Dragonspine. Fatui agents came after the sword, and some of its power accidentally revived a dead Cryo Regisvine, which had to be defeated. The sword's own text is a fond memory of Durin thanking his mother for his wings and wishing to tell a land of lovely songs about her.

51.comment: Dragonspine: Shadows Amidst Snowstorms and Subject Two
51.content: During this 2.3 limited-time event, while Albedo, Eula, Amber, Bennett and the Traveler were on Dragonspine, the story revealed Subject Two, Rhinedottir's failed first attempt at a synthetic human, abandoned inside Durin. Escaping the corpse, he haunted the mountain, envied Albedo's life among people and planned to replace him, using Durin's blood to create a Fellflower that mimicked Albedo as a decoy. Albedo went to confront him and afterwards said only that the impostor's plan had failed; the others never learned the full truth at the time. Paralogism (5.6) revealed that Albedo had killed and buried him, that creatures of Durin's blood carried his remains back into the dragon, and that he had returned as the core of the network of impostor creatures.

52.comment: Dragonspine: The Nail Anomaly at Dragonspine
52.content: After the 7.1 Archon Quest, in which Ronova destroyed Hyperborea's Celestial Nail with Eitr, the Celestial Nails across Teyvat began emitting a strange sign into the sky, and the Skyfrost Nail changed in the same way. Albedo, who had never seen anything like it on Dragonspine, stayed at the summit to study it and its effect on the surrounding ecosystem. What it portends is unknown as of 7.1.

53.content:
Dragonspine Adventurer Camp: A small adventurers' camp on the outskirts of Dragonspine, on the path from Dadaupa Gorge up toward the snowbound mountain. The chef Harris built it so adventurers would have somewhere to rest and a hot bowl of soup after a hard day in the cold.

Besides Harris's cooking, the camp has a weaponsmith, Orban, and several other residents. It is the practical last stop before the mountain, not a settlement with any government of its own.

People: Harris is the chef and founder; he sells hot dishes daily and says he came to help local adventurers. He credits a young Liyue chef he met while travelling (the wiki identifies her as Xiangling) with teaching him that cooking should bring people joy and satisfaction. Orban is the weaponsmith. Other named residents are the adventurer Iris, Joel, Joserf, and the researcher Stevens.

None of the residents has a detailed canon biography; they are open-world NPCs with short dialogue, so keep their personalities light. Harris is warm and hearty: he greets frozen visitors with an offer of hot food and consoles a losing card-game opponent with soup.

Places: A cooking stall run by Harris and a forge run by Orban. The Alchemist's Crafting Bench sits beside Orban.

The bench is tied to the Dragonteeth gathered on Dragonspine: Orban found the material could not be worked with ordinary tools, and after consulting Albedo (through Sucrose) the camp received a Runestone that holds great vitality, in Orban's account a relic left to the Knights of Favonius by a wandering troupe that helped Mondstadt against its old nobility about a thousand years ago. The method as told is to charge one Dragontooth from the Runestone and use it to treat others so they can be forged. This becomes available only after the quests Paralogism (5.6) and The Festering Fang.

Travel: The camp lies at the foot of Dragonspine, reached from Dadaupa Gorge in Windwail Highland. Beyond it the road climbs into the permanent snow, where warmth and supplies matter.

Atmosphere: Cold air, a cooking fire and the smell of soup against the white of the mountain; adventurers in thick coats stamping snow from their boots. Practical and friendly rather than grand.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the camp is open and running. Nothing in canon through 7.1 reports it damaged or closed.

54.comment: Dragonspine Adventurer Camp: Harris and the Dragonteeth Bench
54.content: Harris cooks for adventurers; Orban forges. After Paralogism and The Festering Fang, Orban explains that Dragonteeth resist ordinary tools and must be treated using vitality drawn from a Runestone, a relic Albedo had Sucrose send; the Alchemist's Crafting Bench beside him performs the transfer, turning raw Dragonteeth into Empowered ones.

55.content:
Drunkard Gorge: Drunkard Gorge is a stretch of road in Windwail Highland that separates Dawn Winery from Wolvendom. It used to be a popular place for travelling merchants, but it now has a reputation for danger and most people have left.

It is a minor roadside location, known mostly through two open-world NPCs who frequent it.

People: Farrah, a fruit vendor, is found in front of the gorge between Springvale and Dawn Winery. He says he used to set up his stall in the canyon, that monsters had recently driven the vendors off, and that a merchant caravan was stuck with no way through; his chief worry is his fruit rotting. Greg wanders the gorge at night. He claims to work at Dawn Winery and to have been given a bottle by Diluc, but he bears a Ravenwing insignia on his bandana and tries to rob drunks, which makes him a Treasure Hoarder in all but admission.

Greg's pitch is to invite a visitor to share a bottle and walk them toward the winery, offering to hold up anyone who seems tipsy while eyeing their coin pouch; when caught he drops the friendliness and tells a sober person to go away. Farrah is a worried, polite family man who offers a few apples as thanks for sympathy.

Dangers: Monsters the vendors cannot manage, and opportunistic thieves like Greg after dark. Occasional monsters were once shrugged off as bad luck; now the route is avoided.

Travel: Lies on the road between Dawn Winery and Wolvendom. It had been used by merchant caravans.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no canon change to the gorge is reported. The merchants' flight and the stalled caravan are the last stated situation.

56.comment: Drunkard Gorge: Greg and Farrah of Drunkard Gorge
56.content: Greg is a night wanderer in the gorge posing as a Dawn Winery employee while robbing drunks; Farrah is a daytime fruit vendor who was chased off by monsters.

57.content:
Durin's Core (also: Durin's heart, heart of Durin): Durin's Core is the still-beating heart of Durin, the Abyssal dragon killed above Dragonspine, found in Wyrmrest Valley. Its ominous vitality could turn Strange Teeth into Empowered Dragonteeth, and it gives off warmth.

During the Interlude Chapter quest "The Gardener" (version 5.6), Albedo drains the blood from the heart, and it goes inert. It no longer makes Empowered Dragonteeth but still warms the surroundings.

History: Durin was slain over Dragonspine by Dvalin about 500 years before the present, and his blood seeped into the mountain's ley lines. The heart in Wyrmrest Valley is what remains of him there. Its unusual energy is why the Mondstadt adventurers could use it to make Empowered Dragonteeth.
