The same blood is what revived the Frostbearing Tree, which is described as carrying the Abyss's malevolent energy in the newborn tree. The wiki's page for the core links this location to that wider story but canon does not spell out the mechanism.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: before the Festering Fang quest the core only shows flavour text. Afterwards, offering four Strange Teeth gives four Empowered Dragonteeth. After The Gardener, interacting with it shows that it has lost its power, and Dragonteeth are obtained at the Alchemist's Crafting Bench near Orban at the Dragonspine Adventurer Camp instead.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the heart is inert, still warm, and no longer a source of vitality. The quest text frames the change as a solemn quiet after power left it.

Atmosphere: A cave-bound hulking mass that looks like a heart: once warmly glowing and unsettling, now silent and still. Suits tense or melancholy scenes.

58.content: Durin's Core is the Abyssal dragon Durin's still-beating heart in Wyrmrest Valley. It transformed Strange Teeth into Empowered Dragontooth until Albedo drained its blood in The Gardener, after which it became inert but remained warm.

59.content:
Entombed City - Ancient Palace (also: Entombed City Ancient Palace): The Entombed City - Ancient Palace is the frozen palace district of Sal Vindagnyr, an ancient kingdom on the mountain now called Dragonspine. The official description calls it an ancient city that lies silent beneath the eternal ice. Cryo hilichurls prowl its ruins.

The kingdom was founded by refugees and ruined when the Skyfrost Nail fell, turning a green mountain into a snowfield. Its last inhabitants left painted frescoes and word-boxes that tell what happened.

Geography: On Dragonspine, with a Statue of The Seven, Warming Seelie, Scarlet Quartz and Ancient Rime to clear. A tower on the leftmost bend of the route above the palace holds the Priest's Box. A sealed cave door near the palace leads to the Mural Room.

Scarlet Quartz and Warming Seelie help against the cold. The Mural Room door opens after the Hidden Exploration Objective Dragonspine's Glacial Secret is completed. A chest near the palace's cave door holds the first of three investigation journals used in the world quest A Land Entombed.

History: Refugees from a land of snow and strife found a lush green mountain, raised a monument on its peak and founded Sal Vindagnyr, building their capital and palace there. They prospered for a time under Celestia's blessings. Then the Skyfrost Nail fell from the sky, clouds and snowstorms swallowed the city, and the kingdom died.

The chief priest Varuch's daughter, gifted with foresight, painted her visions as frescoes, including a black dragon spreading scarlet poison over the land. Varuch climbed the mountain seeking guidance and wanted a third fresco of thawing ice, which she could not paint. The kingdom's great white tree withered; the princess died and the scribe Ukko buried her. The outlander Imunlaukr, who had left to seek a cure, came back to find everyone dead. Five hundred years ago the princess's dream came true when the dragon Durin fell on the mountain.

Dangers: Deadly cold unless warmed by Scarlet Quartz or Seelie, plus Ice Shield hilichurl guards, Cryo hilichurl grenadiers and shooters, Cryo samachurls and the Great Snowboar King.

Atmosphere: Buried ruins under permanent snow, a hush broken by wind and the crack of ice, carvings half eroded, and a sense of a people frozen mid-sentence.

Status as of 7.1: Still buried in ice as of 7.1; no later change is recorded.

60.comment: Entombed City - Ancient Palace: Sal Vindagnyr
60.content: Sal Vindagnyr was a kingdom on the green mountain Vindagnyr, now Dragonspine, in the unified-civilisation era. The Skyfrost Nail split into three and its fragments froze the land; its great white tree was shattered. Its entire population died. The Imunlaukr Clan descended from the outlander Imunlaukr, who left the kingdom for wars.

61.content:
Entombed City - Outskirts (also: Entombed City Outskirts): The Entombed City - Outskirts is the outer edge of Sal Vindagnyr's buried city on Dragonspine. The official description says the city has been entombed by snow so deeply that it is nearly indistinguishable from its former self. Cryo hilichurls and the Cryo Hypostasis make it dangerous.

A stone monument here is tied to the kingdom's last scribe,.

Geography: The subarea sits on Dragonspine's slopes with a Teleport Waypoint, a Cryo elemental monument, pressure plates, ruin braziers, Scarlet Quartz, Ancient Rime and Warming Seelie to manage the cold. A weathered stone monument lies to the west of the waypoint.

The Cryo Hypostasis's arena lies in the outskirts; a cavern below it holds one of the Ancient Carvings and is reached by an entrance near the waypoint that opens during the quest In the Mountains. The wiki also places one of the three ice-bound spheres from the split Skyfrost Nail in an underground chamber near the outskirts.

History: The outskirts belonged to Sal Vindagnyr. After the Skyfrost Nail split, its pieces released orbs that froze the places where they stopped: one deep in Starglow Cavern, one in a chamber near the city's outskirts, and one shattered the kingdom's white tree.

The scribe Ukko, last keeper of the kingdom, tried to heal the withered ley lines, buried the princess, and left a bitter last message: a wish that the world burn, and hope that a "new nation without gods" might stand against it. Offering Cecilia at the weathered monument to the west of the waypoint reveals the scribe's box containing this message.

Dangers: Ice Shield hilichurl guards, Cryo hilichurl grenadiers and shooters, Cryo samachurls, Ice Shieldwall Mitachurls, Frostarm Lawachurls and the Cryo Hypostasis, plus the cold itself.

Atmosphere: Snowdrifts over broken walls, a few blue-glowing plants, and an enormous silence in which a half-buried city seems to wait.

Status as of 7.1: Frozen ruins, unchanged as of 7.1.

62.comment: Entombed City - Outskirts: Stone monument near the outskirts waypoint
62.content: A stone monument west of the outskirts waypoint, its writing worn away by wind. Placing three Cecilia flowers there causes the Scribe's Box to appear. The box carries the scribe Ukko's last wishes for the world to end in flames and for a nation without gods to rise.

63.content:
Entrance to Stormterror's Lair: The Entrance to Stormterror's Lair is a set of ruins in Decarabian's architectural style in Brightcrown Canyon. It once led straight into the capital of Decarabian, the old God of Storms, and is now the way into the area known as Stormterror's Lair.

It is a point of interest, not a settlement. The old capital behind it was later abandoned and, after the dragon Dvalin took refuge there, became known by the name Mondstadt's people gave him.

Geography: The ruins lie in Brightcrown Canyon, within the Brightcrown Mountains of Mondstadt, at the approach to the old capital of Decarabian's Mondstadt. They are built in the Decarabian style and open directly into that city. The only road shown in-game leads out of the ruined city to a boar habitat to the south.

Whether further stretches of the road existed and were lost is not stated by canon.

History: According to the Teyvat Travel Guide, soldiers were once stationed along the road in Brightcrown Canyon that led into the capital. After Decarabian was killed in an uprising and Barbatos took his place, the people moved their capital to an island in Cider Lake, where Mondstadt stands today, leaving the old city empty.

Centuries later the Dragon of the East, Dvalin, wounded in his fight with the corrupted dragon Durin, fell into a long sleep in the ruined capital. Mondstadt had forgotten him by the time he woke, and called him Stormterror, which gave the area its present name.

Atmosphere: Weathered stone gateworks of an extinct storm-god's kingdom, silent apart from wind in the canyon, with the vast and half-forgotten city beyond.

Dangers: Ruin guards and hilichurls are among the enemies in the surrounding Stormterror's Lair area. The area is protected by a storm barrier until the quest Hurdle is completed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruins remain abandoned. No Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya content changes them.

64.content:
Falcon Coast: Falcon Coast is a long sandy coast in Galesong Hill, east of Mondstadt, stretching from Windrise to the sea. With Cape Oath, it shelters a bay on three sides. Citizens stroll its white sand and shallow water, and falcons can be seen above the waves.

The Temple of the Lion ruin sits on this coast. The Hexenzirkel's floating tea-party island is entered from the cliff overlooking the beach.

Geography: Official text describes the long coastline and shallow water as ideal for walking. An Elemental Monument (Pyro) stands here; dandelion seeds and small lamp grass grow.

Hilichurl Cryo Shooters, Wooden Shield Guards, Hydro Samachurls and slimes inhabit the beach.

Places: The Temple of the Lion is an abandoned temple to the Lion of the South, taken over by monsters. The Hexenzirkel's Island in the Sky is a floating meeting place for the coven's tea parties, with a long table for seven.

To enter the island, one stands at the cliff and speaks a rhyme about a squirrel, a pointy-eared cat and a pious puppy. Its access history is covered in the entry below.

People: Two children, Will and Jill, are here by day, hoping to reach Dr. Edith at Windrise; they are hiding from Mack, a Knight of Favonius who is watching over them wherever they go. The wiki notes Mack says the Knights are holding a training exercise nearby.

After Alice's failed launch experiment near Springvale, her Travel Guide says Jean arranged for her to be watched; she wandered Falcon Coast bored, while Amber, who was sent to monitor her, enjoyed playing with the local children.

History: By the Wolf-Fang story, in the early days of the Knights of Favonius the nameless Knight of Boreas hunted demons from the Dark Sea on this coast, and the carrion drew thousands of falcons that circled for days. That, not the legend of Vennessa the Falcon of the West, is said to be the true source of the name.

A one-time time tunnel from the Minacious Isle also led here during a limited event (see the entry below).

Atmosphere: Soft surf, bright sand and long, open sightlines; calm and unhurried.

Dangers: Light: hilichurls and slimes. A Knights' exercise may restrict access.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 unchanged.

65.comment: Falcon Coast: Hexenzirkel's Island in the Sky
65.content: A floating tea-party island above Falcon Coast, kept under Barbatos' care and entered by an incantation, with seven chairs around a long table and a lantern at its centre. It was accessible during Windblume's Breath (3.5) and permanently since Paralogism (5.6).

66.content:
Favonius Cathedral (also: Mondstadt Cathedral, Cathedral of Favonius): The Favonius Cathedral is the great Gothic-looking church at the top of Mondstadt City, standing behind the plaza with the giant statue of the Anemo Archon Barbatos. The Church of Favonius runs it as the centre of Barbatos worship: nuns pray and hear confessions there, Deaconess Barbara works there, and its guarded basement held the Holy Lyre der Himmel, which the Traveler tried to steal for Venti in the Prologue.

The Church is overseen by the Knights of Favonius, so knights guard the doors and stairs. The building's grandeur is a point of debate: the map description wonders whether a city taught freedom by its god needs to spend so much on so lavish a cathedral, and Dainsleif remarked on the same thing.

Geography: The Cathedral crowns the upper end of Mondstadt City. Long stairs climb from the Anemo Archon statue plaza to its doors; inside are rows of pews leading to the apse, and a staircase at the far end leads down to a guarded basement.

The statue in front shows Barbatos hooded and winged, hands cupped together, with the words "The Gateway of Celestia" carved on its pedestal in Teyvat script. The basement is a separate, stone-walled level with bookshelves, ladders and a back room where the Holy Lyre was kept.

Places: Nave and pews, where townsfolk and nuns pray; the confessional, where Sister Victoria listens to confessions all day; the front lawn and steps; the basement vault, normally closed to the public and watched by knights.

People: Clergy of the Church of Favonius: Deaconess Barbara (healer, singer and "idol" of Mondstadt), the nun Rosaria (who skips nearly every Church duty), Deacon Dahlia, and, since his return from Nod-Krai, Seneschal Seamus Pegg.

Regular faces include Sister Victoria (sharp-tongued, keen on "sinners"), Sister Grace (who leads prayers at the statue by day and is inside by night), and the nun Jilliana, a former Treasure Hoarder who prays while her husband Rudolf and young daughter Lily wait nearby. Knights of Favonius Otto and Aramis guard the entrance and the stairs. Albert, head of the Barbara fan club, loiters outside and is regularly shooed off by the sisters.

Cardinal Calvin ran the Church's affairs while Seamus was away and was so buried in work that the sisters barely saw him; Barbara last saw him when the Lyre was stolen. Other sisters on record include Gotelinde, who handles the Cathedral's paperwork. For a long time the Fatui diplomat's assistant Viktor idled inside the Cathedral, sneering at Barbatos while befriending little Lily; he left Mondstadt after Signora's death.

Governance: The Cathedral belongs to the Church of Favonius, which the Knights of Favonius manage. Its leader is the Seneschal (Seamus Pegg, the Cardinal of Daybreak); Cardinal Calvin served as acting head during the long expedition. Use of the Holy Lyre der Himmel is regulated: it is normally used only at Ludi Harpastum, and any other loan needs documents signed by the Grand Master, the Seneschal and the Community Representative.

Culture: Worship here is gentle and informal. The faithful say a prayer spoken on the breeze will reach Barbatos; the usual blessing is "may Barbatos' gentle wind be with you". Nuns hear confessions, offer guidance, run hymn and choir practice, care for the sick and tend children without parents; Barbara's healing and singing make her the Cathedral's most beloved figure. Almost nobody inside knows that the bard Venti is Barbatos himself; when Venti declared himself the god, a nun simply went back to her paperwork.

Rosaria's records show the Church's formal side: compulsory classes, theological essays and hymn practice supervised by sisters such as Mother Maria and Sister Ophila. Barbara's Vision came while she was nursing a feverish boy for the Church and sang for him for the first time.

History: The Viewpoint text says the site was once a palatial estate from which the aristocracy displayed its power, before it became a place of worship tended by Barbatos' devotees. During the Stormterror crisis the Lyre was stolen from its basement, and outside its doors Signora took Venti's Gnosis.

Later the Cathedral kept records of strange incidents such as "The Lost Statue of The Seven" and "The Tyrant's Final Fury", which Barbara consulted for the Traveler while investigating the Abyss Order. In 6.5, after the Nod-Krai expedition, Seamus Pegg was back at work there, hearing confessions and receiving the expedition's personnel report.

Atmosphere: Quiet and high-ceilinged, with many windows (the sisters clean them all by hand), with murmured prayers, the odd scolding from Sister Victoria and singing practice. Outside, wind sweeps the high plaza, Sister Grace leads open-air prayers at the statue by day, Albert hovers near the doors, and a knight on the steps grumbles about his knees.

Quests: Prologue Act II (Venti's Plan, Venti's New Plan): the attempt to borrow and then steal the Holy Lyre. Prologue Act III (Song of the Dragon and Freedom): the Lyre is returned and Signora attacks Venti outside. Chapter I Act IV (Dishonorable Trial): the Traveler consults the clergy about the Abyss Order.

Barbara's Hangout (1.4) starts with Sister Victoria worried about her, and asks the Traveler to clean the Cathedral. The daily commission "Stop, Albert. Stop!" has Victoria sending the Traveler to chase off Albert. Dahlia's anecdote "Day of Confession" (6.5) is set at the doors and inside. Lohen's hidden objective "Reporting Back" (6.5) ends there with Seamus.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Cathedral is in normal use. Seamus Pegg has returned from Varka's expedition and works there again, taking on work the clergy carried alone for years. The Church has the Holy Lyre back, and Barbara has refused to lend it out again.

Before his return, Cardinal Calvin carried his duties. Dahlia expects Seamus to be working at the Cathedral for some time; Barbara, still awkward around her father, calls him by his title there and has avoided confessing to him.

67.comment: Favonius Cathedral: The Theft of the Holy Lyre der Himmel
67.content:
In Prologue Act II, Venti needed the Holy Lyre der Himmel, the rosewood lyre Barbatos once played, to cleanse Dvalin. Sister Gotelinde turned him away when he asked to borrow it and ignored his claim to be Barbatos, going back to the Cathedral's paperwork. When the Traveler asked on the Knights' behalf, she explained the three signatures required and noted the Seneschal was away. So the Traveler sneaked into the basement at night, past patrolling guards, only for a Fatui Cicin Mage to snatch the Lyre first. Knights caught the Traveler at the scene and they fled with Venti.

Knight Otto guards the stairs to the basement by day during this period. The Lyre came back into the Traveler's hands in the quest Chasing Shadows, its Anemo power exhausted, and was partly repaired before the confrontation with Dvalin.

68.comment: Favonius Cathedral: Signora's Ambush at the Cathedral
68.content: At the end of the Prologue, Jean asked the Traveler to return the Holy Lyre at the Cathedral. Barbara received it badly damaged; Venti gave it a quick illusion so it only looked repaired, then slipped out. Outside, Fatui agents froze Paimon and Venti, held the Traveler, and the Harbinger Signora tore Venti's Gnosis from his chest before fleeing ahead of the Knights. Barbara found them afterwards, but her healing did nothing for Venti, who left for Windrise.

69.comment: Favonius Cathedral: Clergy of the Cathedral
69.content:
Victoria hears confessions, gives guidance not everyone wants, and obsesses over sinners who will not change; she keeps an eye on the heavy drinker Nimrod and on Albert. Grace is a motherly nun who cares for children without parents in Mondstadt (Glory and Timmie call her mother) and leads open-air prayers. Jilliana, Lily's mother, left the Treasure Hoarders for her family and became a nun. Gotelinde manages Cathedral paperwork. Cardinal Calvin was acting Seneschal during Seamus' absence.

Mother Maria and Sister Ophila appear in Rosaria's stories, despairing of her truancy and of her theological essays.

70.comment: Favonius Cathedral: Dahlia's Day of Confession
70.content: After Seamus Pegg's return, Deacon Dahlia was one of the first to make confession to him at the Cathedral. Light-heartedly, he confessed to hiding from Barbara that Venti is Barbatos, to drinking, and to slipping off for a drink with Rosaria. He asked Seamus about Frederica's whereabouts on Barbara's behalf, then heard Seamus' own confession in turn. Seamus mentioned that Jean was working overtime at headquarters when he got home.

71.comment: Favonius Cathedral: Dainsleif at the Cathedral
71.content: While tracking the Abyss Order in Chapter I Act IV, the Traveler and Dainsleif came to the Cathedral. Dainsleif questioned how much the Anemo Archon gave back for so grand a statue and cathedral, then waited outside rather than risk insulting the Church. Barbara refused to lend the Holy Lyre again, and told from Church records of the vanished "Lost Statue of The Seven" and "The Tyrant's Final Fury". Rosaria passed on Jean's order that Barbara keep to her duties with the clergy.

72.content:
Field Tiller (also: Weird Statue, First Field Tiller, Tyrant's Final Fury): The Field Tiller is an inactive Ruin Guard on the upper deck of the central tower of Stormterror's Lair in the Brightcrown Mountains. Before the quest We Will Be Reunited the game calls it a Weird Statue. It is the original prototype of the war machines now known as Ruin Guards.

"Field Tiller" was a Khaenri'ah codename for such machines. This one was far stronger than its later copies and, according to Dainsleif, unrestricted in combat power.

History: The first Field Tiller left Khaenri'ah and wandered Teyvat, ending up in Wolvendom, where Boreas took it for a challenger and fought it. Badly damaged, it fled to the ruins of Old Mondstadt and became immobile but still active. Sensing danger, it fired missiles at anyone approaching the old city. Mondstadters, who knew little of Ruin Machines, took this for a last outburst of the dead storm god Decarabian and called it the Tyrant's Final Fury. This lasted about a year before the machine shut down.

Dainsleif says all current Ruin Guards are replicas of this prototype. He cites a Khaenri'ah saying that land is won with steel and blood rather than farm tools. The Abyss Order planned to place its eye into the Defiled Statue and attach Osial's limbs to it, creating a mechanised god. When the Traveler's elemental sight failed to extract the eye, Dainsleif explained that the machine does not run on elemental energy; he removed it himself and vowed to guard it.

Status as of 7.1: Inactive. After We Will Be Reunited it is labelled Field Tiller rather than Weird Statue, and says nothing. Its eye is in Dainsleif's keeping as of the quest; no later change is reported through 7.1.

73.comment: Field Tiller: The Tyrant's Final Fury
73.content: The name Mondstadters gave to the missiles that struck at anyone approaching Old Mondstadt for about a year. It was the prototype Field Tiller reacting to perceived danger, not Decarabian.

74.content:
Floral Whisper: Floral Whisper is a small flower shop in the market district of Mondstadt City. Its owner is Flora, who sells flowers for Mora. The shop is open from 06:00 to 19:00.

Flora is the younger sister of the botanist Chloris, who wanders around Windrise. Unlike her sister, Flora cares only about the flowers themselves.

Places: A flower stall-shop with five kinds of flower on offer: Sweet Flower, Windwheel Aster, Cecilia, Small Lamp Grass and Calla Lily. In gameplay terms the stock refreshes every three days but the range never changes.

The flowers on display are strictly for sale. If a customer tries to handle them by day, Flora scolds them that they are goods; at night Donna takes over the scolding in her place.

People: Flora is the owner. She is described as having short blonde hair, light blue-green eyes and a pink and white dress. She keeps an imaginary friend, a Bloatty Floatty she calls Mr. Floatty.

Flora is Chloris's younger sister and shares none of her interest in botany. Alodia of Fragrant Whispers in Dornman Port says Flora sometimes buys flowers from Millhaven.

Culture: Flora's festival-time dialogue appears only during the Invitation of Windblume event. Outside it she talks plainly about flowers, for example insisting that dandelions count as flowers.

Atmosphere: A daytime shop of cut flowers in a busy market, with an owner who treats the display as stock and not as something to touch.

Travel: In the market district of Mondstadt City, near the Donna and Flora spot on the map. It closes in the evening.

Status as of 7.1: Operating as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

75.content:
Forgotten Sword Cemetery (also: Sword Cemetery, Unnamed Sword Cemetery): The Forgotten Sword Cemetery lies in the middle of the large lake in Dadaupa Gorge, Galesong Hill. It is described as having witnessed the battle against the monsters of Khaenri'ah, and it is guarded by a three-layer seal.

In the world quest "Break the Sword Cemetery Seal", Dr. Livingstone explains that three hilichurl camps hold the tri-seal. Defeating each camp's guards unlocks an Elemental Monument, and breaking all three opens the cemetery.

Geography: It sits at the centre of the lake in Dadaupa Gorge. The three camps tied to the seal lie south, north and south-east of it, in the gorge among the Meaty, Sleeper and Eclipse hilichurl tribes' territory.

The three seals can be released in any order. Unlocking them gives access to a treasure at the cemetery's centre.

History: The only history canon gives is that the place witnessed the battle against the monsters of Khaenri'ah. Who the fallen were, and whose swords lie there, is not stated in the sources read.

Dangers: Hilichurls and some Fatui skirmishers are common in the gorge. Mitachurls guard the camps linked to the seal.

Atmosphere: A still, windswept lake island of old blades, quiet apart from the hilichurl camps around the shore. Suits solemn, mysterious scenes about forgotten war.

76.comment: Forgotten Sword Cemetery: Dadaupa Gorge tri-seal
76.content: The Forgotten Sword Cemetery is protected by three layers of seal. In the world quest started by Dr. Livingstone, the Traveler breaks them by defeating guards at three hilichurl camps and activating the Elemental Monuments there.

77.content:
Fragrant Whispers: Fragrant Whispers is a flower shop in the middle of Dornman Port, the port town in the northern Windrest Peak area of Mondstadt. Alodia owns it. It first appeared in Version 6.5.

Besides the flowers common in Mondstadt, Alodia says she sells new varieties cultivated by Lilian of Millhaven.

People: Alodia runs the shop and works with Lilian from Millhaven, relying on her skill in growing flowers. Her idle greeting offers customers a flower.

If the player has the Special Perfume: Wind's Breath effect, Alodia remarks on the unusual scent.

Culture: Alodia says a few flowers around a home lift the mood. The Millhaven varieties are unique to that village, so even Flora of Mondstadt City sometimes buys them. Alodia mentions she should send Flora more for the next Windblume Festival.

The stock mixes flowers commonly found in Mondstadt with the newer varieties Lilian has carefully cultivated.

Travel: In the centre of Dornman Port.

Status as of 7.1: Operating as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

78.content:
Frostbearing Tree (also: Frostbearing Trees): The Frostbearing Tree is a new sprout of an ancient Irminsul tree that the Skyfrost Nail destroyed. It was revived by the blood of the Abyssal dragon Durin and grows in Dragonspine, marked with red rather than the usual blue.

The Traveler frees it from a shell of Ancient Rime in the world quest "In the Mountains". Offering Crimson Agates then makes it grow, and at full strength it bears a single fruit, the Frostbearer catalyst.

History: The tree was once an Irminsul tree revered by the ancient civilisation of Sal Vindagnyr, and the kingdom's last princess is said to have been born beneath it. About six thousand years ago Celestia drove the Skyfrost Nail into Sal Vindagnyr, burying the mountain in ice and snow, and the tree's trunk and canopy shattered and froze. The Crimson Agate's archive text says the trunk and canopy broke into many fragments that were then frozen.

The princess saved one branch and tried to graft it onto another plant on a small island, but the attempt failed and she is implied to have died. About 500 years ago Dvalin killed Durin over Dragonspine, and his blood seeped into the mountain's ley lines; this revived the tree, which is described as having a "thirst for more power" and seems tainted by the Abyss.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not story: Crimson Agates scattered around Dragonspine can be offered to the tree to raise its Gratitude level and earn rewards. At the maximum level crystalline crimson butterflies appear on its branches.

Atmosphere: A great old tree glowing with scarlet markings against the snow, at once hopeful and unsettling because of the Abyss-tainted blood that revived it.

79.content: Crimson Agate is a crystal formed from concentrated life force and an energy unique to Dragonspine, found across the mountain. It is the ideal nutrient for the Frostbearing Tree.

80.comment: Frostbearing Tree: Princess of Sal Vindagnyr and the tree
80.content: The last princess of Sal Vindagnyr is said to have been born beneath the Irminsul tree that became the Frostbearing Tree. She saved a branch after the Skyfrost Nail fell and tried to graft it elsewhere; the attempt failed and she is implied to have died.

81.content:
Galesong Hill: Galesong Hill is the windswept eastern part of Mondstadt, a region of open hills running down to the sea. Its best-known spot is Windrise, a plain under a giant oak where a Statue of the Seven stands, said to mark the place where Vennessa ascended to Celestia. East of it lie the Falcon Coast and Cape Oath, favourite places for walks and for young couples, while the rugged Dadaupa Gorge belongs to hilichurl tribes.

There is no town here; the area is travelled rather than lived in. Offshore, the island of Musk Reef holds the portal to the Spiral Abyss and is reached through a time tunnel at Cape Oath.

Geography: Rolling grassland and breezy plains that fall to a shallow, sandy coast. Windrise sits inland; Falcon Coast stretches east from it to the sea, and with Cape Oath it shelters a bay east of Mondstadt. Dadaupa Gorge is a mountain stretch of cliffs and ledges nearby. Local plants include calla lily, dandelion seed, small lamp grass and windwheel aster.

Official text says the long coastline and shallow water make the shore pleasant to walk, and that falcons can often be seen above the blue waves. Cape Oath is the south-eastern corner of Mondstadt's surrounds and borders Galesong Hill; from its drop in terrain Windrise, which faces the sea, is easy to see. Dadaupa Gorge is described as a mountain near the city crowded with hilichurls. In Hilichurlian, "dadaupa" means "large mountain" according to the Handy Handbook of Hilichurlian.

Places: Windrise (the oak and the Statue of the Seven; the Temple of the Falcon ruin lies beneath it as a one-time domain); Falcon Coast; Cape Oath; Dadaupa Gorge with the Forgotten Sword Cemetery; Musk Reef.

Windrise has a fishing point, a Ruins Torch and an Elemental Monument. Dadaupa Gorge also holds the Temple of the Lion domain, a Ruins Torch and an Elemental Monument. The Temple of the Falcon is a ruin deep underground through which strong winds still pour.

People: The hilichurl tribes of Dadaupa Gorge: the Meaty tribe, the Sleeper tribe and the Eclipse tribe. Otherwise only passers-by: the botanist Chloris, the historian Dr. Edith and the Knight of Favonius Godwin are met at Windrise, the researcher Dr. Livingstone in the gorge, and on Falcon Coast the knight Mack and the locals Jill and Will.

Culture: Windrise is where Mondstadters remember Vennessa, the gladiator who founded the Knights of Favonius and is counted as the Falcon of the West among the Four Winds. Cape Oath is known as a romantic spot, a favourite place for couples.

Official viewpoint text says the plain "bathes in an everlasting breeze" and that an ancient tree left by a heroine speaks softly in the wind. The expedition description says the oak's shade shelters the Statue of the Seven at its foot from rain and wind, as Vennessa once protected Mondstadt.

History: Windrise is the site where Vennessa is said to have ascended to Celestia about 1,000 years ago, becoming a god who now watches over Mondstadt; the huge oak is believed to have grown afterwards. Falcon Coast takes its name from the first Knight of Boreas, who fought demons from the Dark Sea on the shore: thousands of falcons circled the remains for several days.

Musk Reef was once the summit of a great mountain, Pilos Peak, which the adventurer Leonard tried and failed to climb. When Barbatos blew snow and ice off the land about 2,600 years ago, the peak was swept from its place and the melting ice formed the sea, leaving the island. Dadaupa Gorge's Forgotten Sword Cemetery is described as a witness to the battle against the monsters of Khaenri'ah.

Atmosphere: Constant sea-breeze, long grass, falcons overhead, a lone oak throwing deep shade. Sunrises and sunsets are especially fine from Cape Oath. The gorge is the opposite: rough, echoing, with hilichurl camps and the occasional mitachurl.

Dangers: Hilichurls of every kind, slimes, and in the gorge Fatui skirmishers, mitachurls and Abyss mages. Dadaupa Gorge is the dangerous part; Falcon Coast and Windrise are mild.

Cape Oath is listed as the area of an Electro Hypostasis boss, and Electro slimes there guard the seelie that raise the wind current to the time tunnel.

Travel: Reached from Mondstadt City by road east across the plain. The time tunnel at Cape Oath carries travellers to Musk Reef. Windrise is a convenient rest stop with a Statue of the Seven.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Galesong Hill is peaceful countryside; none of the pages read for this entry records a change to it after Version 1.0.

Its Archive neighbours Windrest Peak (opened in 6.5) and Starfell Valley are where recent Mondstadt events have been centred.

82.content:
Windrise is a plain where the giant oak grows, believed to have sprung up after Vennessa ascended to Celestia on this spot. A Statue of the Seven stands in the tree's shade. Mondstadters say she now watches over them as the Falcon of the West. See the Mondstadt entry for the full account of her rebellion.

The Windrise viewpoint is titled Windswept Wilderness.

83.comment: Galesong Hill: Falcon Coast and Cape Oath
83.content: Falcon Coast runs from Windrise to the sea and, with Cape Oath, shelters a bay east of Mondstadt. Its name comes from the first Knight of Boreas, whose fight against demons from the Dark Sea drew thousands of falcons. Cape Oath is where two unnamed lovers once swore an oath, and young couples still come, especially for sunrise and sunset. A time tunnel here leads to Musk Reef.

84.content: A rugged mountain gorge that is home to three hilichurl tribes, the Meaty, Sleeper and Eclipse tribes. The Forgotten Sword Cemetery in it is remembered as a witness to the fight against the monsters of Khaenri'ah. The place is known for its danger, with mitachurls and samachurls more common than in the surrounding country.

85.comment: Galesong Hill: Musk Reef and Pilos Peak
85.content: Musk Reef is a small island east of Cape Oath whose main feature is the portal to the Spiral Abyss. Before Barbatos reshaped the land about 2,600 years ago it was the summit of Pilos Peak, which the adventurer Leonard tried and failed to climb; his journal is the book Of Mountains and Seas.

86.content:
Golden Apple Archipelago (also: Haar Islands, Golden Archipelago): The Golden Apple Archipelago is a set of mountainous islands in the sea east of Mondstadt. It was a limited-time summer event map: first as the setting of Midsummer Island Adventure (1.6), when Klee and her friends followed a mysterious letter from "Dodo-King" to it, and again in Summertime Odyssey (2.8) with a new look. It was formerly the fog-bound Haar Islands. It is not accessible as of 7.1.

Its islands are the tops of Mondstadt's old mountains, flipped upside down into the sea when Barbatos reshaped the land. The archipelago was the first place to introduce the Waverider boat.

Geography: In 1.6 it began as a handful of small islands in thick fog and, after the quest "Summer Vacation: Proceed With Caution", rose into a group of mountainous islands under a golden sun, with a tropical feel. Four named areas: Pudding Isle (where visitors start), Twinning Isle to the north, Broken Isle to the west and Minacious Isle to the south. Later in 1.6 further islands emerged, among them a Central Platform where the samurai puppet stands.

The 2.8 version gave each isle a theme. Pudding Isle: a Kaedehara Kazuha-themed island in two halves that switch between Mondstadt, Liyue and Inazuma styles. Broken Isle: Xinyan-themed, with parts that rise and fall at an overgrown drum. Twinning Isle: Fischl-themed and home to Night Raven statues. Minacious Isle: Mona-themed, letting visitors travel between two time periods. Specialties of several nations grow here (dandelions, starconches, sea ganoderma and more), unusual for one area. The sky shows no Celestia, unlike the main map.

History: About 2,600 years ago, when Barbatos terraformed Mondstadt, he split the tops off mountains and they landed upside-down in the sea, forming the islands (the Haar Islands; "haar" is a cold sea fog, and the islands were initially covered in it). A group of shipwrecked people settled and lived on the archipelago for generations; many tried to escape and canon does not say whether any succeeded.

About 500 years ago a pirate fleet under Ako Domeki, thrown off course in a battle with the Shogunate's forces at Seirai Island, was shipwrecked on the islands. It carried a stolen samurai puppet (a Maguu Kenki) that protected the islanders until it was damaged. Pirates and islanders together devised an escape route that used the archipelago's odd features and everyone left; Domeki's fleet returned to a ruined Seirai Island. The wiki's timeline (a fan compilation of conch and quest text) also places Minacious Isle's arrival, with a Seelie, from Mondstadt waters before the settlers.

People: No permanent inhabitants in the present. The islands are home to hilichurls, slimes, Mimic creatures and other monsters. In 1.6 Klee, Jean, Barbara, Kaeya, Diluc, Albedo and Razor appear as event NPCs. In 2.8 the event focuses on Fischl, Mona, Kazuha and Xinyan and their islands, with the Night Raven statues on Twinning Isle.

Dangers: Dense fog once made the sea around the islands extremely dangerous, and the changing winds and tides made escape hard. Present-day threats are hilichurl camps, slimes, Abyss mages, Mimic creatures and a Maguu Kenki on the Central Platform (a gameplay boss).

In 2.8 an area on the archipelago also features a Fatui dream machine, shown in event art as both broken and repaired.

Travel: In 1.6 Klee's group were flown to the islands on Dvalin, summoned by Venti. The islands are also reached by the Waverider boat, which is the area's characteristic means of travel. In 1.6 a time tunnel from Minacious Isle back to Falcon Coast could be used once, during the quest "The Winding Homeward Way". The archipelago has its own map tab, separate from Teyvat.

Quests: In 1.6 the Midsummer Island Adventure quests were "Mysterious Islands: Journey to the Unknown", "Summer Vacation: Proceed With Caution", "Dodo-King of the Sea: Lying in Wait" and "The Final Riddle: A Secret Uncovered". World quests included "A Trip Through Fog and Wind", "The Other Side of Isle and Sea", "From Outer Lands", "Who Wields the Wild Wind?", "They Who Hear the Sea" and "The Winding Homeward Way". The 2.8 Summertime Odyssey began with the quest "The Golden Apple Vacation Returns!".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the archipelago is not accessible: both event runs have ended and the map is removed. Nothing in Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content revisits it. Its events remain canon but are not widely known.

Many of its elements, such as the Waverider, reappeared later in Inazuma.

87.comment: Golden Apple Archipelago: Midsummer Island Adventure (1.6)
87.content: This limited-time event (June 2021) began when Klee received a letter from "Dodo-King" threatening to take her plush Dodoco away unless she proved herself. With the Traveler and Paimon she followed clues to the archipelago, accompanied for her safety by Acting Grand Master Jean and Deaconess Barbara; Dvalin flew them there at Venti's call. Kaeya, Diluc, Albedo and Razor, who had received letters of their own, followed and were briefly separated when Razor jumped off Dvalin's back. The mystery ends with the revelation that Klee's mother Alice had arranged it all so her daughter would have a memorable summer.

88.content: In this limited-time event (July to August 2022), the archipelago returned with a new look after Fischl received an important missive and set out with others for another summer journey. Each isle has the theme of one character: Kazuha (Pudding Isle), Xinyan (Broken Isle), Fischl (Twinning Isle) and Mona (Minacious Isle). Gameplay centred on Waverider challenges and "Phantom Realm" trials. The plot beyond that outline is not summarised here because it was not read in full.

89.content:
Good Hunter: Good Hunter is the most popular restaurant in Mondstadt City. The waitress Sara serves simple food and cooking ingredients and sells recipes. It stands in the market district, across from Mondstadt General Goods.

Its map description says the only venue busier is the tavern, and that it is always full of appetising smells. When tables are taken, take-out is the fallback.

Places: A restaurant with a take-out counter and an outdoor billboard, Good Hunter's Daily Recommendation, beside it. The sign shows Teyvat script reading OPEN and Fine Food.

The billboard advertises a Cold Cut Platter of Good Hunter sausages, Wolvendom boar bacon and ham dried in the winds of the Archon, served with Mist Flowers to keep the meat cold.

People: Sara is the waitress. Before the Stormterror affair was resolved she complained that business had collapsed because no one felt like eating.

A quest called Food Delivery shows that the take-out service is badly understaffed because demand is so high.

Culture: Good Hunter prides itself on fresh local ingredients: meat comes from hunters in Springvale, and it uses home-grown Mondstadt apples. Sara says it is known for its venison steak and Satisfying Salad.

The tavern Angel's Share is the only other venue the map description rates above it for popularity.

Atmosphere: A loud, welcoming eatery full of cooking smells, always short of staff.

Travel: In the market district of Mondstadt City, across from Mondstadt General Goods. Open all day.

Status as of 7.1: Open and busy as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

90.content:
Goth Grand Hotel (also: Goth Hotel): The Goth Grand Hotel is Mondstadt City's hotel, owned by Ludwig Goth. The Fatui delegation has reserved the entire building, and the guard Luke stands at the door to keep unauthorised people out. Ordinary guests can no longer stay.

The Goth family has long been in the hotel and catering trade and prides itself on serving Mondstadt. The Fatui lease runs against that tradition, which bothers Goth.

People: Goth also owns the Dawn Breeze Inn and rents out other housing in the city. Luke is dedicated to his post, repeatedly saying that the hotel is reserved for the Fatui delegation alone. He sometimes lets secrets about the Fatui slip and then hastily denies it. Early on, he predicts the Mondstadters will come begging the Fatui for help and expects Signora to arrive and handle the Stormterror crisis.

Goth is upset about the lease but accepted it: Harbinger Pantalone paid the entire period upfront with a sum Goth could not refuse. Goth says the Fatui's behaviour concerns him more than Stormterror's: they seem always to be in meetings, and they even chased away the cleaning staff. He worries about what they are planning and fears for the hotel's name. He also admits he had planned to renovate the hotel, which the lease made moot.

History: Before the Traveler arrived, Pantalone booked the whole hotel for the Fatui's exclusive and indefinite use. Goth objected in principle, since his family motto is serving the people, but took the payment.

Trivia: in the Chinese, Japanese and Russian versions of the game the hotel's name uses "Goethe" rather than "Goth".

Atmosphere: A closed, tense building at the heart of the city: a doorway watched by a surly Fatui guard, and a hotel booked solid by a single party. Goth's cleaning staff have been chased away from the Fatui's rooms, and no ordinary traveller is admitted.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the wiki records no end to the Fatui reservation; treat the hotel as still closed to the public unless a scene says otherwise.

91.content: Goth is the owner and manager of the Goth Grand Hotel. He has a son, Marvin, whose betrothal to Marla he opposes. Goth also owned the house with a magic laboratory that Mona rents in her story quest, after she dispelled a Hydro seal on it. He wonders aloud whether he might take a trip to Sumeru.

92.comment: Goth Grand Hotel: Luke the Guard
92.content: Luke is a Fatui member who guards the hotel door. He calls himself loyal and never abandons his post, but boasts about the Fatui's strength and slips out secrets before backpedalling.

93.content:
Hexenzirkel's Island in the Sky (also: Hexenzirkel's floating island, Hexenzirkel tea party island): Hexenzirkel's Island in the Sky is a floating island above Falcon Coast where the Hexenzirkel used to hold tea parties. Barbatos looks after access to it, and one has to speak an incantation at the cliff to enter.

It was first opened during the limited-time Windblume's Breath event (version 3.5), and became permanently accessible once the Traveler completes the Paralogism archon quest (5.6).

Places: At its centre stands a long tea table with seven chairs: three on one side, two on the other and one at each end. The Lantern of Utmost Joy sits at the table's centre, and a small phonograph like Alice used in "Midsummer Island Adventure" stands near the head. Books, flowers and silverware are scattered around.

The lantern can be operated by four people sitting around it and saying the words "Please allow me to disturb your happy peace."

Travel: The incantation is spoken at the cliff above Falcon Coast, and begins "Place the squirrel on the back of the pointy-eared cat..." (the full verse is in the event quest). Venti granted the Traveler access during the Windblume Festival's event quest.

History: After Paralogism the island stays reachable. There the Traveler faces "The Game Before the Gate", the trial of Alice and Barbeloth. In the quest "The Gardener" the Hexenzirkel's trial is accepted as part of the story of the Interlude Chapter.

Atmosphere: An airy, whimsical garden party suspended in cloud, with tea things and flowers and the faint music of a phonograph; a place of gentle riddles that can turn serious.

94.comment: Hexenzirkel's Island in the Sky: Hexenzirkel tea party island access
94.content: The Hexenzirkel's floating island above Falcon Coast is entered by an incantation spoken at the cliff and kept open by Barbatos. During the Windblume's Breath event the Traveler used it to find the Lantern of Utmost Joy.

95.content:
Imaginarium Theater (also: Theater Lobby, Mysterious Room): The Imaginarium Theater is a hidden room entered from Mondstadt's Knights of Favonius library, a stage and lounge where guests perform fantasy plays. It is looked after by Wolfy, a small talking stuffed wolf. It appeared in Version 4.7.

Guests must be invited, and can invite friends. The room is described as the place before the story begins and after it ends, so guests have all the time they need.

Places: The Theater Lobby, formerly called the Mysterious Room, holds a sofa where Wolfy dozes, a painting whose figure moves, a table of fresh desserts, a locked treasure chest, a wardrobe, a curtain and an old desk with a stopped clock behind it. Furnishings are self-serve: guests can change the music or have their fortune told.

The wiki notes that the Traveler's remarks at the wardrobe and desk echo The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe and Goethe's Faust, and that the moving painting features the Boar Princess of the storybook of that name.

People: Wolfy is the concierge. He is a small stuffed wolf wearing a golden purple crown and a purple bow tie with two stars. Madame Mage put him in charge, and he waited a long time for guests, falling asleep while he did.

Madame Mage is an unnamed mage whom Wolfy says can see the path of fate in starry reflections. He says her friends are mages too, each a master of one kind of magic, and one of them writes with a quill and a bottle of ink holding 'fantasy truth'. He says the others turn that into 'true fantasy'.

Culture: The room runs on performance: Wolfy says the stage becomes a place of magic only when guests believe from the heart that it is real. Toy Medals, which the audience is said to give for a good show, can be exchanged with Wolfy for Thespian Tricks, which are poses for photographs.

Wolfy likes storybooks and imagines himself as Wolfy the Brave, Wolfy the Wise or the Big Bad Wolfy. He remembers a curse of unmelting ice, playing with White Fang, and a victory parade in which a queen honoured him, and cannot tell these dreams from real memory.

Gameplay: Gameplay, not story. Unlocked at Adventure Rank 35 after the world quest Unbegun, Unending Story. The player assembles a cast of characters, plays through numbered acts that include boss stages, and earns Fantasia Flowers, Stella and Toy Medals. Each season features three elements, and there are five difficulties up to Lunar Mode.

Each character has two units of Vigor, spent as stages are cleared. Supporting Cast characters borrowed from friends can be added. Thespian Tricks from past seasons stay on sale after a season ends.

Atmosphere: Warm, strange and theatrical: soft light, curtains, a toy host who cheerfully forgets his own name, and the sense that the room sits outside ordinary time.

Travel: Enter by a door on the lower level of the Knights of Favonius library in Mondstadt City, which does not open until the player has completed the unlocking quest.

Quests: In the unlocking quest, Unbegun, Unending Story, the Traveler and Paimon enter the room, find the toy and, once an act is performed, meet Wolfy properly. The wiki also notes the Theater Lobby is visited during the quest The Gardener.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, with new seasons rotating in.

96.content: Wolfy is the concierge of the Imaginarium Theater: a small stuffed wolf with a golden purple crown, purple bow tie and beady black eyes. He woke from a long sleep when the Traveler arrived, at first could not recall his own name, and says Madame Mage made him concierge in a dream of a garden of forking paths. He does not know where the theater is.

97.content:
Knights of Favonius Base (also: Dornman Port Knights base, Windrest Peak Knights base): The Knights of Favonius Base is the Knights' forward base at Dornman Port in Windrest Peak, built around the 5th (Ranged) Company. Detachments from the 6th (Logistics), 7th (Combined Arms), 8th (Support) and 10th (Investigation) Companies are stationed there too. "Knights of Favonius Base" is an unofficial name.

It opened to players with Windrest Peak in 6.5. Lohen, the Ranged Company's Vice Captain, is posted here.

People: Residents named on the wiki: Ematol, the Investigative Team's weapons officer; Glenfidia of Logistics; Gunther and Ursula, Ranged Company snipers; Herstal and Koch, Support Company gunsmiths; and Phonia, a Combined Arms intelligence officer.

Lohen loves fighting up close but admits that ranged firepower is the company's bread and butter. Observed scenes: he uses himself as the target, apple in hand, during shooting practice, with terrified Gunther and Ursula under threat of "special training" if they miss. He asks the Traveler to help choose between roasting Electro Slimes and freezing Hydro Slimes, saying he likes the plunge of a blade into solid ice. Herstal, the gunsmith, offers tea and runs marksmanship challenges, telling the Traveler that aim slips if practice is skipped for a day.

Places: A compound with a shooting range, training dummies, and a bulletin board for Dornman Port requests. A knight watching the dummies praises the Honorary Knight's strength as the Traveler smashes them.

History: Dornman Port is a major trade hub that was an Abyss front line five hundred years ago. The Combined Arms Company's Captain Frederica Gunnhildr was ordered back to Mondstadt to help defend it. The base reflects the Knights' modern emphasis on firearms: the Support Company provides muskets, mostly for the Ranged Company's snipers.

After the events of "A Knight's Legacy" (6.6), the Ranged Company's Captain seat is vacant for the time being, so the chain of command falls to the second-highest officer, Vice Captain Lohen.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the base is active and the Ranged Company remains stationed there.

98.comment: Knights of Favonius Base: Ranged Company Soldiers
98.content: The base's named personnel are Gunther and Ursula (Ranged Company snipers), Herstal and Koch (Support Company gunsmiths), Ematol (Investigative Team weapons officer), Glenfidia (Logistics Company member) and Phonia (Combined Arms intelligence officer). None has a detailed profile on the wiki.

99.content:
Knights of Favonius Headquarters (also: Knights Headquarters, Favonius Headquarters, Mondstadt Library, Knights of Favonius Library): The Knights of Favonius Headquarters is the order's main building in Mondstadt City and the centre of the nation's government. Inside are the Grand Master's office, where Acting Grand Master Jean works almost without pause, Chief Alchemist Albedo's office on the second floor, a locked solitary confinement room that Klee has more or less made her own, and the Mondstadt Library, kept by the librarian Lisa. The library is the largest in northern Teyvat and is open to everyone.

This is where newcomers are brought to meet the Knights: Kaeya escorted the Traveler here after Stormterror's attack, and Jean welcomed them and laid out the plan against Dvalin.

Places: Main hall on the ground floor, with the library and the Grand Master's office leading off it. The Grand Master's office holds a large map of Mondstadt on the wall, a desk and bookshelves, and a grandfather clock. Albedo's office is upstairs and usually kept shut. Three rooms stay locked; the ground-floor one is solitary confinement. The library has two levels: an upper floor with the librarian's desk and a lower floor.

In the library basement stands a heavy poplar-wood door that is older than the Knights and survived the great fire. The Knights officially say the restricted section lies behind it. A door on the library's lower floor leads to the Theater Lobby of the Imaginarium Theater (4.7). Kaeya takes the Traveler to a courtyard just outside the building for a private talk. The stairwell continues to upper floors that are never shown.

People: Jean (Acting Grand Master), Lisa (librarian), Albedo (Chief Alchemist), Klee (when confined), and the knights and captains who report here, including Kaeya.

Knights Athos and Porthos guard the front door. Inside, Wood watches the confinement room and Wyratt guards a library door, asking visitors to keep quiet and wipe their shoes before going in. The hilichurl-language scholar Ella Musk studies in the library; the travelling scholar Sayid reads there at night.

Grand Master Varka's desk is here, and he has been back since 6.4. When Hertha, Eula and the captains of the 2nd and 3rd Companies, Note and Skeiron, were called in for Albedo's case in 5.6, headquarters was crowded with knights.

Governance: Mondstadt's government works out of this building: the Grand Master's office sets the Knights' orders, receives captains' reports and the Grand Master's letters, and handles the paperwork the order is famous for. Discipline is enforced here too, from Klee's confinement to the trial Jean convened for Albedo, for which every captain was summoned.

Culture: The library is free to use and lending is not limited to Mondstadters: apart from the restricted section, every book is open to the public. The posted "Library Rules - Seventh Edition" cut the list down to three rules: be quiet, do not damage books, return books on time. It adds, darkly, that everyone already knows how violations are dealt with.

With the right paperwork even a whole set of volumes can be borrowed for a year or more. Works from Yae Publishing House are shelved under "Children and Teens". The Favonius Codex was the Knights' scholars' handmade tome, and the library's founding ideal is that songs fade and wine is fleeting, but what is written lasts.

History: When the Knights were founded after Vennessa's rebellion, the Dawn Knight Ragnvindr turned the aristocrats' indoor baths into a library. Gifts from bards, scholars and travellers made it the largest collection in the northern half of the continent. The "Great Fire of Fall Equinox" later burned it, leaving only a fraction of the collection (one-sixth, per the Chinese text), yet it remains the largest library in the north.

The building was the base for the Knights' response to Stormterror in the Prologue (1.0). In 3.1 Varka's letter from the expedition was read in the main hall and the office. In 5.6 Albedo was tried and later carried out the ritual for Durin from his office. In 6.2 Alice smuggled a mages' book in among a large donation of books, and in 6.4 Varka returned.

Atmosphere: Hushed in the library (the guard will remind you), businesslike in the hall, and buried in paperwork in the Grand Master's office, where Jean works late and a grandfather clock ticks. Faint crackling from behind the confinement door means Klee is in again.

Quests: Prologue Act I "Knights of Favonius" (meeting Jean and Lisa), Prologue Act II "Shadow Over Mondstadt", Kaeya's story quest (1.0), Interlude Chapter Act IV "Paralogism" (5.6), the world quest "Unexpected Commission" (6.2), and the Lupus Majoris act "To Those Who Embark on the Expedition" (6.4).

Kaeya's Hangout (3.8) involves reporting in the Acting Grand Master's office, and the Traveler can talk to Klee through the confinement-room door. The Of Ballads and Brews event quest "Sounds From Afar" (3.1) and the 6.4 event "Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind" also use the building.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the headquarters is fully active. Varka has been home since 6.4, Jean still holds the title Acting Grand Master and works long hours here, and Lisa still runs the library.

Varka's secret drinking money, tucked in the office desk, was found and handed to the Traveler as a reward after the 6.4 rescue. Seamus Pegg has mentioned Jean working overtime at headquarters after his return (6.5).

100.comment: Knights of Favonius Headquarters: The Mondstadt Library
100.content:
The library of the Knights of Favonius, run by Lisa, is the largest in northern Teyvat even after the Great Fire of Fall Equinox. Ragnvindr founded it in the old aristocrats' indoor baths. Anyone may read or borrow books, except from the restricted section, which officially lies behind an ancient poplar door in the basement, and which Lisa consults for dangerous research.

Lisa offered the Traveler books on monsters and a part-time job on first meeting. Xilonen of Natlan once napped in the library before moving to trees so as not to disturb readers. The Traveler is given the Teyvat Travel Guide - Mondstadt here in a world quest.

101.comment: Knights of Favonius Headquarters: The Grand Master's Office
101.content:
The office of the Grand Master, used day to day by Acting Grand Master Jean. Here Jean briefed the Traveler on Stormterror, consulted Lisa there as the Stormterror crisis deepened, and later assigned the Traveler their own investigation into Albedo's case. A large wall map of Mondstadt hangs inside.

In 3.1 Varka's letter told Lisa that a wooden box of things Razor's parents left him was in a cabinet above the third bookshelf to the right of the office's grandfather clock, and that it was time to give it to Razor.

102.comment: Knights of Favonius Headquarters: Albedo's Office and the Paralogism Trial
102.content: During Windblume in 5.6, Jean called the captains to headquarters because Albedo stood accused of murder and of disposing of remains. The Knights and the Church held a closed trial together, with Hertha prosecuting, Kaeya defending and Deacon Dahlia as assessor. Albedo said he had been in his second-floor office, and Sucrose confirmed he had been with her in the library, though she admitted she had fallen asleep. He was found guilty and taken away. Jean privately doubted the verdict and sent the Traveler to investigate, and a search of Albedo's office with Kaeya turned up a secret compartment in his desk, holding notes on an experiment. Later Mini Durin was found hiding in that office. During the festival fireworks Albedo began his long-prepared ritual there, lighting arrays across the city with Mini Durin at the centre. This led to Durin's rebirth. The trial itself turned out to have been planned by Albedo and the Knights over half a year to lure out a Durin-spawned impostor, the prosecuting "Hertha".

103.comment: Knights of Favonius Headquarters: Klee's Solitary Confinement Room
103.content: A locked ground-floor room that is formally the Knights' solitary confinement cell but is used almost only for Klee, who is shut in after her explosive mischief. The guard Wood jokes that it is more or less her private property and that crackling noises inside suggest she is working on new bombs.

104.comment: Knights of Favonius Headquarters: The Poplar Door and the Imaginarium Theater
104.content: The Favonius Codex says a sturdy poplar door in the library basement predates both the library and the Knights, and survived the fire. Officially the restricted section is behind it, but tales hint at a deeper secret. Since 4.7 a door on the library's lower floor opens onto the Theater Lobby of the Imaginarium Theater, whose concierge Wolfy is said to have been made by a mage.

105.content:
Knights of Favonius Ruins: The Knights of Favonius Ruins are the remains of an ancient battlefield beneath Dornman Port, where the Knights of Favonius fought the Abyss and where their dead lie buried. They are reached from the base of the port's old lighthouse. The ruins first appear in version 6.5.

In the world quest Winds Beneath the Tower of Silence, the Traveler traces a flashing alarm and rumoured ghosts to this place and finds only a hidden graveyard, old mechanisms and an Eye of the Storm.

Geography: The ruins sit in three underground levels below the old lighthouse of Dornman Port. Alarm mechanisms flash and doors are wired to them; strong air currents run through the passages. There are two entrances, the lighthouse's main door and a lesser-known one used by locals.

Moving crates to block the wind opens gates, a main control switch causes a floor collapse down to a cemetery of weathered tombstones, and a final cave opens onto where the Eye of the Storm falls. A teleport waypoint is unlocked in the ruins during the quest.

Places: The cemetery holds old graves whose inscriptions are unreadable but whose plots have been tended recently; Winslow cleared the weeds and cleaned the stones in recent days.

People: Winslow lives in the old lighthouse. He was terrified of the alarm, thought of the Abyss and then of ghosts, and had pushed to move the graves out to fields beyond the port. Odolf, a local who has recently been in Snezhnaya, tried to stop him.

Lennart and Matthew, drinkers at the Devil's Cut tavern, share the rumours and warn that Winslow was acting strangely. Odolf rigged the mechanism and added a lure for elemental creatures to scare Winslow into leaving the graves alone; it drew an Eye of the Storm instead of harmless Anemo slimes.

History: Five hundred years ago, during the Cataclysm, Dornman Port stood on the brink of destruction, and many knights died defending it; their graves lie beneath the city. The ruins are what remains of that fight against the Abyss.

In the present, the Knights have repeatedly searched the ruins after Winslow's Abyss alarms and found nothing. Honorary Knight status of the Traveler is invoked to persuade Winslow.

Dangers: Hydro and Electro slimes, and an Eye of the Storm that drops into the final cave. The old floors can give way.

Atmosphere: Dusty stone corridors and flashing lights, steady cold draughts, and quiet rows of worn tombstones that someone nonetheless keeps clean.

Quests: Winds Beneath the Tower of Silence is the world quest set here, which requires finishing Song of the Dragon and Freedom, and it begins at the Devil's Cut tavern in Dornman Port.

Status as of 7.1: The alarm is quiet, the graves are tended and the ruins are open as of 7.1.

106.comment: Knights of Favonius Ruins: Winslow and Odolf at the old lighthouse
106.content: Winslow is a nervous resident of the old lighthouse who fears Abyss and ghosts and wants the graves below moved. Odolf is a local who knows a secret route into the ruins and has been quietly protecting the graves. His ghost story is a deliberate fiction.

107.content:
Luyang Academy (also: Amidst the Ink-Tinged Mist): Luyang Academy is the part of the Temple of Space devoted to painting, built in the style of Liyue architecture. Though it is a gallery of paintings from many eras, the sages who first named it believed that books and paintings are one and the same, hence "academy". Under the Watcher Melanta's rule its artists were punished by being turned into ink blots or sealed in paintings. In 6.5 the Traveler, Paimon, Zeitlind and Dex freed them by restoring paintings into real space.

Death does not exist in the temple, so the sealed artists were alive in their paintings and could be released.

Geography: A Liyue-styled compound reached across a small island, with halls such as the Abode of Resplendent Talent, the Pavilion of Paintings and the Tower of Radiant Light. Its defining mechanic is the painting world: with Dex, the player can re-project paintings, entering them to complete missing parts of space, or fight ink blots in a top-down view. The area opens with the quest Long Live Life.

A dim star in ink hangs above the entrance. One door cannot be forced open, since Daozi explains it was manifested from a painting through the mind and is not physical matter as we know it; a painter must open it. Elite enemies are Domain Keepers and the Xuanwen Beast.

People: Daozi, a painter who coached Kanou in Liyue landscape painting, is freed first and guides the party. Kanou, Yoshitoshi and Bosch are painters later freed (Kanou says he never wants to paint another screen); Castiglione, Jinggui and Zhangsun Jijing are also listed there. Bosch and Daozi once taught Raumhilda to draw, and she named a painting "Long Live Life" before leaving it in the Academy.

Daozi says that realism makes the best cage for a spirit because its essence is read at a glance, so realistic paintings hide secrets. They admire the feat attributed to Rex Lapis of bringing stone to life, but Yu Huangyi told them a dragon like Azhdaha already existed in his era.

Culture: Artists sign commissions with secret signatures. They treat the mind as stronger than matter: Istoria's teacher Aristocles said so, and Daozi uses it to explain why a painted door resists a kick. The painters were somewhat unsettled by "Maukie"'s space-bending paintings but like him and use his nickname; Daozi says Melanta regards names as numbers assigned on arrival.

History: Created by Asmoday as a gallery for paintings. When she disappeared, Melanta sought to restore the temple to its original order and punished the Academy by turning its people into ink blots and sealing them in paintings; he also had "Maukie" exiled for defiling the laws of space. In 6.5, in Long Live Life, the party freed Daozi, then Kanou, Yoshitoshi and Bosch, and unrolled the great scroll by plucking the star in the Pavilion of Paintings.

Along the way the party meets a lone figure who says he is the painter Escher and offers to take them somewhere safe; he proves a fake, and ink floods in as the party flees through re-projected paintings, until a bridge painting collapses and drops them near the Tower of Radiant Light. Daozi blames Melanta, who works behind the scenes. In one painting Zeitlind finds photographs from her sister's Kamera, which she takes. Afterwards Bosch shows Zeitlind a painting her sister left, which Zeitlind chooses to leave in the Academy. Istoria later chats with the party outside about philosophy.

Dangers: Domain Keepers, ink blots (harmful to touch), the Xuanwen Beast, and the disorienting rules of painting-space.

Atmosphere: Mist and ink, silent halls in a Liyue style; paintings that could hide doors, cages or whole landscapes.

Status as of 7.1: As of 6.5 (and still at 7.1) the Academy is freed and its painters live there again.

The painters remain in the Temple of Space; Raumhilda's painting "Long Live Life" stays on display.

108.content: Raumhilda, who had spent time in the Academy, made a painting that Bosch thought neither mastery nor childlike innocence, only sadness. She said the canvas, once coloured, cannot become white again, and signed it with a secret signature. Her younger sister Zeitlind finds it, learns it is hers, and decides it should remain here in peace instead of being taken outside, where it might be lost within a hundred years.

109.content:
Mahavaipulya Chamber (also: Mahavaipulya Hall, Mahavaipulya Archives, The Moving Finger Writes): The Mahavaipulya Chamber is the Temple of Space's library, devoted to ancient texts and to the new novels written by some of its Uplifted residents. Its loading-screen text says it stores books from various eras. Because the residents' stories blurred history and fiction, the Watcher Melanta pressed them between the pages; in 6.5 the Traveler, Paimon, Zeitlind and Dex restored the library and freed them.

The name comes from the Sanskrit "Mahavaipulya", the great expansive sutras, an allusion the wiki ties to the Buddhist Avatamsaka tradition of infinite realms. The place can be called the Mahavaipulya Hall or Archives.

Geography: A library whose pages are doorways: with Dex the player can flip pages to open passages, fold them and ride floating pages to other places, revealing rooms in different styles (one is an Inazuma-style room). Restoration Cores hidden in these spaces must be gathered and inserted to restore the building. The area opens with the quest Counterfeit Classics.

Seelie wander the reading rooms. A large book called "Tale of the Lochknight Aerinny" is a retelling of the Remuria-era story "Erinnyes", and the party can enter it as a trial of rewriting its plot.

People: Yu Huangyi comes from the era when Shanhui Fort stood below Mt. Tianheng, before the Guili Assembly; Calcerius is a Remurian; Okikuni comes from the youkai age before the Narukami unified the archipelago. Istoria spoke highly of Calcerius's rewrite of "Erinnyes", saying it captured the moment realism collapsed into nominalism.

Yu Huangyi, who guides the party through the library, says besides the borderland newcomers all Remurians are made of rock; Calcerius, who lost his faith in Phobos in the Apathic Interval, corrects this as "ichorification". Okikuni was fascinated by Liyue novels and wished to join their adventures. The three joke that together they have the strength of an entry-level rookie soldier.

Culture: The Uplifted swapped stories and kept writing novels even after the Apathic Interval, and enjoyed Liyue novels written by later generations. Zeitlind says her favourite among the Yaksha was Alatus. Naming things is a game: the Restoration Core was named by Paimon after the residents' own jokes.

History: Created by Asmoday as an archive of books. After she vanished the Shades allowed small changes, and the Uplifted began writing novels that mingled fact and fiction. Melanta classified this as pollution and punished them by pressing them between pages. In 6.5, during Counterfeit Classics, the party freed the paper people, collected Restoration Cores, and restored the library, which broke Melanta's control over the area.

To retrieve the last core the Traveler and Paimon entered the retold "Aerinny", guided by Zeitlind's imagination to steer a tragedy toward a happy ending. Zeitlind also finds a chest of letters she and her sister exchanged.

Dangers: Domain Keepers, traps hidden in pages, and trap rooms. Floors may fall away when a Restoration Core is touched.

Atmosphere: Quiet rooms of shelves and oversized pages, with the chatter and jokes of the freed paper people.

Status as of 7.1: As of 6.5 (unchanged through 7.1) the library is restored and its residents free.

The residents remain in the Temple of Space and are friendly with visitors.

110.content: The Restoration Core is the device Paimon named for the objects Dex uses to unfold manipulated space back to its original form. Yu Huangyi says space manipulated leaves a residual trail of its reversal. Cores must be carried and inserted; some are in pieces hidden within pages.

111.content:
Midsummer Courtyard (also: Sommernachtgarten, Midsummer Courtyard domain): Midsummer Courtyard is a Domain of Blessing near Starsnatch Cliff in Starfell Valley, Mondstadt. Per its entrance text, when the ancient lost civilisation fell, the once magnificent Sommernachtgarten ("Summer Night Garden") was buried underground, leaving only ancient trees and stones to recall its glory. It is an ancient blessed altar full of monsters that fear Pyro, and clearing it rewards artifacts.

The name Sommernachtgarten is German for Summer Night Garden.

Geography: The entrance is by Starsnatch Cliff, a quiet spot in Starfell Valley. Inside lie sunken garden remains with old trees and stones.

Higher trial levels add an elemental node at the centre that empowers nearby foes with Cryo or Electro until reactions strip the buff.

History: Canon states only that the garden belonged to the lost ancient civilisation and was buried when it fell. No builder, date or event is named beyond that.

Dangers: Cryo and Hydro slimes, shielded Hilichurls, Abyss Mages, Electro slimes and Fatui Electro Cicin Mages. The ley line disorder punishes certain elemental reactions with a blast, so reaction choice matters.

Atmosphere: Overgrown stone beneath ancient trees, a once-lavish garden now silent underground.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the domain is open and unchanged since 1.0.

112.content:
Millhaven (also: Blossoms in Fragrant Bloom): Millhaven is a peaceful, tranquil village in Windrest Peak, in northern Mondstadt, known for its sweet-smelling flowers and fragrance products. It is an idyllic place of windmills and fields of the Windrest Flower. Its loading screen calls it a peaceful and tranquil town.

Windrest Flowers grow only in Millhaven's fields and are a key ingredient in perfume making. The village appeared with Windrest Peak in version 6.5.

Geography: Millhaven lies in Windrest Peak, near Dornman Port. It has windmills (one in the northeast), flower fields, a bulletin board and shops. Local specialties include Windrest Flower, calla lilies, dandelion seeds, Etherwing moths, Philanemo mushrooms and windwheel asters.

Windrest Flower is found only in the village's flower fields. A harpastum can be found here as an exploration object.

Places: Scents and Senses is the fragrance shop of Annick, who trades a Special Perfume: Wind's Breath for Windrest Flowers. Shattuck is run by Benthem. Estragon is a merchant.

A small signboard near Shattuck displays a notice by Prune, who signs as a Witch Hunter and accuses a witch codenamed "A". Replies from anonymous locals mock or redirect the notice, and the Traveler can tear it down (an open-world interactable).

People: Annick (perfumer), Estragon (merchant), Lilian (florist), Benthem (shop owner), Genna (Knight of Favonius), Leonore (veteran of the Combined Arms Company), Leopoldine, Tyutcheva and Uchida Kotaro live or work here.

Prune and Klee show up in open-world scenes: doodles of Dodoco on walls draw a remark from Prune about crayon that will not wash off, and Klee offers to blow the wall up.

Culture: Fragrance making is the village's trade. A folk tale from Dornman Port says the first Windrest Flower grew from the lyre of the Lord of the Wind, who healed snow-covered wounds in the age of white earth; the Church does not recognise it as a miracle. The Archive text adds that the real credit belongs to countless humble people whose names are forgotten.

A dish called Millhaven's Morning Plate was added to cooking in 6.5.

Atmosphere: Scented, gentle and slow; flower fields rolling under turning windmills, with children's mischief (doodles, notices) and squirrels to add humour.

Status as of 7.1: Peaceful and unchanged as of 7.1; no Millhaven content from 7.0-7.1 was found.

113.content: A fragrant, delicate flower found only in Millhaven's fields (24 can be found every two days in game). Five can be traded to Annick for Special Perfume: Wind's Breath. Dornman Port folklore credits its origin to the lyre of Venti.

114.content:
Mona's Laboratory: Mona's Laboratory is a house at the southern end of Mondstadt City, a little past Schulz's Blacksmith. Goth owns it and Mona, the astrologist, rents it. For most of the game its door is shut.

Before the quest Beyond This World's Stars is completed, a Hydro seal blocks the door. The prompt reads that the door seems locked by a curious seal and wonders whose place it is.

Places: One house with a door the player can only examine or speak through.

The house becomes interactable again during the quest Owe Mora, Pay Mora.

People: Goth, a landlord who also runs the Goth Grand Hotel, owns the property. Mona rents it. During the quest the Traveler can talk to Mona through the door.

Goth says someone had put a Hydro seal over the house and he could not lease it. Mona broke the seal and moved in, and Goth let her rent it at the lowest possible price.

History: The seal predates the quest. Canon does not say who placed it.

After the quest ends and the player leaves the area, the house is no longer interactable.

Atmosphere: A shut door in a quiet southern lane, with a faint magical seal and the sense of someone busy inside.

Travel: Go to the southern end of Mondstadt City, beyond Schulz's Blacksmith.

Status as of 7.1: Nothing after the quests is recorded; the door stays closed to the player outside them.

115.content:
Mondstadt (also: Mond, City of Freedom): Mondstadt is the nation of freedom in northeastern Teyvat, the land of the Anemo Archon Barbatos, who walks among his people unrecognised as the bard Venti and deliberately does not rule. The Knights of Favonius govern in practice; the Church of Favonius tends worship. The capital, Mondstadt City, sits on an island in Cider Lake amid windmills and rolling green country. Mondstadters are easygoing lovers of taverns, song and festivals, proud of the gifts they credit to their god: dandelions, flight (gliding) and wine.

Barbatos stays out of government so that he never becomes a tyrant like the god before him. Neighbours in Liyue often mock Mondstadt as a city "without rule" whose god abandoned it.

Geography: Green, windy country of lakes, oak forests and plains. Areas: Starfell Valley (the capital, Cider Lake), Galesong Hill (Windrise's great oak), Windwail Highland (Springvale, Dawn Winery, Wolvendom), Brightcrown Mountains (ruined Old Mondstadt, Stormterror's Lair), snowbound Dragonspine, and northern Windrest Peak (Dornman Port).

Starfell Valley also holds Whispering Woods, Starfell Lake, the Thousand Winds Temple and Stormbearer Point; Galesong Hill holds Falcon Coast and Cape Oath. The weather in Windrest Peak is clearer and more varied than in the south. Dragonspine is the great exception to the mild climate: snow gathers there and never melts, and its cold can kill.

Government: No king rules.
