The Knights of Favonius, founded by Vennessa about 1,000 years ago so aristocrats would never rule again, are police, garrison, lawmakers and civil service, led by Grand Master Varka (Knight of Boreas) with Jean Gunnhildr (Dandelion Knight) as Acting Grand Master and ten company Captains. The Church of Favonius is separate but managed by the Knights; its Seneschal is Seamus Pegg, Cardinal of Daybreak.

Most trials are held by either the Knights or the Church alone; grave cases may require both, as when Albedo was tried in closed session with a deacon as assessor. Knighthood is earned by passing written and practical examinations, not conferred by royalty. Companies: 1st General Affairs, 2nd Garrison (Note), 3rd Vanguard (Skeiron), 4th Reconnaissance (Eula), 5th Ranged (Vice Captain Lohen; bows and muskets), 6th Logistics (Hertha), 7th Combined Arms (Frederica Gunnhildr), 8th Support (inventions), 9th Cavalry (Kaeya) and 10th Investigation (Albedo, Chief Alchemist). Also: Amber, the last Outrider; Lisa, Librarian; Klee, Spark Knight; Noelle, maid and aspiring knight; the Traveler, Honorary Knight.

Religion: Worship of Barbatos is light and festive rather than doctrinal, centred on the Favonius Cathedral behind the giant Anemo Archon statue. Hardly anyone knows the tipsy bard Venti is their god; his irreverent songs about Barbatos get called blasphemy. The deacon Dahlia serves as the Herald of Barbatos and is one of the few who know Venti's true identity. Deaconess Barbara Pegg is the city's singing "idol".

Statues of the Seven dot the countryside, one beneath the great oak at Windrise. Older faiths left traces. The ancient Arcadians worshipped the Three Moons, above all the Frost Moon under the name Prusmene, and built the Thousand Winds Temple for Istaroth; after Barbatos' rise it was rebuilt to honour both gods until Istaroth was forgotten. For about five hundred years after Vennessa, Mondstadt also venerated the Four Winds and built temples to them, but that worship faded after the cataclysm.

Economy: Wine is Mondstadt's signature trade. The Dawn Winery, owned by the Ragnvindr family for about a thousand years and now by Diluc, is the chief winery and specialises in dandelion wine; part of each year's output is sold at home and the rest goes out along the trade route south of the city. Elzer has handled the winery's affairs since Crepus' death and chairs the Mondstadt Wine Guild; Adelinde is its head housemaid. Farming, orchards and hunting (Springvale) support the countryside, and the Adventurers' Guild posts work for freelance adventurers. In the north, Dornman Port is one of the continent's major trade hubs, known for cargo shipping and flower cultivation, while Millhaven's windrest-flower fields supply a fragrance trade.

History: About 2,600 years ago the people of Decarabian, God of Storms, rose against his wind-walled city (Old Mondstadt); a wind spirit among the rebels became Barbatos, cleared the snow, founded the new city and withdrew. The noble clans after him turned tyrannical until about 1,000 years ago the gladiator Vennessa, aided by Barbatos, overthrew them and founded the Knights. Five hundred years ago the dragon Durin ravaged Mondstadt until Barbatos and Dvalin slew it. In the Prologue the Traveler and Venti freed Dvalin ("Stormterror") from the Abyss Order, and the Fatui Harbinger Signora took Venti's Anemo Gnosis.

Decarabian walled his city against the blizzards of Boreas, the northern wolf-god; the rebels' code word "Windblume" became a festival. The Lawrence Clan led the aristocracy's decline. Four years ago Crepus Ragnvindr died fending off an attack by "Ursa the Drake" on his caravan, engineered by the traitorous Inspector Eroch and the Fatui, and the cover-up led Diluc to quit the Knights. Half a year before the Traveler arrived, Varka led the Knights' elite north on an expedition that ended in Nod-Krai. At a recent Windblume Festival (5.6) Albedo's staged trial exposed creatures born of Durin's lingering life force, and Durin was reborn as a human; Varka came home after the Nod-Krai crisis (6.4).

Customs: Festivals: spring's Windblume Festival (flowers and gifts for Barbatos and loved ones; a Windblume Star makes the formal offering), Ludi Harpastum (fifteen days of games, song and wine) and autumn's Weinlesefest (new wine uncasked for the Archon). Gliding is a national pastime.

In Mondstadt a rose means a kept secret ("as wine bottles are corked, so too are my lips sealed"), not love. Nobody agrees what flower the windblume really is: Dandelionites say the dandelion (and a lovers' festival), Asterists the windwheel aster (and a remembrance of liberation from Decarabian); Barbatos lets everyone choose their own. During Ludi Harpastum the champion chooses a maiden who throws the harpastum, a ball wrapped in red cloth, into the crowd, and whoever catches it is blessed with a year of fortune. At Weinlesefest new wine stays sealed until Windcoming Day; if the Archon is pleased, a gentle breeze blesses the people. Springvale's young hunters looking for love catch foxes in Wolvendom during Windblume and release them crowned with flower wreaths. The Gunnhildr motto is "For Mondstadt, as always."

Foreign relations: Liyue: close trade partner; Liyue folk tease Mondstadt as godless and lawless, not knowing why its Archon refuses to rule. Snezhnaya: a Fatui diplomatic mission operates in the city and has repeatedly abused its position; the Fatui's role in Ursa the Drake's attack and Dottore's slaying of the beast left Mondstadt indebted to them, Signora seized the Anemo Gnosis, and a Lawrence, Schubert, once plotted with the Fatui to restore aristocratic rule. Nod-Krai: the Knights keep an outpost there, Favonius Keep, from which they fought the Wild Hunt. Sumeru: Mondstadters such as Lisa study at the Akademiya. Natlan: Vennessa was a Muratan from the southern plains. Inazuma's closed borders once stranded Mondstadt sailors.

Dangers: Hilichurl camps, slimes and wandering Ruin Machines; Treasure Hoarders; the Abyss Order, which manipulated Dvalin and has smuggled cargo through Dornman Port; Fatui schemes; the killing cold of Dragonspine; the wolf pack of Wolvendom, which even fearless hunters avoid; and old ruins such as Stormterror's Lair. Recent threats came from Durin's remains in Dragonspine and from Wild Hunt corruption that followed the ley lines into Wolvendom.

Atmosphere: Constant breezes, dandelion seeds on the air, half-timbered houses and windmills, bards in the squares, knights on patrol, and wine-scented evenings at the tavern. Mondstadt City has a famously relaxed pace; Windrest Peak's port is busier, more cosmopolitan and full of sailors and merchants.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Mondstadt is at peace. Grand Master Varka has returned from the long expedition to Nod-Krai but still travels to the Knights' outpost there, so Jean remains Acting Grand Master. Venti no longer holds his Gnosis.

Varka came home in 6.4; the outpost is Favonius Keep. Seamus Pegg is back too. Signora took the Gnosis for the Tsaritsa; as of 6.6 it is counted among the Gnoses in the Fatui's possession. Durin, a storybook dragon reborn in a human body, lives in Mondstadt. Windrest Peak in the north opened in 6.5. The Archon Quest has moved to Snezhnaya (Chapter VII, 7.0-7.1), and no new crisis in Mondstadt is shown there.

116.comment: Mondstadt: Starfell Valley and Cider Lake
116.content:
Starfell Valley is Mondstadt's most varied area, from Stormbearer Point to the Whispering Woods, and the heart of the Knights' patrols. Mondstadt City (the "Crown of the North") stands on a large island in Cider Lake behind a stone wall, reached by a long bridge, with cobbled streets, windmills, the Knights of Favonius Headquarters and its library, and the Favonius Cathedral behind the Anemo Archon statue. Starsnatch Cliff is a quiet spot where Venti has met the Traveler. The ruined Thousand Winds Temple, built by ancient Arcadians for Istaroth, was later rebuilt for both Istaroth and Barbatos; a Ruin Guard still lurks there.

The Mondstadt Library, which Ragnvindr converted from an aristocrats' bathhouse after Vennessa's rebellion, grew into the largest library in northern Teyvat; the Great Fire of Fall Equinox reduced it to one-sixth of its former size, yet it is still the largest in the north. The Temple of the Wolf, once a training ground, lies near the Thousand Winds Temple.

117.content: In Galesong Hill, Windrise is a breezy plain where a giant oak is said to have grown on the spot where Vennessa ascended to Celestia; a Statue of the Seven stands beneath it, and travelers resting in its shade have heard a young bard singing tales of Barbatos. The Temple of the Falcon stands between the city and the oak, the Temple of the Lion on Falcon Coast, and Cape Oath is a favourite spot for Windblume couples.

118.comment: Mondstadt: Windwail Highland, Springvale and Wolvendom
118.content: Windwail Highland is Mondstadt's rustic heart of clear springs, orchards and forests. Springvale is a hunting village built over a spring that, by legend, a "Spring Fairy" (an Oceanid from Fontaine) filled with life-saving water. The Dawn Winery, the Ragnvindr family estate and Mondstadt's chief winery, stands nearby. Wolvendom, a dark, silent forest, is home to Boreas (Andrius), the Wolf of the North, and his pack; locals avoid it, though the wolf-raised boy Razor lives there.

119.comment: Mondstadt: Brightcrown Mountains and Stormterror's Lair
119.content: The Brightcrown Mountains in the northwest hold the ruins of Old Mondstadt, Decarabian's walled city, and his broken tower. Dvalin slept there for centuries after the cataclysm, and during the Prologue it was "Stormterror's Lair", sealed by a barrier until Venti dispelled it. Ruins and wind currents make it hazardous.

120.content:
Dragonspine is a snow-locked mountain whose snow never melts; its cold is deadly without warmth or the dragon-blood crystals called Scarlet Quartz. Long ago, as Vindagnyr, it was a green mountain where refugees founded Sal Vindagnyr; the Skyfrost Nail fell from the sky, burying the kingdom in snow, and a fragment turned its great tree into the Frostbearing Tree. Five hundred years ago the dragon Durin fell dead here; his blood seeped into the mountain and his heart still beat in Wyrmrest Valley (Durin's Core). Albedo keeps an alchemy camp on the slopes.

Imunlaukr, an outlander living in Sal Vindagnyr, was away seeking a branch of Irminsul when its people perished; he is the namesake of the Imunlaukr Clan, one of Mondstadt's founding clans. About 1,000 years ago an aristocratic expedition organised by Landrich came to grief on the mountain amid a murderous plot by Eberhart. Since Albedo drained Durin's Core during Paralogism, the core has gone inert.

121.comment: Mondstadt: Windrest Peak and Dornman Port
121.content:
Windrest Peak, Mondstadt's northernmost area (opened in 6.5), centres on Dornman Port, a bustling port north of Cider Lake that is one of the continent's major trade hubs. In the aristocratic era it was the Gunnhildr Clan's fief and held Mondstadt's very first sanctuary to Barbatos, but the port has had no church since the late aristocratic era, when the Gunnhildrs, breaking with the tyrannical Imunlaukr Clan, threw a bishop sent from the capital out of the sanctuary's high tower and tore it down. Millhaven is an idyllic windmill town of windrest-flower fields and fragrance makers. The Knights keep a base at the port, with members of the Ranged, Logistics, Support and Combined Arms companies; Vice Captain Lohen has been stationed there.

Five hundred years ago Dornman Port was a front line against the Abyss and nearly fell; the knights who died defending it lie in catacombs beneath the city (the Knights of Favonius Ruins under the old lighthouse). Long before, the Arcadian city-state of Elysium stood in these mountains under Gunnhildr control. The Old Sanatorium Site, a sanatorium demolished a few years ago, was built atop ruins left when the Temple of Space was lifted into the sky; Asmoday transformed the floating temple into "Segment-Domain Tau" (explored in the world quest series "A Long Day in the Mountains").

122.comment: Mondstadt: Decarabian and the First Liberation
122.content:
Decarabian, God of Storms, ruled Old Mondstadt from his tower and walled it in gales against the blizzards of Boreas. He believed his rule loving and orderly, assigning every home and banning tunes that might signal dissent, but his people felt imprisoned. Around 2,600 years ago they rose under the code word Windblume, led by the Nameless Bard, a wind spirit, Amos, Gunnhildr and a red-haired warrior. Decarabian was slain; Amos and the Nameless Bard died too. The wind spirit ascended as the Anemo Archon, took the dead bard's form and name (Venti), blew away the snow, flattened Pilos Peak into what is now Musk Reef, and led the people to found the new city on Cider Lake before departing.

Boreas judged himself unfit to be the Anemo Archon and withdrew north to Nod-Krai to sleep; when he later returned to Mondstadt, realising his blizzards could only take life, he let his body die and his power flow into the ley lines of the land; his spirit lingers. The red-haired warrior turned away from Barbatos and was forgotten, though his line became the Ragnvindrs. Before the rebellion the Gunnhildr Clan had left Decarabian's city; a weak wind spirit answered their prayers, and their faith strengthened him. Gunnhildr crowned the new Archon with laurels. The Nameless Bard's last song drew on a melody belonging to Istaroth, which is why he could not survive it.

123.comment: Mondstadt: The Aristocracy and Vennessa's Rebellion
123.content:
After Barbatos left, noble clans descended from the founders' heroes (chiefly Lawrence, Gunnhildr and Imunlaukr) led Mondstadt, at first for the people's good. From about 1,600 years ago the Lawrence Clan dominated and degenerated into tyranny: slavery, gladiatorial bloodsport, suppressed history, a knight order serving the nobles and a Church split in their favour. About 1,000 years ago Vennessa, a Muratan exiled from Natlan and enslaved as a gladiator, fought for her people's freedom; Barbatos, awakened by the people's cries, revealed himself at her final battle against Ursa the Drake. The nobles were exiled (the Gunnhildrs, who kept faith, stayed), Vennessa founded the Knights of Favonius and restored the Church, and later ascended to Celestia at Windrise.

Official histories stop there, but Barbatos also forged a treaty "proving" the aristocrats had sold Mondstadt, troops included, to Morax; their soldiers turned on them, and scholars only discovered the forgery long afterwards. Ragnvindr, the disowned Lawrence Kreuzlied and Church faithful aided the revolt. Afterwards the Gunnhildrs pushed to abolish hereditary fiefs. Today Lawrence descendants still face hostility, which Eula, a captain of the Knights, endures; the Imunlaukr bloodline is lost.

124.content: Five hundred years ago Grand Master Arundolyn, the "Lion of Light", and his friend Rostam, the "Wolf Pup", led the Knights against the monsters pouring from Khaenri'ah; Rostam died and Arundolyn laid down his sword. Rhinedottir's dragon Durin then ravaged Mondstadt with no Lionfang Knight to stop it, until Barbatos called on Dvalin and they killed it together. Dvalin swallowed Durin's Abyss-tainted blood and retreated into a centuries-long sleep in Decarabian's tower. Rostam's lover Rosalyne-Kruzchka Lohefalter, returning from the Akademiya, turned herself into living flame for vengeance as the Crimson Witch of Flames; Pierro later recruited her into the Fatui as the Harbinger Signora. Afterwards worship of the Four Winds faded.

125.content: The Four Winds are the guardians Barbatos entrusted with Mondstadt, formally established after Vennessa's revolution. Dragon of the East: Dvalin. Wolf of the North: Boreas (Andrius), and in Knights' tradition the Knight of Boreas, currently Varka (earlier the Wandering Knight, Ravenwood and Rostam). Lion of the South: passed to Grand Masters or Acting Grand Masters as the Dandelion (Lionfang) Knight, now Jean. Falcon of the West: Vennessa after her ascension, though the Knights are sometimes called the Falcon collectively. Venti's ballad credits the four winds, not himself, with Mondstadt's seasons. Their symbols mark the city's four sides.

126.content: When the Traveler arrived, the dragon "Stormterror" was raging over Mondstadt. He was Dvalin, the Dragon of the East, poisoned by Durin's blood and manipulated by the Abyss Order into believing Mondstadt had abandoned him. Venti and the Traveler spirited the Holy Lyre der Himmel out of the Cathedral, purified Dvalin's tears, and confronted him in Stormterror's Lair with Jean and Diluc, freeing him from the Abyss's hold. Immediately afterwards, the Fatui Harbinger Signora ambushed Venti outside the Cathedral and ripped out his Anemo Gnosis.

127.comment: Mondstadt: The Varka Expedition and Homecoming
127.content: Half a year before the Traveler arrived, Grand Master Varka took about eighty percent of the Knights' strength, including the cavalry, Seamus Pegg, Frederica Gunnhildr and Mika, on a long expedition against an Abyssal calamity he foresaw in the north. It ended in Nod-Krai, where the Knights fought the Wild Hunt from Favonius Keep until its master Rerir was defeated. Varka then sent Vice Captain Lohen home with ten letters. Wild Hunt corruption reached Wolvendom through the ley lines, while in Nod-Krai an abyssal copy of Roland, Rostam's long-lost disciple the "White Knight", corrupted the remains of the half of Andrius' soul that had stayed there. With Boreas and Razor guarding Wolvendom and Dvalin ferrying the Traveler north, Varka gathered the scattered wolf-spirit fragments, let Andrius return to the ley lines, survived being swallowed by the abyssal wolf, and woke at Windrise among his friends. Before he left, he had told Jean she would become Grand Master if he did not return.

128.comment: Mondstadt: The Windblume Trial and Durin's Rebirth
128.content: At a recent Windblume Festival, Albedo was tried behind closed doors for murder and was found guilty: a trap planned for half a year to expose beings spawned from the dead dragon Durin's life force, which devoured and impersonated Mondstadters (including a false Hertha). The retrial unmasked them and a full assault on the city followed, repelled by the Knights, Diluc, the Church and the Traveler while Venti linked defenders with wind currents. Albedo convened the Tripartite Conference (Knights and Church, the Anemo Archon, the Hexenzirkel), won reagents from Alice and Barbeloth, drew the vital energy from Durin's Core and, with Venti as Windblume Star singing, transmuted Mini Durin, a kindly dragon from the storybook world Simulanka, into a synthetic human body that took the fallen dragon's place.

129.content:
Mondstadt City (also: City of Mondstadt, Crown of the North, City of Wind, City of Bards, City of Pastorals): Mondstadt City, the "City of Wind" and capital of Mondstadt, stands on a large island in Cider Lake in western Starfell Valley, ringed by a stone wall and reached by a long bridge. Cobbled streets climb past windmills and half-timbered houses to a plaza where a giant statue of the Anemo Archon Barbatos stands before the Favonius Cathedral. The Knights of Favonius govern from their headquarters here; the city is known for its relaxed pace, bards, festivals and taverns.

Also called the City of Mondstadt and the "Crown of the North"; Signora sneered at it as the "City of Bards" and Albedo has called it the "City of Pastorals". The god it worships, Venti, wanders its streets unrecognised as a tipsy bard.

Geography: The city fills a large island in western Cider Lake. A stone wall encloses its lower, eastern end, where the main gate opens onto the bridge; the ground rises through market streets and a fountain plaza to the high ground of the statue, Cathedral and Knights' headquarters.

Cider Lake is clear, never freezes, and is credited with the fame of Mondstadt's ciders and wines. Besides the main gate there are side and southern gates. Windmills stand within the walls (a windmill keeper, Michelle, tends the northern and western mills). A small park lies south of the Knights' headquarters. Starsnatch Cliff, a quiet lookout where Venti likes to meet the Traveler, is a short walk outside the city in Starfell Valley.

Places: Anemo Archon Statue and Favonius Cathedral (the Church's seat) on the upper plaza; Knights of Favonius Headquarters with the Mondstadt Library; the taverns Angel's Share (Dawn Winery, owned by Diluc) and The Cat's Tail (Margaret's, with bartender Diona); the Market District with Good Hunter and the Adventurers' Guild post; and the Goth Grand Hotel, taken over by the Fatui delegation.

Further sites: Floral Whisper (Flora's flower stall), Mondstadt General Goods (Blanche), With Wind Comes Glory (Marjorie), Wagner's smithy (Schulz's Blacksmith) at the south end, and Mona's Laboratory, a sealed house just beyond the smithy that Mona now rents. A door in the lower library of the headquarters leads to the lobby of the Imaginarium Theater.

People: Knights, clergy, merchants and bards fill the streets. Notable residents and regulars include Acting Grand Master Jean, Grand Master Varka (home from Nod-Krai), Captains Kaeya and Albedo, Librarian Lisa, Outrider Amber, the deaconess and singer Barbara, the deacon Dahlia, Klee, Diluc of the Dawn Winery, the astrologist Mona, and Durin, who lives in the city since his rebirth as a human. Everyday faces: Katheryne, receptionist at the Adventurers' Guild, and Cyrus, its branch master; Charles, bartender at Angel's Share; Margaret, owner of The Cat's Tail; Sara, waitress at Good Hunter; the blacksmith Wagner and his apprentice Schulz; Flora the florist; Timaeus, an alchemy scholar; Ella Musk, who studies the hilichurl language in the library; Hertha, a Knights coordinator; Ludwig Goth, the hotelier and landlord; nuns such as Victoria, Jilliana and Grace; and street bards including Six-Fingered José, Helen and Sansa. A Fatui diplomatic staff (Lyudmila, Mikhail and Viktor among them) works openly in the city, with the guard Luke posted outside the Goth Grand Hotel.

Governance: There is no monarch or city council separate from the nation: the Knights of Favonius police, garrison and administer the city from their headquarters, and the Church of Favonius, managed by the Knights, runs the Cathedral. Trials are normally held by either the Knights or the Church; grave cases can require both. The Grand Master's Office in the headquarters is Jean's workplace as Acting Grand Master. The building also holds a ground-floor solitary confinement room, used almost exclusively for Klee. Visitors, not only Mondstadters, may borrow from the library.

Culture: City life centres on taverns, song and festivals (Windblume, Ludi Harpastum, Weinlesefest), which decorate the streets and statue plaza.

Amber calls Sticky Honey Roast a traditional Mondstadt delicacy. Gliding is a point of local pride; Amber gives the Traveler a wind glider on their first visit. Wine culture is everywhere. Angel's Share takes its name from brewers' slang for the portion of liquor lost to evaporation and the barrels. It long held a near monopoly on the city's drinking, until Diona's cocktails, which taste good whatever goes into them, made The Cat's Tail a real rival; Angel's Share still sells more. The Cat's Tail is also where Mondstadt plays the card game Genius Invokation TCG. Good Hunter, the most popular restaurant in town, buys meat from Springvale hunters and prides itself on local apples.

History: About 2,600 years ago, after Decarabian's fall, Barbatos led the people from Old Mondstadt to Cider Lake, where they built the present city. In the early aristocratic era Venerare of the Lawrence Clan raised the Barbatos statue before the Cathedral, inscribed by the clan leaders with a pledge to defend Mondstadt; the late, tyrannical aristocracy pulled it down. After Vennessa's rebellion (about 1,000 years ago) the statue was restored without its original inscription.

Ragnvindr then turned the aristocrats' indoor bathhouse into the Mondstadt Library. The library grew into the largest in northern Teyvat until the Great Fire of Fall Equinox cut it to one-sixth of its size; it remains the largest in the north, and its restricted section behind the poplar doors in the basement survived untouched. In the Prologue (1.0) the dragon Stormterror attacked the city on the Traveler's first day there; after Dvalin was freed, Signora took Venti's Gnosis outside the Cathedral. In the Windblume Festival of the Paralogism crisis (5.6) monsters born of Durin's remains assaulted the city.

Atmosphere: Constant breezes turning windmills, dandelion seeds on the air, bards at the plaza, knights on patrol, and wine-scented evenings in the taverns. The pace is famously unhurried; one shop door even carries a note saying it is closed because friends came for a drink.

During Stormterror's attacks the streets emptied, though Amber noted that the tavern by the wall did better business than ever.

Dangers: Inside the walls the city is normally safe and well policed. Real threats have come from outside or in disguise: Stormterror's attacks in the Prologue, Fatui intrigue around the diplomatic mission, and, during Paralogism, Durin-born impostors who took the identities of residents before monsters stormed the gates.

Travel: The long bridge from the main gate links the city to the roads of Starfell Valley: toward Windrise and the Dawn Winery to the south and west, Springvale and Windwail Highland beyond, and the northern trade road that the Knights patrol to Dornman Port. Wind currents and gliding from the high ground are a quick way down; the Traveler's first glider lesson was on the city's heights.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the city is at peace. Jean still works as Acting Grand Master from the headquarters, Grand Master Varka is home from the Nod-Krai expedition, and Durin now lives in Mondstadt. The Archon Quest has moved to Snezhnaya, and no new crisis in the city is shown.

The Fatui diplomatic mission still occupies the Goth Grand Hotel. Venti no longer holds his Anemo Gnosis.

130.comment: Mondstadt City: Favonius Cathedral and the Anemo Archon Statue
130.content:
The Gothic Favonius Cathedral, seat of the Church of Favonius, stands at the top of Mondstadt City behind the giant statue of Barbatos, whose hooded, winged figure cups its hands over the plaza. The deaconess Barbara serves here and nuns such as Victoria tend daily worship. The Holy Lyre der Himmel was kept under guard in the Cathedral basement until Venti and the Traveler took it during the Stormterror crisis.

The statue was first raised by Venerare of the Lawrence Clan to commemorate Barbatos' descent, with a pledge by the clan leaders carved beneath it; the late aristocracy tore it down and it was restored after Vennessa's rebellion without the lost inscription. Its pedestal now reads "The Gateway of Celestia". Signora seized Venti's Gnosis outside the Cathedral after Dvalin was freed, and in Chapter I Act IV the Traveler came here to ask the Church about an Abyss Order plan.

131.comment: Mondstadt City: Knights of Favonius Headquarters and the Mondstadt Library
131.content:
The headquarters on the city's high ground holds the Grand Master's Office (Jean's workplace), Albedo's office as Chief Alchemist, a solitary confinement room used almost only for Klee, and the Mondstadt Library, kept by Lisa. Ragnvindr converted the library from an aristocrats' bathhouse after Vennessa's rebellion; it was the largest library in northern Teyvat until the Great Fire of Fall Equinox reduced it to a sixth of its size, and it is still the largest in the north.

Its restricted section lies behind poplar doors in the basement and survived the fire. Anyone, Mondstadter or not, may borrow books, and with the proper paperwork a whole set can be checked out for a year or more. Lisa offered to teach Durin to read, and in Durin's story quest unlisted restricted books that seemed to move between shelves led him and the Traveler into Andersdotter's unfinished storybook.

132.comment: Mondstadt City: Angel's Share and The Cat's Tail
132.content:
Mondstadt City's two great taverns. Angel's Share, established and funded by the Dawn Winery and owned by Diluc, stands near the city gate with Charles behind the bar. The Cat's Tail, owned by Margaret, is famed for its cats and for its bartender Diona, whose drinks taste delicious whatever she puts in them, though praising her skill is unwise. Diona's arrival broke Angel's Share's monopoly, and Elzer of the Dawn Winery was bitten when he tried to poach her.

Angel's Share is named for the brewers' term for liquor lost to evaporation and does not give credit. The Cat's Tail, between the Adventurers' Guild post and Good Hunter, is the city's gathering place for Genius Invokation TCG players.

133.content:
The lower end of Mondstadt City, inside the gate, is a market of two-storey tan-walled, red-roofed shops: Good Hunter (Sara's restaurant, the most popular eatery in town, with take-out always in demand), Katheryne's Adventurers' Guild post, Flora's Floral Whisper, Blanche's Mondstadt General Goods, Marjorie's With Wind Comes Glory, and Wagner's forge with his apprentice Schulz.

Good Hunter sources meat from Springvale's hunters and boasts of Mondstadt apples. Mona's Laboratory, a house owned by the hotelier Goth that had been locked behind a mysterious Hydro seal, sits just beyond the smithy; Mona broke the seal and Goth rented it to her at his lowest rate.

134.comment: Mondstadt City: Goth Grand Hotel and the Fatui Delegation
134.content: The Goth Grand Hotel belongs to Ludwig Goth, whose family has long served Mondstadt in hospitality. Before the Traveler arrived, Goth accepted a large sum from the Harbinger Pantalone to rent the whole hotel to the Fatui indefinitely, so a guard, Luke, now turns away everyone else. In the Prologue the Traveler found Jean outside the hotel rebuffing the Fatui diplomat Anastasia, who offered to have the Fatui "put an end" to Stormterror; Jean refused to hear talk of killing one of the Four Winds.

135.comment: Mondstadt City: Stormterror over Mondstadt City
135.content: On the Traveler's first day in the city, Stormterror (Dvalin) descended on Mondstadt City, darkening the sky and whipping up tornadoes around the walls. The Traveler was caught up and drove the dragon off in an aerial fight, kept aloft by a mysterious voice (Venti) commanding the winds, and then met Kaeya on landing. The attacks had already emptied the city's usual crowds. The crisis ended with Dvalin freed from the Abyss Order's hold, after which Signora took Venti's Gnosis outside the Cathedral.

136.comment: Mondstadt City: The Windblume Assault on the City
136.content: During a Windblume Festival (Interlude Chapter Act IV, "Paralogism") several residents behaved oddly, and Albedo was tried behind closed doors at the headquarters and found guilty of murder. The trial was a trap planned for half a year: creatures born of Durin's lingering life force had devoured and impersonated Mondstadters, including a false Hertha. Exposed, they launched a full assault, storming the main and side gates and fighting through the city centre, the residential streets, Angel's Share, the plaza, the Goth Grand Hotel and the windmill, with Ruin Machines striking at the side gate. Knights, Diluc, Kaeya, the Church, adventurers and residents defended their homes while Venti, feigning helplessness, linked them with long-distance wind currents. When Venti sensed a "child's anger" in the winds nearby, Phonia, missing for over half a year, came forward and Jean had her taken into custody; Albedo assured Jean he could save her. Two days later Venti, as Windblume Star, sang while Albedo transmuted Mini Durin into a human body to take the fallen dragon's place.

137.content:
Mondstadt General Goods: Mondstadt General Goods is a small shop in the market district of Mondstadt City, run by Blanche. It sells cooking ingredients and is open at all hours. An order board stands beside it.

Blanche says that despite its size the shop has the largest catalogue and the fastest shipping in Mondstadt, because it keeps a warehouse in Liyue Harbor.

Places: The shop itself, and the Mondstadt General Goods Order Board next to it, where customers pin slips with the wares they want and wait for a clerk's reply.

Stock is basic: salt, pepper, onion, milk, tomato, cabbage, potato and wheat, refreshed daily.

People: Blanche is the shopkeeper. She greets customers with quality goods at honest prices and has her own Genius Invokation TCG challenge for players.

When asked about Mondstadt she says it is known for wine and that most people head to a tavern after work.

Culture: The order board replies politely in a formal shop voice: requests that cannot be met get a standard apology. It refuses an order for a deliberately revolting dish, since the shop will not demean Mondstadt's hospitality, and cannot supply hair-loss medicine or books not yet published.

Other replies include sending someone who wants Chicken-Mushroom Skewers to Good Hunter across the street, a note that a rare history book is hard to find, and a stern reply to a customer who wondered whether the shop inspired the magical shop in a storybook.

Atmosphere: Brisk and businesslike, with an eager shopkeeper and a board full of slightly absurd customer requests.

Travel: Market district of Mondstadt City, across from Good Hunter.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

138.content:
Mondstadt Market District: The Mondstadt Market District is the shopping quarter at the lower end of Mondstadt City. Its two-storey buildings have tan walls and red-tiled roofs and house shops, a tavern and the stalls of merchants and craftsmen.

It occupies the lower end of the city, where locals buy everyday goods and the city's craftspeople work.

Places: Named businesses include Mondstadt General Goods (Blanche), Floral Whisper (owner Flora), Cat's Tail tavern (boss Margaret), With Wind Comes Glory (owner Marjorie), the Good Hunter (waitress Sara), a blacksmith (Wagner, with apprentice Schulz) and a jeweller (Shiliu). The city also has notice boards, among them the Cat's Tail Message Board, Good Hunter's Daily Recommendation and the Mondstadt General Goods Order Board.

Timaeus is a scholar of alchemy; Helen is a bard; Stanley, an adventurer, sits outside the bar by day. Knights Bruce, Huffman and Miles are seen here, with Hertha, coordinator of the Knights of Favonius, and Katheryne, receptionist of the Adventurers' Guild.

People: Shopkeepers, craftsmen and shoppers fill the streets by day, with extras such as Anna, Anthony, Beatrice and Donna in the crowd.

Flora's elder sister Chloris sells flowers and berries at Windrise instead. Xi'er is listed as a gourmet in the district.

Atmosphere: Busy daytime shopfronts, shoppers and craftsmen at work, with bards and knights passing through.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 unchanged.

139.comment: Mondstadt Market District: Mondstadt Market District Shops
139.content: Floral Whisper (Flora), Mondstadt General Goods (Blanche), With Wind Comes Glory (Marjorie) and the Good Hunter (Sara) are among the market's named shops.

140.content:
Mural Room: The Mural Room is a hidden chamber on Dragonspine that holds frescoes painted by the Princess of Sal Vindagnyr. A claymore, the Snow-Tombed Starsilver, stands stuck in a platform at its centre. It preserves the kingdom's image from before the snow and the outlander Imunlaukr's farewell.

The room's name is unofficial. It opens only after the hidden exploration objective Dragonspine's Glacial Secret is completed.

Geography: A cave southwest of Dragonspine's Statue of The Seven, behind a sealed door near the Entombed City - Ancient Palace. The Starsilver is stuck in the platform in the middle of the room, with the frescoes around it.

The door opens after Dragonspine's Glacial Secret, a follow-up to the objective Dragonspine's Last Trio. It requires activating numbered Ancient Carvings across the mountain, found for example south of the statue, atop Starglow Cavern, south of Wyrmrest Valley, before the Peak of Vindagnyr domain, under the Ancient Rime in the southwestern ruins, and in a cavern below the Cryo Hypostasis arena. One carving is inside the secret room.

Places: Two distinct frescoes survive; a third is a copy. The first is divided in two. Its right half shows a green mountain (Vindagnyr), an angel pointing skyward and a floating island above, with a Latin line roughly meaning "Listen and be silent, if you wish to learn". Its left half shows one large figure with a shining symbol over its hand, facing two crowned figures and three small people, beside the line "Fidelis angeli iuvant" (the angels help the faithful). The second fresco shows three green mountains amid wind, the tallest topped by a structure beneath a circle with a golden centre.

The wiki reads the floating island as Celestia and the crowned figures as Sal Vindagnyr's priest-kings receiving something from an angel, the symbol combining upright and inverted triquetras. In the second fresco's broken top-right corner an inverted triquetra can still be seen.

History: The princess had the gift of foresight and painted her visions. Her father Varuch wanted the third fresco to show the thaw of the snow, but she had been in winter so long that she could not remember what colours to use for blue sky and green grass. She also promised Imunlaukr that a fourth fresco would be his likeness. She never finished the third and never painted the fourth.

Before he left to seek a way to save the kingdom, she gave Imunlaukr a Starsilver greatsword, the Snow-Tombed Starsilver, and said she would wait for him, but the storm drowned out her words. When he returned and found everyone dead he was disillusioned with Celestia, vowed to entertain the heavens with a "song of iron and blood", and left the sword in this room as he went in search of wars to fight. The princess's box laments that she could no longer bear the cold.

Atmosphere: A quiet, enclosed cave with faded green hills on its walls and a sword standing at the centre: a mourning room more than a gallery.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1; open to anyone who completes the objective.

141.content: The Starsilver greatsword the Princess of Sal Vindagnyr gave to Imunlaukr; its in-game description says it was kept between frescoes and can cleave ice and snow. Imunlaukr left it in the Mural Room.

142.content:
Musk Reef (also: Pilos Peak): Musk Reef is a small island off the coast of Galesong Hill in Mondstadt. Its main feature is the portal to the Spiral Abyss, and it is reached through a bluish-purple time tunnel at Cape Oath (or by gliding there from the cape). Long ago, before Barbatos reshaped the land, it was the summit of a great mountain called Pilos Peak.

The island is also tied to the adventurer Leonard, who failed to climb Pilos Peak and later invented the wind glider. Long after his time, his lingering will fell on the reef during the Unreconciled Stars event.

Geography: A rocky islet rising above the sea off Cape Oath, within Galesong Hill. It holds the Spiral Abyss domain entrance, an Anemo elemental monument and Anemograna to collect. Visitors arrive by stepping into the time tunnel (wormhole) at the edge of Cape Oath, which the wiki lists as a one-way link, or by gliding across from the cape.

The reef is the surviving tip of a vanished mountain: Mona observes that its summit still reaches just above the water. In Leonard's day the peak lay under heavy snow, as his journal describes; today only a modest island stands above the waves.

Places: The Spiral Abyss portal is the one significant feature on the island. Entry becomes available once a player reaches Adventure Rank 20 (a gameplay requirement; the Abyss itself is described in its own entry).

History: Before Barbatos became the Anemo Archon, about 2,600 years ago, the area was part of the continent and the reef was the summit of Pilos Peak. The adventurer Leonard tried to reach the top but never managed it. When Barbatos raised the winds to clear the ice and snow from the land and reshaped Mondstadt, the mountain was swept from its place, the meltwater became sea, and its peak became the island now called Musk Reef.

Leonard recorded his attempt in a journal, "Of Mountains and Seas" (a copy is in the Mondstadt library), and mentions help from Venerare of the Lawrence Clan in getting across to the peak. He died before achieving his dream. His other legacy is the wind glider, built so that people could go where their legs could not carry them.

Dangers: Canon describes no ordinary dangers on the island. Its one notable hazard was the meteorite core during the Unreconciled Stars event (see the sub-entry below), which also drew Fatui agents.

Travel: Cape Oath hosts the time tunnel that leads here. Gliding off the cape is the alternative route. The usual reason to visit is to reach the Spiral Abyss.

Quests: Musk Reef features in the 1.1 Unreconciled Stars event quest "Where Ancient Stars Align" (see the sub-entry below) and as the Spiral Abyss location.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Musk Reef remains an ordinary accessible island in Mondstadt, still holding the Spiral Abyss portal. The meteorite crisis of 1.1 ended long ago. Nothing in Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content changes it.

143.comment: Musk Reef: Leonard and Pilos Peak
143.content:
Pilos Peak was the mountain Leonard could never climb. In his journal he writes that by forty he had conquered every domain, but the peak alone defeated him, and fear of the cold, snow-buried summit cost him his courage as a climber. He turned to building tools, reasoning that where legs fail, wings might carry. That ambition produced the wind glider. The journal also thanks Venerare, of the Lawrence Clan of his day, for help in getting across to the mountain.

Mona, who reconstructed the missing parts of the book with her astrolabe, dates him roughly two thousand years back; the wiki argues for about 2,600 years. Barbatos' reshaping of the land later turned the mountain into the reef.

144.comment: Musk Reef: Unreconciled Stars at Musk Reef
144.content: During the 1.1 event Unreconciled Stars (a limited-time event), meteorites fell across Mondstadt and put those who touched them into a deep sleep in which they felt driven to climb a mountain. Mona identified them as the fallen constellation of an ancient adventurer, Leonard, carrying his unfulfilled will. She and the Traveler found his journal, worked out that the largest meteorite, the core, would have fallen on the summit he never reached, and went to Musk Reef. Fatui agents were there; the Fatui Harbinger Scaramouche, who had entered the dream, left shaken, claiming to have discovered something about the sky. The Traveler and Mona fought off the agents and destroyed the core, ending the dreams.

145.content:
Nameless Island (also: the nameless island, Mondstadt sundial island): The Nameless Island is a small, uninhabited island off the coast northeast of Starfell Valley in Mondstadt, with no name on the map. A weathered sundial stands at its centre, and the island is where the world quest Time and Wind begins.

The sundial is carved with a riddle about stories carried on the wind, and a second, matching sundial stands near the Thousand Winds Temple on the mainland. Reaching the island is itself a small discovery for a traveller.

Geography: The island lies across the water northeast of Starfell Valley, within sight of the mainland coast in clear weather (Henry Morton says he has sometimes seen it). It has a central stone circle with a sundial, some ruined stonework and pillars along its edges. It is not marked on the map. Travellers cross by freezing the water with Cryo, gliding from Starsnatch Cliff, or using a Waverider.

Wind is the island's character. Near its centre a strange gusting sound can be heard that grows stronger behind the sundial and stops at the very middle. The same sound is heard at the wind barrier around Stormterror's Lair.

Places: The sundial, with its carved riddle, is the one notable feature. Around it are a stone circle, a few ruins on the eastern coast and a large pillar, all used as places where wind gathers during the quest. A breakable rock on the island's south end hides a ragged notebook.

History: Nobody on the island is known. Its makers and purpose are unrecorded. The only human trace is the notebook left by an archaeologist who surveyed the matching sundial site at the Thousand Winds Temple, then vanished; his friend Henry Morton, a scholar, searched for him in Mondstadt.

The notebook's author reasoned that the island and the Thousand Winds Temple were linked, that together the sundial inscriptions form one message, and that the pair may relate to a forgotten god of Time, possibly connected by ancient scholars to the Anemo Archon. He noted that something odd happens there between about 2 and 5 in the morning, but, lacking a Vision, he could not investigate. This is his theory, not confirmed canon.

Atmosphere: Quiet, windblown and slightly uncanny: a lonely islet with old carved stone and sea air, where the wind seems to carry a faint whisper in the early hours.

Dangers: A Ruin Guard (an elite enemy) sometimes spawns there. During the quest, wind clusters dispersed with Anemo summon Anemo slimes, and an Eye of the Storm (a pure elemental lifeform) appears.

Quests: Time and Wind (world quest, 1.0). Reaching the island, breaking the rock on its south end and reading the Ragged Notebook starts it. The Traveler uses Elemental Sight in the early morning to find and disperse wind clusters, scatters a deposit of wind, and fights the Eye of the Storm, which flees toward the Thousand Winds Temple. There the Traveler finds the identical sundial and Henry Morton, who learns of the island and plans to visit it with the Traveler.

In the second half the Traveler must again wait for the small hours, disperse four small wind clusters and scatter another deposit of wind, and face a stronger Eye of the Storm. The faint voices heard along the way speak of an ancient tale carried on the wind and of something that will sprout again in time. Morton concludes the two sundials and places must be linked but the quest ends without explaining the link.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the island is unchanged and still uninhabited. No later content revisits the riddle, the sundials or the missing archaeologist.

146.content:
Old Sanatorium Site: The Old Sanatorium Site is a former mountain sanatorium on Windrest Peak, torn down a few years ago. It stands above the ruins of a temple left behind when the Temple of Space was lifted into the heavens, and its Anemo Archon statue is the gateway up to that temple. Locals say that whoever visits the sanatorium stays in the enchanted hills forever.

The site is kept by its doorman Mann, who oversees demolition and heritage preservation. A cemetery of patients' graves lies inside the ruins.

Geography: The sanatorium lies up the mountain from Dornman Port. Its corridors and rooms are half collapsed and full of dust-covered beds and abandoned things. A cemetery with patients' tombstones lies within, and Dandelion Seed grows on the grounds.

Weasels burrow in the broken buildings, and a lizard can startle a visitor on an old bed. The statue of the Anemo Archon at the site is a gateway: investigating it, as Nihilita directs, opens a path into the sky above Windrest Peak.

Places: Rooms with beds and a stack of notes left by patients, and the graveyard at the back with portrait-bearing stones.

Three patient letters are on a stack of paper. Old Bauer gives his bought burial plot and headstone to Koche on leaving the sanatorium after making peace with his family; Koche, a miner changing careers, then offers it to any other patient who wants it; and Totengrabov, a stonecarver, offers free inscriptions in Liyue, Mondstadt or Inazuman style, recognised by the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and the Church of Favonius.

People: Mann is the elderly doorman who guards the site. He says he oversees demolition work and heritage preservation, worries that the building is being left to rot, and is followed everywhere by a dog named Hauptmann.

Zeitlind, whose elder sister Raumhilda wrote that the sanatorium was closing and that she was going far away, comes to the site seeking her and to say goodbye. She is startlingly like the portrait on her sister's gravestone. Huffman, who stands with Mann at the Dornman Port waypoint, asks the Traveler to check the site.

History: Before the sanatorium there was a temple of the Arcadians dedicated to Istaroth; it was once connected to the Temple of Space. After a disaster, the Temple of Space was lifted into the heavens and hidden, while the earthbound half fell into ruin and was later expanded into the sanatorium. The sanatorium has since been demolished.

Asmoday's gaze fell on the lifted temple only after its destruction and made it a watchtower called Segment-Domain Tau. In the present, the Watcher Nihilita, having fallen to the mortal world, asks the Traveler to ascend and free the uplifted people of the past.

Quests: The Wind Has Ceased, the opening quest of the series A Long Day in the Mountains, begins near the northern waypoint in Dornman Port with Mann's story of ghosts. The Traveler investigates at night, meets Zeitlind, and is taken up through the Anemo statue to the Temple of Space.

Atmosphere: Dust, damp and the creak of old beds in a half-collapsed building, where the notes patients left behind keep their jokes and their grief.

Dangers: No fighting in the ruins themselves. In the first quest, patrol Domain Keepers are visible on the road to the sanatorium.

Status as of 7.1: Demolished and decaying as of 7.1; an access point to the Temple of Space.

147.comment: Old Sanatorium Site: Zeitlind and Raumhilda
147.content: Zeitlind came to the site seeking her older sister Raumhilda, whose letters said the sanatorium was closing and that she was going somewhere far away. Her sister's portrait gravestone reads "One lifetime doesn't count". Istoria in the Temple of Space remembers a "Hilda" and says she always looked a little gloomy.

148.comment: Old Sanatorium Site: Mann and the ghost story
148.content: Mann is an old doorman who swears he saw ghosts at night. The figure he took for a ghost was Zeitlind, who arrived late at night to visit her sister's grave and ended up scaring him. He is trying to keep people away from Windrest Peak.

key: Pillar Hall of Space: Front Hall
Pillar Hall of Space: Rear Hall
149.content:
Path of the Forgotten World (also: Pillar Hall of Space: Front Hall, Pillar Hall of Space: Rear Hall): The Path of the Forgotten World is the entrance area of the Temple of Space, the floating hall above Windrest Peak in Mondstadt. The wiki calls it the entrance area, leading toward the central Pillar Hall. Creatures from lost ages are exhibited along it. The area has very little recorded lore of its own.

The wiki describes it as Asmoday's adaptation of the Login Screen environment. Its map levels are labelled the Pillar Hall of Space Front Hall and Rear Hall.

Geography: A pair of halls running from the entrance to the central Pillar Hall, with a Teleport Waypoint, Harpasta (which turn the player into a Plume Moth) and Organization Type Segment-Domain Keepers. Dex helps the player move architecture along the way.

The Organization Type Keepers usually do not harm people unless they try to steal relics, according to Istoria.

People: No residents are listed. Exhibits include two Fontemer Aberrants: an Armored Crab and a Blubberbeast, which speak when interacted with.

The Armored Crab recalls seeing creatures like it in the southern territories when the apostle of the Golden City (Hyperborea) still walked the world, wonders what the Great Mother who made them would think of one of her creations confined here, and adds that perhaps every place in the world is a cage. The Blubberbeast notes that this "lazy and degenerate lower creature", as Remurians called it, has wandered the seas for longer than Remuria endured, and so may be closer to eternity than any empire.

History: Part of Asmoday's temple. The temple selects not only people but landscapes, relics and ecosystems from vanished ages, which is why animals from lost civilisations are kept here.

Dangers: Organization Type Keepers (avoid stealing relics) and Domain Keepers elsewhere in the temple.

Atmosphere: Hushed and museum-like: exhibits left standing in a space with no wind and no passage of time.

Status as of 7.1: As of 6.5 (unchanged through 7.1) the Path is open and uneventful.

No quest is listed as centred on it.

150.content:
Peak of Vindagnyr (also: Elegiac Rime): The Peak of Vindagnyr is a Domain of Blessing on the summit of Dragonspine, at the Skyfrost Nail. It was once a ritual site close to the sky where Sal Vindagnyr's priests ascended to face the heavens, until a frigid nail from the firmament buried it in the mountainside. The cold inside is a trial in itself: visitors must conquer it to pass.

Clearing it yields artifacts. It opens after the world quest "In the Mountains".

Geography: The entrance is on Dragonspine's peak at the Skyfrost Nail subarea, a tilted doorway unlike any other domain's. Inside, the unique frigid environment is made of platforms that alternate between a Warm and a Subzero state.

The surrounding peak was once the lush mountain of Vindagnyr. Its ruins include the white Frostbearing Tree and the Entombed City below, all frozen after the nail came down.

History: Sal Vindagnyr was an ancient kingdom founded by refugees on a green mountain in the era of the unified civilization. The domain's description calls the peak a festive site where priests ascended to face the heavens. After the Skyfrost Nail fell, the site was buried and that voice fell silent; the priests did not return.

In Sal Vindagnyr lore the nail fell from Celestia for unknown reasons, shrouding the city in cloud and snowstorm; the kingdom perished, and the hero Imunlaukr returned too late to find survivors. The domain is named "Elegiac Rime" at every level, an elegy being a song of mourning and rime a quick-formed ice.

Dangers: Sheer Cold accumulates on characters and drains HP once full; Warm areas diminish it while Subzero areas speed it up. At higher levels Warm areas also let Pyro remove Cryo from opponents.

Opponents are cryo slimes, ice-shield hilichurls, ice shieldwall mitachurls and, at the final stage, a Frostarm Lawachurl. Gameplay notes: it requires Adventure Rank 30 to 45 across four levels and rewards the Blizzard Strayer, Heart of Depth, Defender's Will and Gambler artifact sets, as of the wiki's current listing. The 4.8 update changed its recommended element to Pyro and revised the enemies.

Quests: The domain is unlocked by completing the world quest "In the Mountains", in which the Traveler helps restore the Skyfrost Nail subarea. Chests lie near the entrance.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains a permanent Domain of Blessing, unchanged since 4.8.

151.content: Sheer Cold is Dragonspine's lethal chill. It builds up on those who linger and costs HP once full. It is eased by sources of warmth and, in this domain, by Warm platforms.

152.content:
Pillar Hall Central Zone (also: Hall of a Thousand Pillars, Pillar Hall of Space, Center of the Pillar Hall): The Pillar Hall Central Zone is the centre of the Temple of Space, the floating hall above Windrest Peak. It houses the Memory Core, a storage device holding information about unknown civilisations. The hall is lined with display boards presenting relics of many eras, and it is the safest place in the temple: suppression-type guards cannot enter it. The philosopher Istoria and the shopkeeper Josephus keep to it, and it is the hub from which the three themed exhibition areas are reached.

Its loading-screen title is "Hall of a Thousand Pillars". The Memory Core's description says countless replicas of civilisations drift here, suspended in the windless instant before their extinction.

Geography: A cold, columned hall with a rotating platform at its heart. Dex-assisted puzzles use malleable platforms, path bridging (vertical and horizontal) and spatial dragging. From it the party reaches the Luyang Academy, Mahavaipulya Chamber and Desert Pavilion. The Memory Core stands at its centre.

Elite enemies in the zone are Domain Keepers and the Ruin Grader. Display cases hold relics, and the nearby Path of the Forgotten World and the Apathic Interval are separate parts of the temple.

People: Istoria, a philosopher of the unified civilisation, gathers the party's allies here. Josephus, called the Master of Anti-Self-Termination, is a friend of Istoria's and runs the souvenir shop Emberic Reconstruction, open after The Wind Has Ceased. The wiki also lists Amoxcihuatl, Cirsteen and Soga Sumidanoryu Sakon Shigehira here, without detail.

Josephus says everyone in the temple is everyone else's friend, since otherwise one would drown the world in sorrow, and that no one dies in the Temple of Space. Istoria notes the Organization-type Keepers do not harm people unless they try to steal relics.

Culture: A cooperative and dryly funny society of long-lived scholars and artists. They treat mortality as a joke and philosophy as daily conversation.

History: Once the sacred hall of the God of Space, who is nowhere to be found. After Asmoday vanished, her Watchers Nihilita and Melanta remained; Nihilita departed, and Melanta grew severe. When the laws began to fail, Istoria left the safety of the centre to rescue friends, and met the Traveler there during The Wind Has Ceased in 6.5. The party freed the three exhibition areas and then reached the Cage of Suchness; after Melanta's fall Istoria is found here.

The temple selects people and objects from a vanished age as "segments" and keeps them as living memories. Istoria thinks it was not designed as an eternal paradise. Early on, the God of Space's sisters occasionally brought interesting things in and allowed small pardons for change; Melanta reversed this. Zeitlind's lost belongings, classed as relics, were scattered through the temple's areas.

Dangers: Domain Keepers, Patrol Type Keepers (which send people to the Apathic Interval) and the Ruin Grader. The centre itself is protected from Suppression Type Keepers.

Atmosphere: Echoing and cold, with towering pillars and silent exhibits, broken by Istoria's wry quips and Josephus's grumbling.

Status as of 7.1: As of 6.5 (unchanged through 7.1) the hall is a safe hub for the freed residents and for visitors.

The Memory Core remains an offering system for Memory Factors; offerings raise its level and give rewards, and surplus factors can be traded to Josephus once it is maxed.

153.comment: Pillar Hall Central Zone: Memory Core
153.content: The Memory Core is a storage device at the Temple of Space's heart holding information about unknown civilisations. Memory Factors found in chests or floating clusters are offered to it for rewards; Josephus's shop trades excess factors for items or Mora once the core reaches its maximum. Its lore text says the Pillar Hall stands in silent vigil, no less taciturn than its master.

154.comment: Pillar Hall Central Zone: Pillar Hall Display Boards
154.content: Exhibits include "A Corner of Valivija", a hymn to Nabu Malikata; "Arcadia, the Entombed Capital", a verse about the Knight of the Golden Bough, with Istoria remarking that Arcadian doors seem to open only from within; "From Swords to Plowshares", a Khaenri'ah-made Field Tiller displayed as a farm machine; "Lord Trubetskoy's Treasure", a corner of the Nod-Krai governor's vault now overrun by weasels; "Musica Instrumentalis", a conversation among Calcerius and others about palaces razed; "The First Scroll", about the Masters of the Night-Wind; "Three Strategies Scroll", a tengu sword-training formation; and "The Very First Print of The Steambird". "Deathly Silence" appears after The Starry Night.

155.comment: Pillar Hall Central Zone: Istoria and Josephus
155.content: Istoria is a tall philosopher of the war of funerary flame era with a layered white and dark blue toga; Josephus is his friend, dressed similarly with a laurel wreath, and the pair banter. Istoria called Raumhilda "Hilda" and she called him "Grandpa Istoria". Josephus says nobody dies in the Temple of Space.

156.content:
Sal Vindagnyr (also: Vindagnyr, Entombed City, Kingdom of Sal Vindagnyr): Sal Vindagnyr was an ancient kingdom on the mountain once called Vindagnyr, which is now Dragonspine in Mondstadt. Refugees from a land of snow and strife settled the then-green mountain, and their kingdom prospered under the heavens' blessing. Then the Skyfrost Nail fell from the sky. Endless blizzards buried the kingdom, its sacred white tree was shattered, and its people died. Today only frozen ruins remain, along with murals, carved tablets and a few personal keepsakes.

Its story is pieced together from scattered texts. The chief priest Varuch climbed toward the summit to seek the heavens' guidance and did not come back. His daughter, the princess, painted prophetic frescoes and died trying to save the sacred tree. The outlander hero Imunlaukr went to look for a way to save the kingdom and returned to find everyone dead. A scribe recorded the end.

Geography: The kingdom covered the mountain now called Dragonspine, which was green and fertile before the nail fell. Its capital and palace stood on the mountainside, in the ruins now called the Entombed City. The summit held a ritual site where priests went up to face the heavens. The Skyfrost Nail came down there, and the Peak of Vindagnyr domain sits there now.

Ruins survive in two main places: the Entombed City's ancient palace and its outskirts. Other remains include the hidden Mural Room near the palace, Starglow Cavern, carved tablets scattered across the mountain, and the sacred white tree on the eastern slopes, now called the Frostbearing Tree. A small island east of that tree holds a withered tree with a sword driven into the ground beneath it.

Places: - **Entombed City**: the snow-buried capital and its ancient palace, now the largest field of Sal Vindagnyr ruins on Dragonspine.
- **Frostbearing Tree**: the kingdom's sacred white tree, an Irminsul tree under which the princess was born. A fragment of the nail shattered it.
- **Peak of Vindagnyr**: the former summit ritual site, buried in the mountain by the nail.
- **Mural Room**: a sealed great hall holding the princess's frescoes and the abandoned greatsword Snow-Tombed Starsilver.
- **Starglow Cavern**: a deep cavern where one fragment of the nail lay frozen; the scribe seems to have gone down there after the end.
- **The princess's island**: the small island east of the Frostbearing Tree where she tried to graft a branch of the shattered tree and died. The Princess' Box was found there.
- **A weathered memorial stone** west of the Entombed City outskirts, where the Traveler can lay flowers. It held the Scribe's Box, and the wiki suggests it may be the princess's grave.

People: The texts name only a few people. **Varuch** was the chief priest and the princess's father. **The princess** was born under the white tree, received a blessing that let her foresee the future, and painted what she saw. **Imunlaukr** was a hero from another land who lived in the kingdom. **Ukko** is named in the princess's last words and is generally taken to be the scribe who recorded the kingdom's end.

The kingdom's annalists believed the princess's blessing, like the undying tree, would last forever. Her last words apologise to her father and to Ukko and wish she could see Imunlaukr again. The scribe's final lines are bitter. They wish fire on the frozen sky, call Imunlaukr "that outsider who abandoned the princess", and hope that people building "a new nation without gods" might be strong enough to stand against the world.

Governance: Sal Vindagnyr appears to have been ruled by priests. A weapon appearance released in 7.0 says a divine envoy of the heavens once gave a spear to the high priest of Sal Vindagnyr, and with it the right to lead the city-state. The first mural likewise shows crowned figures receiving something from an angel. In the kingdom's last days, the chief priest Varuch was the one who sought the heavens' guidance on the summit, and his daughter was called the princess.

Culture: The people of Sal Vindagnyr revered the heavens and believed their prosperity was Celestia's lasting blessing. The white tree was sacred to them. Their priests climbed to the summit to ask the heavens for guidance. The princess recorded her visions as frescoes in the great hall, and the annalists wrote the kingdom's history on stone.

Texts from Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya add more. A Nod-Krai prayer to Maadteraahka, Mother of Life (Naberius), recorded in Hymns of the Far North (6.0), says her compassion was revered "from Hyperborea to Sal Vindagnyr". An artifact text (6.3) recalls the age of the three moons, when some peoples climbed the heights of Vindagnyr to offer laurel-crowned verses to the moons, as others did at Lang-Gan and in Arcadia's sacred groves.

History: Thousands of years ago, people fleeing a land of snow and strife found a green mountain. They raised a monument on its peak and named their new home Sal Vindagnyr. For a time the kingdom flourished. Then the Skyfrost Nail descended onto the summit ritual site. Cloud and mist sealed the city in, and snowstorms never stopped. As snow whipped across the sky, the pillar split into three. One fragment shattered the white tree, and the others froze the places where they landed. The trees withered and life on the mountain failed.

Varuch climbed the peak again, hoping his daughter's third fresco would show the snow thawing. She could not paint it, because she had not seen blue sky or green grass in so long that she no longer knew which colours to use. She gave Imunlaukr the Starsilver greatsword and promised to wait for him. Then she took the most intact branch of the shattered tree to a small island to graft it, and died in the cold beside it. The scribe tried to heal the withered ley lines, buried the princess, and recorded that there was no more need for records. Imunlaukr returned to a hall of "deathly echoes", cursed the heavens, left the greatsword between the frescoes, and went down the mountain in search of war.

Atmosphere: The ruins are sad and frozen: snow-choked halls and broken towers, ice that will not melt, and a deadly cold that drains anyone without a source of warmth. The weathered memorials feel ancient. Modern Mondstadters know almost nothing of the kingdom. Even Albedo, who has studied Dragonspine for years, knows it mainly from its stone tablets.

Dangers: The ruins share Dragonspine's deadly cold and its Cryo hilichurls, slimes, Abyss Mages and dormant or active Ruin Machines. A Ruin Grader guards one of the old shard sites below the Entombed City outskirts. The Peak of Vindagnyr shifts between warm and subzero ground, and the subzero ground speeds up the chill.

Quests: In the world quest **In the Mountains** (1.2), the adventurer Iris asks the Traveler to look into the strange ice blocking Dragonspine's routes. Thawing the three frozen fragments of the Skyfrost Nail frees the Frostbearing Tree and restores the nail above the summit. Hidden exploration objectives on the mountain gather the Priest's, Princess' and Scribe's Boxes, light the Ancient Carvings, and open the Mural Room, where the Traveler finds the greatsword Snow-Tombed Starsilver.

In **Ripples That Will Never Reach** (Archon Quest, 6.2), Razmaspes, a man from an ancient age whose ancestors lived in Hyperborea, asks the Traveler's party about Sal Vindagnyr. Albedo replies that he has seen its name on Dragonspine's stone tablets but that only its ruins remain. Razmaspes sighs that there was no way to turn things around.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Sal Vindagnyr is a dead kingdom whose ruins lie frozen under Dragonspine's snow. The Skyfrost Nail that destroyed it hovers, restored, above the summit.

In the 7.1 world quest Anomaly: Mondstadt, the nail has changed in the same way as the other Celestial Nails. Albedo says he had assumed that the nail's purpose ended once the Heavenly Principles passed judgment and it destroyed the ancient civilization. He now sees that it is not that simple, and he stays to observe the change.

157.comment: Sal Vindagnyr: The Princess of Sal Vindagnyr
157.content: The princess of Sal Vindagnyr was the daughter of the chief priest Varuch. She was born under the sacred white tree and blessed with the ability to foresee the future, which she painted into frescoes. She dreamed of a black dragon blotting out the sun and took it as an omen of doom. After the Skyfrost Nail fell, she gave Imunlaukr the Starsilver greatsword and promised him a fresco of his likeness. She could not finish the fresco of the thaw her father hoped for. She died on a small island, trying to graft a branch of the shattered tree, and the scribe buried her.

158.comment: Sal Vindagnyr: Imunlaukr of Sal Vindagnyr
158.content:
Imunlaukr was an outlander hero living in Sal Vindagnyr when the Skyfrost Nail fell. He left to find a way to break the ice; one account says he went looking for a branch of Irminsul. The princess gave him the Snow-Tombed Starsilver. He came back too late, found no one alive, cursed the heavens, and left the greatsword in the Mural Room. His descendants became Mondstadt's Imunlaukr Clan.

Lore added in 6.6 says that a single blow from his spear, struck to save a maiden, is remembered in song as ruining three kingdoms. He was hunted afterwards and gave up the warrior's life.

159.comment: Sal Vindagnyr: The Ancient Carvings and the Three Boxes
159.content: Eight carved stone tablets on Dragonspine, apparently left by the kingdom's last scribe, record its founding and its end, and the Traveler can light them up. Three ornamented boxes, the Priest's, the Princess' and the Scribe's, hold their owners' last thoughts. Varuch hopes his daughter's third fresco will show a thaw. The princess cannot paint it and says goodbye. The scribe wishes ruin on the world and turns to a godless new nation. Together, the boxes open a sealed door on the mountain.

160.comment: Sal Vindagnyr: The Frostbearing Tree's Origins
160.content: The Frostbearing Tree was Sal Vindagnyr's sacred white tree, an Irminsul tree. The Skyfrost Nail shattered it and it froze. Five hundred years ago it absorbed Durin's blood, and after the Traveler broke its icy shell and fed it Crimson Agate, it bore one crimson, icy fruit: the catalyst Frostbearer. The fruit is dedicated to those who lived in its shade, to its priests, and to the girl who painted it.

161.comment: Sal Vindagnyr: Sal Vindagnyr in Ancient Accounts
161.content: Later texts place Sal Vindagnyr among the ancient human peoples of the unified-civilization era. A prayer to Maadteraahka (Naberius) says she was revered "from Hyperborea to Sal Vindagnyr", and Razmaspes, a man of an ancient age whose ancestors lived in Hyperborea, still remembered it by name. An artifact text says pilgrims climbed Vindagnyr to honour the three moons. The Amethyst Crown says the heavens sent the divine nails to "mend the land" and laid mortal realms to waste. Sal Vindagnyr, Hyperborea and Lang-Gan are each tied to a fallen nail.

162.content:
Schulz's Blacksmith (also: Schulz Smithshop): Schulz's Blacksmith is the main forge in Mondstadt City, near the front gate. Wagner the blacksmith and his apprentice Schulz run it, and it forges and sells weapons.

Its map description calls it the most trusted blacksmith in Mondstadt, always hot from the fires and from the owner's passion. It is named after the apprentice Schulz, because Wagner lost a drinking game to him.

Places: A forge with a shopfront. Wagner forges weapons and sells self-defence weapons; Schulz sells the cheapest ones and wanders about the forge all day. The sign over the door reads Schulz Smithshop in Teyvat script.

Mona's Laboratory lies a little further south from here.

People: Wagner is a burly man with dark hair, dark eyes and a white shirt who is proud of his forging. Schulz is his apprentice. Their idle lines are a master's boast that nothing at his shop is second-rate, and an apprentice's awe at the master.

According to the character stories, Wagner nearly sank into despair trying to forge a sword that would hold up for Noelle: over ten blends of alloy dulled quickly because her strength outstripped them. He finally made her a sturdy, heavy claymore reinforced to suit her Geo affinity.

Atmosphere: Heat, hammer noise and warm pride: a working forge in a market district, with a master and a modest apprentice.

Travel: Near the front gate of Mondstadt City, in the market district.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

163.content:
Shattuck: Shattuck is a restaurant in the village of Millhaven in northern Mondstadt. Benthem owns it. It sells simple food and cooking ingredients and first appeared in Version 6.5.

Places: A single restaurant. In gameplay terms the food restocks daily and the ingredients weekly, and the stock includes a local dish, Millhaven's Morning Plate.

People: Benthem is the owner. His idle call is to gather round and see the fresh venison.

The wiki lists the Knight of Favonius Genna and a man named Uchida Kotaro among the people there; their roles are not given.

Travel: In Millhaven, in the Windrest Peak region, the northern part of Mondstadt added in Version 6.5.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

164.content:
Skyfrost Nail (also: Nail of Cold Heavens): The Skyfrost Nail is the Celestial Nail (a "Nail of Retribution") planted at the summit of Dragonspine in Mondstadt, and the summit area takes its name from it. It looks like a colossal broken crystalline pillar. Thousands of years ago it fell from the heavens onto the green mountain of Vindagnyr, burying the kingdom of Sal Vindagnyr under the endless snow that still makes Dragonspine deadly. In the Traveler's time its scattered shards were rejoined, and it now hovers in the air above the peak.

It is one of several nails cast down across Teyvat by the Heavenly Principles. Its fall shattered Sal Vindagnyr's sacred white tree (an Irminsul tree, today the Frostbearing Tree), and the kingdom's people perished in the cold. Before the Traveler, no one in modern times had reached the summit: strange ice blocked the paths.

Geography: The nail stands at Dragonspine's summit, above the ritual site where it struck. The summit is reached through a cave southwest of Dragonspine's Statue of The Seven; until the nail's shards were freed, a strange, powerful air current blowing out of that cavern blocked the way. Beneath the nail's impact point a large hollow lies under the ice, where the Peak of Vindagnyr domain entrance now sits.

Places: - **The nail itself**: a towering pillar with a stone-like shell and a blue crystalline interior visible at its broken end, crowned with the celestial motif shared by all such nails. Since its restoration it floats above the summit, and it can be climbed.
- **Peak of Vindagnyr**: the domain beneath the nail. Its description calls it a ritual site once close to the skies that the frigid nail buried into the mountainside; inside, the cold is so intense that one must fight it as well as the enemies.

History: Thousands of years ago, refugees fleeing a land of snow and strife settled the lush mountain they named Vindagnyr, raised a monument on its peak and founded Sal Vindagnyr, which prospered under the heavens' blessing. Then the Skyfrost Nail descended on the ritual site at the summit. Clouds and blizzards closed over the kingdom, the cold never lifted, and the sacred tree was shattered. The chief priest Varuch climbed to the summit to beg the heavens for guidance and never returned; the princess died trying to graft a branch of the dead tree; the outlander hero Imunlaukr went in search of a way to break the ice and came back to find no one left alive.

The Ancient Carvings, apparently left by the kingdom's last scribe, record that as snow whipped across the skies "the pillar that fell from the heavens was riven in three". The fragments froze the places where they came to rest, and one struck the white tree. Another fragment records that someone (the surviving text does not say who) attempted to heal the ley lines, but the tree had already withered. Albedo calls the nail's fall a judgment passed down by the Heavenly Principles. In general, canon texts say the heavens sent the nails down after the war of funerary flame to purge corruption and "mend the land", laying waste to mortal realms as they did. No source says why Sal Vindagnyr in particular was struck.

Quests: In the world quest **In the Mountains** (1.2), the adventurer Iris at the Dragonspine Adventurer Camp asks the Traveler to look into the strange, fire-proof ice blocking her teams' routes. Using Scarlet Quartz, the Traveler thaws the shard frozen at the Frostbearing Tree and then the ones at the Entombed City outskirts and Starglow Cavern. Each one flies up toward the summit. That opens the cavern to the peak, where Paimon spots a giant pillar with the three shards frozen around it again. Once they are thawed a second time and rejoined to the main body, the ice beneath the pillar shatters, revealing the hollow below, and the restored nail rises to hover over the summit. Iris is astonished to hear of a huge pillar floating there and plans to send explorers up.

In **Anomaly: Mondstadt** (7.1, part of the world quest series The Anomaly, available after A Rekviem for the Underworld), the Traveler and Paimon find that the Skyfrost Nail has changed in the same way as the other nails. Albedo, waiting at the summit, says he has never seen anything like it in all his time on Dragonspine. He had assumed that once the Heavenly Principles passed judgment and the nail destroyed Sal Vindagnyr, its purpose was complete, but now sees it is not that simple. He stays to observe how the change affects the surrounding ecosystem.

Dangers: The summit is the coldest part of a mountain whose cold kills. Without warmth, Sheer Cold builds up until it drains a person's life, so warmth sources such as braziers, torches, Warming Seelies and the crystals called Scarlet Quartz matter. Cryo hilichurls and slimes roam the summit area, and a Frostarm Lawachurl guarded one of the frozen shards.

Atmosphere: Biting wind and snow, bitter cold that even Paimon complains of, and above it all a vast pillar hanging silent in the air; those who climb it find themselves dizzyingly high above the mountain. The ruins of Sal Vindagnyr below and the blue plants around the old ice give the area a mournful, ancient feel. Ordinary visitors have no idea what the pillar is: Paimon could only guess that it fell from the sky.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Skyfrost Nail is whole again and hovers above Dragonspine's summit. After the Ruler of Death Ronova's last act in Snezhnaya, it is giving off the same strange mark of light into the sky as the other Nails of Retribution across Teyvat, and Albedo is studying it.
