The change began when the dying Ronova fused the Eitr with Snezhnaya's nail, causing that nail to crumble (Archon Quest Chapter VII, 7.1). Albedo's observations focus on how the change affects Dragonspine's ecosystem. What it means has not been revealed.

165.comment: Skyfrost Nail: Celestial Nails Across Teyvat
165.content: The Skyfrost Nail is Mondstadt's Celestial Nail. Others are known in Liyue (the Spiritstone over the Chasm, which destroyed Lang-Gan), on Inazuma's Tsurumi Island, under Sumeru's Eternal Oasis and Mt. Damavand, in Natlan, and at Hyperborea in Snezhnaya. All look like broken crystalline pillars that disturb the ley lines and the weather where they land, and Nahida has said they can purify and stabilise powers that should not exist in Teyvat. Withered trees like Dragonspine's lie near several of them. No nail is known in Fontaine, and no Anomaly mark appeared there in 7.1.

key: pillar that fell from the heavens
166.comment: Skyfrost Nail: The Riven Pillar and Its Shards
166.content: After its fall the nail split in three. The fragments, frozen in Ancient Rime, lay at the Frostbearing Tree, beneath the Entombed City outskirts and in Starglow Cavern, each surrounded by blue plants. Fire cannot melt that ice, but the warmth of Dragonspine's Scarlet Quartz crystals can. Each shard freed by the Traveler flew back to the summit and refroze around the main pillar until it was thawed again and rejoined, after which the whole nail rose into the air.

167.content:
Snow-Covered Path: The Snow-Covered Path is the trail up the lower slopes of Dragonspine, Mondstadt's permanently frozen mountain. It is coated in ice all the way up, and the Dragonspine Adventurer Camp and the Frostbearing Tree lie along it.

It is the usual way into the mountain for adventurers, and cold is its main hazard. An official field report describes the climb as less steep than expected but icy throughout, and so cold that even grass will not burn, so travelers keep hunting for the next heat source.

Geography: A glazed mountain trail on Dragonspine's lower slopes. Ancient Rime, Scarlet Quartz and Warming Seelie are found along it, and the Frostbearing Tree, the frozen remnant of a tree tied to the lost kingdom of Sal Vindagnyr, stands here.

Higher up lie Starglow Cavern and, at the summit, the Skyfrost Nail. The path is the lived-in part of the mountain, while the deeper caverns and the peak belong to the ruins and the dragon's remains.

People: The Dragonspine Adventurer Camp sits on the path. Its residents include the researcher Stevens, the chef Harris, the weaponsmith Orban, the adventurer Iris, and Joel and Joserf. A Treasure Hoarder named Knotty is also found on the path.

The camp serves explorers who come to study the mountain and its ruins. The Knights' alchemist Albedo keeps his own, separate campsite elsewhere on Dragonspine.

Dangers: Killing cold above all: without a heat source, warmth or Scarlet Quartz, travelers lose strength. Cryo hilichurls (shooters, grenadiers, shield guards, a Cryo Samachurl), Cryo Slimes and Treasure Hoarders work the path, and Fatui Geochanter, Pyroslinger and Electrohammer agents and a Fatui Cryo Cicin Mage have been seen.

Atmosphere: White slopes, ice underfoot, breath fogging in the air, and a constant search for the next small fire or warming Seelie.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing in canon has changed here: it remains a frozen but travelable trail with a small adventurers' camp. It was introduced with Dragonspine in version 1.2.

168.content:
Spiral Abyss (also: Abyssus Obscura, Abyss Corridor, Abyssal Moon Spire, Moment of Syzygy): The Spiral Abyss is a special domain on Musk Reef, an island off Cape Oath in Galesong Hill. In-game text calls it a massive underground city built by an ancient civilization long gone, whose purpose remains unknown, with forgotten secrets and treasures buried within. Its first-entry message calls it an inverse tower, and gives it the Latin name Abyssus Obscura, "Dark Abyss". Monsters and humans alike flock to it.

Adventurers reach it from Cape Oath's sky wormhole once they are strong enough (Adventure Rank 20) and challenge floor after floor for Abyssal Stars.

Geography: Musk Reef is a small island reached through a time tunnel (a bluish-purple portal) at Cape Oath, or by gliding there. The Spiral Abyss portal stands on it. The structure has two parts: the Abyss Corridor, which "connects worlds", and the Abyssal Moon Spire, which "leads to the unknown".

Twelve floors of three chambers each: floors 1-8 form the Corridor, floors 9-12 the Spire. A menu description says the cycles of the moon mark the turning points of fate, and that the treasures at the Spire's end show themselves as the gears turn. Menu text hints that people who ascended to Celestia saw the same helix-shaped divine ladder shown in Visions.

History: Its history is not told. The first-entry message says only that a great empire, long gone, built it. Musk Reef itself was once Pilos Peak, a mountain summit reshaped when Barbatos blew away the snow 2,600 years ago, and Leonard failed to climb it.

The wiki ties "a great empire" to the unified civilization. It also notes the monthly Spire reset on the 16th, which before 16 June 2024 occurred twice monthly; a gameplay detail, not lore.

Places: Within the domain: the Abyss Corridor (floors 1-8), unlocked from the start; and the Abyssal Moon Spire (floors 9-12), unlocked by clearing floor 8. Each floor has three chambers, each with a Ley Line Disorder.

Dangers: Gameplay labelled: enemies vary every cycle and often include bosses or Local Legends on the last floors; each floor restricts food, party changes and levelling. Enemy HP is raised on later floors (150 percent on floors 3-7, 200 percent on 8-11, 250 percent on 12 versus the open world). From floor 5 two teams of up to four characters are required, with no character repeated.

Challengers choose one Benediction of the Abyss at each chamber (buffs that refresh daily), and each month brings a Blessing of the Abyssal Moon to the Spire. Entering the next floor needs six Abyssal Stars from the last.

Travel: Reached from Cape Oath's edge by the wormhole, or by gliding from Cape Oath to Musk Reef.

Quests: The Abyss Corridor holds permanent rewards. Clearing floor 3 chamber 3 earns Xiangling through "People's Choice", and floor 4 chamber 3 earns Collei through "Curtain of Leaves". Later floors give Primogems, Mora and artifact reliquary materials; the Spire's rewards reset monthly.

Atmosphere: An underground structure of corridors and a spire under a moon that the wiki says looks unlike Teyvat's, monsters waiting in each chamber, and an everlasting whisper (the Benediction text) that encourages challengers to go deeper.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Spiral Abyss remains open as a permanent special domain.

Its enemy lineup changes with the version (floors 11 and 12 each version, floors 9 and 10 yearly), but no new lore about it has been published through 7.1.

169.comment: Spiral Abyss: Moment of Syzygy and the Abyssal Moon
169.content: The Abyssal Moon Spire resets on the 16th of every month, an event called the Moment of Syzygy, and begins a new Blessing of the Abyssal Moon. The wiki infers the moon seen in the Spire differs from Teyvat's and that the Spire follows another realm's lunar cycle; this is inferred, not stated.

170.content:
Springvale (also: Springvale village, Clear Spring Town): Springvale is a small, peaceful hunting village in Windwail Highland, south of Mondstadt City and facing the lake around it. It is a cluster of one-storey tan houses with blue-tiled roofs, a single windmill, and a natural spring beneath it. Most residents are hunters who supply fresh meat to Mondstadt's restaurants, and the village attracts tourists with its rustic charm. Locals pass down a legend of a benevolent spirit living in the spring.

The legend says a Spring Fairy once filled an empty well with life-saving water for a dying boy, and the settlement grew around the miracle. The fairy is real: an Oceanid from Fontaine who settled here.

Geography: Dirt-paved lanes, a windmill and the spring below it. Anemo Slimes and the occasional Fatui Electro Cicin Mage are the creatures noted here. Local specialties are calla lilies, dandelion seeds and Philanemo mushrooms. A seelie can be found for exploration progress.

The Dawn Winery lies a short way southwest, and the dark forest of Wolvendom is nearby, avoided by locals. The village is also the game's safe return point if the open world hits an error.

People: Draff is head of the hunters and father of Diona; Allan and Jotun are hunters, Olaf also lives here. Old Finch, the village's elderly believer in the Spring Fairy, stands by the spring by day. Brook is a chef, and Hopkins the Marvelous also sells goods. The bard Myweiss, Marla and Pepe are further residents.

Younger villagers call Finch "Grandpa". The hunters' reputation for fresh meat is reflected in Mondstadt's restaurants, and a billboard in the village (written by an unnamed local) extols mushroom dishes.

Culture: Hunting, spring water and storytelling define Springvale. Its young hunters seeking love catch foxes in Wolvendom during Windblume and release them wearing flower wreaths. The book series "Heart of Clear Springs" retells the village's fairy tale.

Most villagers regard the Spring Fairy as a fairy tale; a few, like Old Finch, still believe in her. Diona's Character Story credits the fairy's blessing for her gift of making delicious drinks.

History: By legend a mother brought her deathly ill son to an empty well; a fairy filled it with life-saving water, the miracle drew people, and a settlement was built over the spring. Olaf says the water is really melted snow from Dragonspine. The fairy is the Oceanid Callirhoe, who settled here after the Hydro Archon Egeria's death.

Old Finch befriended her as a boy and waited at the spring into old age; his story inspired "Heart of Clear Springs". She befriended Diona as a lonely child and blessed her on her seventh birthday, then withdrew because of the gap between Oceanid and human lifespans.

Atmosphere: Sleepy and sunlit; the windmill turns, hunters come and go, and the spring murmurs. The mood is tender and slightly melancholy, tied to the unrequited fairy tale.

Status as of 7.1: Quiet and unchanged as of 7.1.

No Springvale story after 1.4 was found beyond Callirhoe's appearance in the Waterborne Poetry event.

171.content:
Callirhoe, the Spring Fairy, is an Oceanid who settled in Springvale after Egeria's death. Heart of Clear Springs is a four-volume book collection retelling a story in which a tearful boy makes a wish at the spring and the fairy listens. In the book she gives a parting kiss and he believes in her to his death; per the quest Heart of the Deep, the real events differ.

During Wishful Drops (1.4, limited) Endora sensed her but got no answer at first; later she relayed a poem and a message imploring Old Finch to move on. In Waterborne Poetry she took human form briefly and took part in the Neighbouring Nations Congenial Poetry Gala as "Riddle Writer".

172.content: During the event, Mondstadt's waters turned bitter, but Springvale's spring did not. The Traveler, Paimon and Endora visited Old Finch there, and the spring's poem "The stream of life flows on" was passed to Endora via Oceanid creatures.

173.content:
Starfell Lake (also: The Marsh of Celestial Guardians): Starfell Lake is a lake and marsh in Starfell Valley, Mondstadt, near Mondstadt City and the Whispering Woods. A Statue of The Seven stands here. In the Prologue it is where the Traveler first felt Anemo power answer and glimpsed a green dragon flying toward a distant forest.

Its viewpoint is titled "The Marsh of Celestial Guardians", and local verse links the water to falling stars. Calla Lilies grow here.

Geography: A lake with marshy surroundings in the Starfell Valley subarea, near the capital and the Whispering Woods. The Statue of The Seven is the main feature, and Calla Lily is the local plant specialty.

The viewpoint is catalogued as "The Marsh of Celestial Guardians"; the Chinese name literally reads "Starfall Lake". The wiki treats the lake as its own subarea, separate from Cider Lake, where the city stands.

History: Folklore only: a poem says a star once fell to the earth and formed the lake, while other tales say even stars as bright as the Anemo Archon's eyes will fall into it. These are in-world stories, not established history, and canon records no real origin for the lake.

Atmosphere: Open water and marsh under wind, with a lone statue by the shore. A quiet, scenic spot close to the city.

Quests: In the Prologue (Act I, "The Outlander Who Caught the Wind"), Paimon and the Traveler went to Starfell Lake hoping to contact one of the Seven. When the Traveler touched the Anemo statue, its power resonated with them, and they saw a green dragon (Dvalin) heading toward a distant forest. They followed it into the Whispering Woods.

Shortly before, the Traveler had woken in Teyvat with their powers sealed and fished Paimon from the sea near Cape Oath. The statue's resonance pointed them to Mondstadt and the Anemo Archon as the first lead in the search for the lost sibling. The dragon here is the first sign of "Stormterror", as Mondstadters later call him.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an ordinary, calm area of Mondstadt; no later story has changed it.

174.comment: Starfell Lake: Starfell Lake Statue and the Prologue
174.content: At Starfell Lake's Statue of The Seven the Traveler first felt Anemo power resonate with them. That led Paimon and the Traveler to pursue a green dragon into the Whispering Woods, where they saw a boy (Venti) speaking calmly to it before both fled. Neither yet knew the boy was Barbatos or the dragon Dvalin.

175.content:
Starfell Valley: Starfell Valley is the central and most varied region of Mondstadt, running from Stormbearer Point on the south coast to the Whispering Woods. Its centre is Cider Lake, on whose island stands Mondstadt City, and it is where the Knights of Favonius mainly carry out their duty of protecting locals and travelers. Lakes, woods, ruins and cliffs make it the area most visitors, including the Traveler at the start of the story, first see.

The valley also holds Starfell Lake, Starsnatch Cliff, the Whispering Woods, where the Traveler first meets Venti and Dvalin, and the ruined Thousand Winds Temple in the northeast.

Geography: Abundant lakes and a wide variety of trees. Stormbearer Point lies at the southern tip, with the Stormbearer Coast just south of it; Cider Lake lies at the centre, with Mondstadt City on its island; Starfell Lake and the Whispering Woods are nearby. Local plants include calla lily, cecilia, dandelion seed, philanemo mushroom, small lamp grass and valberry.

Cider Lake's clear, never-freezing waters are the headwaters that made Mondstadt's ciders and wines famous. The Whispering Woods are dense and deep, cut by a small road; travelers took the sound of wind in the leaves for whispers, hence the name. Starfell Lake has a Statue of the Seven, and its viewpoint is titled The Marsh of Celestial Guardians.

Places: Mondstadt City and Cider Lake; Starfell Lake; the Whispering Woods; Starsnatch Cliff; Stormbearer Point (with the Storm Barrier ruins); the Thousand Winds Temple, with the Temple of the Wolf domain beside it.

Stormbearer Point and Starsnatch Cliff each hold a Time Trial Challenge. The Thousand Winds Temple carries an inscription: "Seeds of stories, brought by the wind and cultivated by time."

People: Mondstadt City's people are covered in the Mondstadt entry. Out in the valley the Knight of Favonius Harry and the Storm Watcher Vind are met at Stormbearer Point; the researcher Patchi the Curious, Doolan and Henry Morton at the Thousand Winds Temple; and Marla, Marvin and Sharp appear at Starsnatch Cliff at night.

The wiki describes the valley as where the Knights' duties primarily take place, with guards patrolling the area.

Governance: No lord holds the valley. The Knights of Favonius patrol it from their headquarters in Mondstadt City and protect locals and travelers alike.

Culture: Cider Lake is regarded as a symbol of Mondstadt; two drinks are named for it, a sweet milk-and-juice "Sweet Cider Lake" and an only lightly alcoholic "Cider Lake". Starsnatch Cliff is a quiet nighttime spot.

The Thousand Winds Temple's carvings and its maxim on wind carrying the seeds of tales are the nearest thing to a monument to Mondstadt's old gods. A giant sundial stands east of the Temple of the Wolf.

History: The Thousand Winds Temple was built by the people of Arcadia to worship Istaroth, Ruler of Time, and left in ruins when Arcadia fell. During the Archon War the Gunnhildr Clan settled among the ruins, seeking help against the relentless blizzards of the war between Decarabian and Boreas, built a small shrine to Istaroth and prayed. A small wind spirit, Barbatos, answered instead.

Still only a wind spirit, Barbatos met Istaroth at the temple, and after hearing his wish she entrusted him with fragments of her power and authority. After he became the Anemo Archon the temple was rebuilt to honour both him and Istaroth, and the weapons of the Sacrificial Series were once ritual implements there. Istaroth was gradually forgotten for unknown reasons. In the aristocratic era the temple became an arena in which slaves were forced to fight for the nobles, and it was later abandoned again.

Atmosphere: Open skies, windmills and lakeshore on the south side; hushed, whispering woodland near the lake; cold stone and weeds in the temple ruins. The city's walls and windmills rise over it all.

Dangers: Hilichurls and slimes, with a hilichurl tower near Stormbearer Point. Area bosses are an Anemo Hypostasis and a Cryo Regisvine.

The Temple of the Wolf is a one-time trial domain in which the player chooses Hydro, Electro or Pyro trials.

Travel: The city is reached by a long bridge to its island. Springvale lies south of the city and the Dawn Winery southwest; Windrise and the coast are east, and the Brightcrown Mountains northwest (see the Mondstadt entry). The Stormbearer Coast to the south is where the Traveler's journey begins.

Quests: The Traveler's story begins on the coast south of Stormbearer Point, and the Whispering Woods are where they first meet Venti and Dvalin.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Starfell Valley is the calm, patrolled centre of Mondstadt; the pages read for this entry record no new threat here after 1.0.

Mondstadt City, its Knights and the Cathedral are covered in the Mondstadt entry and their own files.

176.content: The southern tip of Starfell Valley and the coast just south of it are where the Traveler begins their journey across Teyvat with Paimon. Ruins and a Storm Barrier stand here, a hilichurl tower and a seelie court nearby; the Knight Harry and the Storm Watcher Vind can be met.

177.content: Dense woods near Starfell Lake and the city, where wind in the leaves sounds like whispering. The wiki records it as where the Traveler first meets Venti and Dvalin. A Statue of the Seven stands by Starfell Lake.

178.comment: Starfell Valley: Thousand Winds Temple and Temple of the Wolf
178.content: Ruins northeast of the city of an ancient temple. The Arcadians built it for Istaroth; the Gunnhildr Clan prayed to her here during the Archon War and were answered by the wind spirit who became Barbatos, who also met Istaroth here and received fragments of her power. Rebuilt for both gods, later a slaves' arena, now abandoned. The nearby Temple of the Wolf was an ancient civilisation's training ground, a trial domain today.

179.content: A cliff in Starfell Valley with a Time Trial Challenge and, at night, the NPCs Marla, Marvin and Sharp. The Mondstadt entry describes it as a quiet place where Venti has met the Traveler.

180.content: A natural freshwater lake so clear its bottom shows, with waters that never freeze. Official text credits its headwaters with making Mondstadt's ciders and wines famous and the lake a symbol of the nation. Mondstadt City stands on a large island in it.

181.content:
Starglow Cavern: Starglow Cavern is a great, icy cave in the depths of Dragonspine. Strange blue plants called Starglow light even its darkest passages, and before the quest In the Mountains it held one of the three shards of the Skyfrost Nail.

The 1.2 preview text calls it a cavern spanning the depths of the mountain, where peculiar glowing vegetation lights every passage with a cold glow.

Geography: A wide cave system in the heart of Dragonspine. Starglow plants blanket the interior; Ancient Rime, Scarlet Quartz, Warming Seelie, rock piles and an Infusion Stone are found inside.

Its place in the mountain is tied to the story of Sal Vindagnyr: the Skyfrost Nail that fell on the summit later split into three pieces, and one of them lay here. See the Dragonspine and Skyfrost Nail entries for the rest.

Dangers: Cryo hilichurls (shooters, grenadiers, shield guards, a Cryo Samachurl), an Ice Shieldwall Mitachurl, and a Ruin Grader, a large ancient construct, guard the cave. The cold is as severe as elsewhere on Dragonspine.

Atmosphere: Darkness softened by blue light from the plants, with ice all around and warmth scarce.

Quests: Linked to the world quest In the Mountains (version 1.2); before it, the cavern contained one Skyfrost Nail shard.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 canon adds nothing new about the cavern; it remains an explorable cave on Dragonspine.

182.content:
Starsnatch Cliff (also: Star-Plucking Cliff): Starsnatch Cliff is a scenic cliff in Starfell Valley, Mondstadt, with a wide view of the night sky. At night the secret couple Marla and Marvin meet here. The Midsummer Courtyard domain, an ancient ruin, lies beside it. In the Prologue it is where Venti, Jean, Diluc and the Traveler gathered before purifying the dragon Stormterror.

The name speaks of plucking stars from the sky. The top of the cliff is a recognised spot for viewing the night sky.

Geography: A cliff in the Starfell Valley subarea. Cecilia flowers are the local specialty, and a Time Trial Challenge is run in the area.

The Midsummer Courtyard domain lies next to the cliff, in the same subarea. Its buried garden is the remnant of an ancient lost civilisation that the wiki links to Arcadia.

Places: The summit, where the lovers sit at night, and the Midsummer Courtyard, an ancient blessed altar filled with Pyro-fearing monsters whose trial grants artifacts. Its description says the once magnificent Sommernachtgarten ("midsummer night garden") was buried when the ancient civilisation fell, leaving only ancient trees and stones.

People: From 19:00 to 06:00 three Mondstadt residents can be found here. Marla (a young woman who rests on a bench in Springvale by day) and Marvin Goth (son of Goth, general manager of the Goth Grand Hotel) are secretly in love because Goth is strict about whom his son may marry. Sharp, a mercenary called "Black Hound", was hired by Goth to guard Marvin; Marvin pays him to keep quiet, so he earns from both, and he picks flowers while he waits.

By day Marvin sleeps with his eyes open in the city, a ruse so he stays awake for the night. At the cliff the couple trade florid vows that keep tripping into awkward comparisons (ice at a spring's source, an eagle's talons) and correct themselves as they go. After the Stormterror crisis Marvin says a rock narrowly missing him showed him that Marla means the world to him. Canon shows only Goth's objection and never says what he decides.

Quests: Prologue Act II, "For a Tomorrow Without Tears", part 13, "Reunion With the Dragon": once Dvalin's tears had restored the Holy Lyre der Himmel, Diluc, Jean, Venti and the Traveler met here, ready to purify Stormterror. Venti called it a lovely place for a fated reunion and warned that a fight was coming.

In the hangout event "Gift and Intent" (Noelle, version 1.4) the Traveler must photograph the top of the cliff at night (19:00 to 24:00) to help Beatrice choose a gift; the resulting quest item, "Picture of Starsnatch Cliff", shows the night sky above it. Beatrice complains if people are already at the cliff, even when Marla and Marvin are out of frame.

Atmosphere: A hushed, windy ledge under a wide night sky: quiet by day, gently occupied at night, with the couple's whispered declarations and the bodyguard pacing nearby.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the cliff is unchanged: the lovers still meet here at night and the domain remains. No later story has altered it.

183.comment: Starsnatch Cliff: Marla, Marvin and Sharp
183.content: Marla and Marvin Goth are secret lovers who meet at Starsnatch Cliff every night; Marla naps on a bench in Springvale by day, and Marvin feigns sleep in Mondstadt City. His father Goth, manager of the Goth Grand Hotel, would not approve. The mercenary Sharp guards Marvin and keeps the secret for double pay. Their dialogue is comic: the couple speak in grand poetic metaphors and then correct them.

184.content: A domain beside Starsnatch Cliff holding an ancient blessed altar full of Pyro-fearing monsters; clearing it yields artifacts. In-world text says the Sommernachtgarten, once prosperous and magnificent, was buried when an ancient lost civilisation fell, leaving only ancient trees and stones.

185.content:
Stormbearer Mountains: The Stormbearer Mountains are the high country in the north of Starfell Valley, once a place to observe approaching storms. Now only an abandoned watchtower stands there, and monsters roam the slopes.

They lie next to Stormbearer Point on the coast, where the Traveler's journey begins.

Geography: High mountains in northern Starfell Valley with an old lookout tower, fishing spots, and Dandelion Seeds and valberries as local specialties. Anemograna, a Time Trial Challenge and Shrines of Depths are found here.

The merchants' road runs near enough that monsters here concern the Knights of Favonius.

People: No settlement stands here. The Knight Harry, posted at nearby Stormbearer Point, tracks monster camps along the merchants' road and hopes the evidence will persuade Acting Grand Master Jean to order a cleanup of the Stormbearer Mountains area, like the one Grand Master Varka ran in earlier days.

History: The mountains were once an observation post for incoming storms. Barbatos' winds have kept Mondstadt calm for generations, and the post fell out of use, leaving the abandoned watchtower.

Dangers: Many hilichurl camps of different elements, Samachurls, slimes, a Cryo Whopperflower, Blazing Axe Mitachurls, Ruin Guards, Cryo Abyss Mages and a Fatui Electro Cicin Mage; the Anemo Hypostasis is the area's boss enemy.

Travel: Gliding from high ground is the natural way to cross the highlands, and Knights warn travelers about monster camps along the merchants' route.

Status as of 7.1: Through 7.1 canon gives no change: still a monster-ridden highland with a derelict tower.

186.content:
Stormbearer Point: Stormbearer Point is a headland in Starfell Valley. The coast just south of it is where the Traveler begins their journey across Teyvat with Paimon. A Church of Favonius nun named Vind keeps a storm watch here, and a Knight named Harry patrols near the waypoint.

Ruin Guards, hilichurl camps and old ruins share the area with a calm shoreline, and Storm Barriers wall off some of its treasures.

Geography: A rocky point on the coast of Starfell Valley, with a lake, ruins and a hilichurl tower. It has a Time Trial Challenge and Storm Barriers, columns of wind that surround an object and vanish once it is reached, usually by gliding from height or with Anemograna. Valberries are a local specialty. The Stormbearer Mountains lie to the north.

People: Vind, a nun of the Church of Favonius known as the Storm Watcher, stands at the southeastern tip. Her family has kept watch for at least a thousand years at Vennessa's behest, ready to spread word of a storm across Mondstadt, but with Barbatos' gentle winds no true storm has come in generations. Harry, a Knight of Favonius, patrols near the waypoint, helps victims of monster attacks reach the city or Springvale, and gathers intelligence on monster camps along the merchants' road.

Vind is devoted to the point and takes her duty to extremes, once preparing to charge a watchtower overrun by hilichurls before the Traveler cleared it. Harry offers capable adventurers basic self-defence training and a sword. Neither is a major canon figure.

Dangers: Hilichurl shooters of several elements, Samachurls, slimes, a Wooden Shieldwall Mitachurl, Ruin Guards, a Cryo Abyss Mage and a Fatui Electro Cicin Mage.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing new is told about the point; the storm watch continues and the Traveler's early journey is the only story the area carries.

187.content:
Stormterror's Lair (also: Old Mondstadt, Dvalin's Lair, Abandoned Capital of Howling Winds): Stormterror's Lair is the ruin of Old Mondstadt, the capital that the tyrannical God of Storms, Decarabian, built in the Brightcrown Mountains of northwestern Mondstadt. A ring-shaped city surrounds his broken central tower. The city has been empty since his fall about 2,600 years ago. Later the wounded dragon Dvalin came here to rest, and the people of Mondstadt, who had forgotten him and feared him, called him "Stormterror", which gave the ruins their name. In the Prologue, the Traveler, Venti, Jean and Diluc fought their way to the top of the tower to free Dvalin from the Abyss Order's corruption.

The ruins remain deserted and wind-scoured. Old storm walls still block the gates, wind currents rise among the ruins, and monsters and Abyss Order agents sometimes gather there. Dvalin still returns at times, though he is not always present.

Geography: The ruins fill a deep valley in the Brightcrown Mountains, northwest of Mondstadt City. They are approached through Brightcrown Canyon, a pass once held by the King of Gales' soldiers and still guarded by ancient mechanisms. In the centre stands Decarabian's tower, broken but still standing. In 6.5 the area was extended northeast to connect with Millhaven in the newly opened Windrest Peak.

Alice's Teyvat Travel Guide describes the city as built in rings: every resident was assigned a place between an inner and an outer ring, with the King of Gales' tower in the middle. Alice blew up a few of the tower's arcades to make the climb easier, and remarked that the ruin felt more ancient for it. Calla lilies and windwheel asters grow among the stones.

Places: - **Decarabian's Tower**: the broken central spire from which the God of Storms ruled. Its uppermost chambers are where the Prologue's battle with Dvalin began.
- **The ring city**: concentric residential rings, ruined arcades and tall bridges in Decarabian's distinctive style.
- **Brightcrown Canyon and the entrance ruins**: the old approach road into the capital.

- **The first Field Tiller**: a dormant Ruin Guard on one of the tower's upper floors, the prototype from which all later Ruin Guards were copied.
- **Light actuators**: four light mechanisms, one at the top of the tower and three scattered among the ruins, which together opened the seal on the tower in the Prologue.
- **A mysterious camp** on top of a tall rock formation in the southwest, with a tent and a sword planted in front of it, guarded by Anemo slimes and an Eye of the Storm. Who made it is unknown.

History: Decarabian raised this city by his own divine power and walled it in storms against the blizzards of the north. He accepted worship from his tower, unaware that his people did not bow out of love. About 2,600 years ago they rose against him, and after his death the new Anemo Archon led them away to found today's Mondstadt City on Cider Lake. The capital was left empty. Five hundred years ago, during the cataclysm, Dvalin was badly wounded killing the Abyssal dragon Durin. He settled in the abandoned tower to recover, and slept there while the Abyssal poison tormented him and the people forgot him.

In the centuries after the city's fall, a badly damaged machine took refuge in the ruins. It was the first Field Tiller, which had fought Boreas in his proving ground. For about a year it fired on anyone approaching Old Mondstadt, and Mondstadters, who knew nothing of such machines, called it the "Tyrant's Final Fury", the dead storm god's last anger. Then it shut down. In modern times Alice explored the ruins for her travel guide and blew up several arcades.

Atmosphere: Grim and windswept: huge empty streets, toppled arcades and a broken tower ringed by howling wind. Visitors find it oddly sad even without knowing why. Its own descriptions call it a desolate city of "magical mechanisms and painful memories", haunted by winds that still tell a story no mortal remembers, of a nameless wind sprite and the chorus that made the tower tremble. For Venti it is also a peaceful lookout; during the 1.4 Windblume event he said that when he has nothing else to do he sometimes comes here just to sit and gaze.

Dangers: Storm walls and ancient seals bar parts of the ruins, and wind currents are needed to reach the upper tower. Hilichurl camps, slimes, Abyss Mages and other Abyss Order forces have occupied the ruins at times. The lowest floor of Decarabian's tower is too dangerous to enter. The expedition description warns that Stormterror made it a dangerous place, though bold adventurers still go there looking for treasure.

Quests: In **Song of the Dragon and Freedom** (Prologue Act III), killing an Abyss Mage frees Venti to sense how to dispel the wind barrier around the ruins. Hilichurls under Abyss Order direction try to stall the party at the entrance. Venti plays the barrier away, and the group climbs the tower to find it sealed. They light four light actuators, then fight Dvalin in the skies above and break the poisoned blood clots on his body. When the battlefield collapses Dvalin saves them, and he flies off reassured that no one is after him.

In **Bough Keeper: Dainsleif** (1.3), the Traveler and Dainsleif search the lair for an Abyss Herald and check the light actuators. Dainsleif remarks that the ruin has had little to do with the dragon for a long time and that he saw it before Dvalin ever fell. On a cliff above, the Traveler touches a dandelion trampled beside a Ruin Guard's footprint and senses their missing sibling.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Stormterror's Lair is a deserted ruin and a known landmark north of Mondstadt City. Dvalin, now reconciled with Mondstadt, comes and goes, and is often absent.

Since the opening of Windrest Peak (6.5), the ruins connect northeast to Millhaven, so the old capital now sits on a route between the capital's hinterland and the northern regions.

key: Tower of the King of Gales
188.content:
Decarabian's Tower is the broken central spire of Old Mondstadt, where the God of Storms lived and received worship. Its upper chambers are filled with howling wind and memories. In the Prologue the Traveler's party climbed it on wind currents to reach the sealed top, from which they went up to fight Dvalin. The first Field Tiller stands dormant on an upper floor.

Tiles and debris from the tower are said to keep some of the divine power that built the city. Alice deliberately blew up some of its arcades to make it easier to climb.

189.comment: Stormterror's Lair: Dvalin's Nest in the Ruins
189.content:
Dvalin, the Dragon of the East and one of the Four Winds, settled in the tower after the cataclysm to heal from Durin's poison, and slept there for centuries. When he woke, the people had forgotten him, and the Abyss Order took advantage of his pain and resentment. Mondstadters named his roost Stormterror's Lair. After the Prologue he was freed from the corruption and reconciled with Venti and the city.

During the Invitation of Windblume event (1.4), Venti brought the Traveler here to clear away monsters as a Windblume gift for Dvalin. He explained that "Windblume" began as a secret code word for resistance in Old Mondstadt, and Dvalin flew overhead.

190.comment: Stormterror's Lair: The Tyrant's Final Fury
190.content: In the Church's old story, a bombardment once struck anyone approaching Old Mondstadt and was blamed on the dead Decarabian's wrath. It was really the first Field Tiller, the original Khaenri'ahn Ruin Guard. Boreas had badly damaged it, and it lay crippled in the ruins, firing missiles for about a year before it went still. In 1.4 Dainsleif took its eye, which the Abyss Order had planned to use.

191.comment: Stormterror's Lair: Durin's Visit to Stormterror's Lair
191.content: In Durin's story quest Fate's Accursed Wiles (6.2), a clue from Alice's storybook about a castle where a dragon dwells leads Durin and the Traveler to the lair. Through the old battle site atop the tower, they enter the book's story-world. Durin hoped to meet Dvalin there but did not. As they left, Venti and Dvalin watched from a nearby cliff, and Venti said Durin wanted to be friends but that the moment had not yet come.

192.content:
Symbol of Mondstadt's Hero (also: Mondstadt's Hero Oak, Vennessa's oak): The Symbol of Mondstadt's Hero is the enormous oak tree at Windrise in Galesong Hill. Mondstadt believes it grew after the hero Vennessa ascended to Celestia about a thousand years ago. A Statue of the Seven stands under its branches.

It is a landmark of the city's founding-era story of rebellion against the aristocracy, and also somewhere the Anemo Archon Venti is known to come to rest.

History: Roughly a thousand years ago Vennessa led the revolt that overthrew Mondstadt's corrupt aristocracy and became known as the city's hero. Legend says she ascended to Celestia as a reward at the end of her life, and the towering oak is believed to have risen at the spot where she left. This is the tradition as told in Mondstadt; canon does not independently confirm that the tree grew because of her.

The wiki's page cites a historian NPC, Dr. Edith, for this account. The tree's name is a title given to it by the people of Mondstadt rather than the name of a person.

Quests: In the opening Archon Quest, after the Traveler's presence purifies Dvalin's teardrop, Venti thinks of "a friend so dear" and runs off to this tree. The Traveler finds him sitting in its branches, where he says he can feel the Abyssal poison that passed into him leaving his body. Later, after Signora tears his Gnosis away and Barbara's healing has no effect, he returns to the tree to recover.

Atmosphere: A broad plain washed by a constant breeze, with the great oak towering over it and a Statue of the Seven beneath. It suits quiet, reverent or restorative scenes.

193.comment: Symbol of Mondstadt's Hero: Vennessa and the great oak
193.content: Mondstadt tradition holds that the oak at Windrise grew where the hero Vennessa ascended to Celestia about a thousand years ago, after she led the rebellion against the aristocracy. This is presented as belief and legend.

194.content:
Taste of the North: Taste of the North is a restaurant in Dornman Port, owned by Frith, who is said to come from Nod-Krai. It sells simple Mondstadt food and cooking ingredients, and first appeared in Version 6.5. The name is the wiki's unofficial label.

Frith says she is just an ordinary restaurant owner. She does not cook the food herself, since the restaurant has its own cook.

Places: A single restaurant in the port. In gameplay terms the food restocks daily and the ingredients weekly; the menu includes a Harbor Fish Burger.

People: Frith is the owner. Her idle line is the invitation 'A taste of the north - who wants to try?'. The wiki also lists Yangzhen among the people there.

Lohen, a diner there, says the dishes are common Mondstadt staples, that word is she is from Nod-Krai and no ordinary civilian, and that he and others kept an eye on her for a while; it seems she wants to run an honest restaurant in Mondstadt.

History: Frith asks the Traveler to cook Lohikeitto, a Nod-Krai soup, because a guest wanted to taste the past and she has started to forget what it tasted like. When the Traveler hands one over she delivers it and thanks them.

Afterwards Lohen says the Lohikeitto he was served was flawless, though later visits never match it. He wonders aloud whether the restaurant hired a new chef.

Atmosphere: A harbour-side dining room with a quiet owner whose past seems wider than her menu.

Travel: In Dornman Port, Windrest Peak. Reaching it requires the northern area of Mondstadt added in Version 6.5.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

key: Temple of the Falcon of the West
Deep Within the Temple of the Falcon
195.content:
Temple of the Falcon (also: Falcon Temple, Temple of the Falcon of the West, Deep Within the Temple of the Falcon, Abyssal Traces): The Temple of the Falcon is a ruined temple at Windrise in Galesong Hill, between Mondstadt City and the great oak where Vennessa is said to have ascended. It was devoted to the Falcon of the West, one of the Four Winds, and has been abandoned for centuries. Its in-game description says it has watched over Windrise for thousands of years, and that perhaps the winds of the past still linger in its halls.

It is one of three Four Winds temples the Traveler clears in the Prologue, with Amber as companion. Strong winds fill its underground corridors. Much later the Abyss Order is found to have re-infiltrated it.

Geography: The temple stands at Windrise in Galesong Hill. Though the structure lies deep underground, wind currents run through every corridor, and glider updrafts carry visitors between rooms. Inside are sealed doors, pressure mechanisms and Doors of Resurrection, with chests tucked away in side chambers.

The entrance sits between Mondstadt City and the Windrise oak. Hilichurl camps and monsters have taken over the ruined halls; gameplay describes the interior as a one-time domain.

History: After Vennessa's revolution a thousand years ago the Four Winds were formally established, and for roughly five hundred years Mondstadters built temples to them. After the cataclysm that worship faded; the temples were left to ruin and nearly forgotten. By the Prologue, Amber says the Mondstadters almost never visit them.

Because the Falcon's identity is disputed (see uncertainties), the temple does not settle whom it honoured: it names the Falcon of the West and little more. The domain text calls it a temple of the "benevolent" Falcon.

Quests: In "Winds of the Past" (Prologue Act I), Stormterror's attack on Mondstadt has left elemental flows in the old Four Winds temples. Amber waits at the Temple of the Falcon, joins as a trial character in the story domain "Deep Within the Temple of the Falcon", and helps destroy a crystal Stormterror is using to draw power. Amber remarks that even Stormterror has abandoned "its own temple". Clearing the third such temple clears the skies; the Traveler also finds an Anemoculus in one of them.

During the world quest "Bough Keeper: Dainsleif", Dainsleif says that the Abyss Order has re-infiltrated the temple and leads the Traveler back to it. The story domain "Abyssal Traces" there has the Traveler fight through monster-filled rooms looking for traces of the Abyss Herald; once the monsters are beaten, the search moves on to Wolvendom. Standing at the temple, Dainsleif muses on the Falcon of the West in a cryptic aside about something that can soar on the wind but merely hovers under the gods' light; he names nobody.

Dangers: Hilichurls, slimes and Abyss Mages (including a Pyro Abyss Mage in the Abyssal Traces domain) occupy the rooms. As a gameplay note, the one-time domain "Explore: Windy Cliff" is recommended at Adventure Rank 12.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an abandoned, little-visited ruin at Windrise, its story domains complete and its one-time domain enterable.

Nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes it.

196.comment: Temple of the Falcon: Falcon of the West
196.content: The Falcon of the West is the fourth of Mondstadt's Four Winds. Common belief holds it is Vennessa after her ascension, and the Knights of Favonius are sometimes called the Falcon collectively; canon never settles it. The Temple of the Falcon at Windrise is the only Falcon shrine shown in-game.

key: Temple of the Lion of the South
Deep Within the Temple of the Lion
197.content:
Temple of the Lion (also: Lion Temple, Temple of the Lion of the South, Deep Within the Temple of the Lion): The Temple of the Lion is a ruined temple on Falcon Coast in Galesong Hill, devoted to the Lion of the South, one of the Four Winds. It has long been abandoned, and its ruins show signs of monster activity. Folklore holds that the dandelions seen riding the winds across Mondstadt symbolise the Lion's blessing.

In the Prologue the Traveler clears it with Lisa, the Librarian, while Knights of Favonius work to contain the dragon Stormterror.

Geography: It stands on Falcon Coast, the shoreline of Galesong Hill. Inside, wind currents carry visitors between rooms, with Doors of Resurrection, consoles and Electro monuments guarding the way and chests hidden behind crates.

Gameplay notes: the one-time domain "Investigate: Secret Hideout" is recommended at Adventure Rank 18 with Electro, and Elemental Trials become available here at Adventure Rank 16.

History: Like the other Four Winds temples, it dates from the centuries after Vennessa's revolution when Mondstadters worshipped the Four Winds. After the cataclysm the worship faded and the temple was abandoned. Canon gives no precise founding date.

Quests: In "Sparks Amongst the Pages" (Prologue Act I), Lisa meets the Traveler at the temple and joins as a trial character in the story domain "Deep Within the Temple of the Lion". She senses strong elemental energy deeper within; the pair destroy Stormterror's crystal, a source of the dragon's power.

After the crystal is destroyed Lisa names the Four Winds (Dragon of the East, Lion of the South, Wolf of the North, Falcon of the West) as guardians tied to Barbatos, and says the Dragon, whose true name is Dvalin, can channel only three of the four winds' power. She attributes this to hatred of Mondstadt and hands over a very old book, Breeze Amidst the Forest Supplement: The Dragon Tome, for the full story. Paimon notes that clearing the third temple clears the sky.

Dangers: Slimes, hilichurl fighters and shooters, and in the repeatable domain Abyss Mages (Hydro and Cryo) and slimes. The wiki describes the one-time domain as requiring the player to kill slimes in quick succession.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 an abandoned ruin on Falcon Coast; its story domain is complete and its one-time domain and Elemental Trials remain available.

198.comment: Temple of the Lion: Lion of the South
198.content: The Lion of the South is the Four Winds guardian whose title is, by Knights tradition, passed to Grand Masters and Acting Grand Masters as the Dandelion or Lionfang Knight; Jean holds it now. The temple's own text associates the Lion with dandelions carried on the wind. The title's exact scope is not settled in canon.

key: Temple of the Wolf of the North
Deep Within the Temple of the Wolf
199.content:
Temple of the Wolf (also: Wolf Temple, Temple of the Wolf of the North, Deep Within the Temple of the Wolf): The Temple of the Wolf is a ruined temple of the Four Winds near the Thousand Winds Temple in Starfell Valley, devoted to the Wolf of the North. The priests are gone and monsters have seized it, though the spirit of the Wolf is said still to watch over Mondstadt's fields from elsewhere. Its depths are described as a destroyed ancient training ground.

In the Prologue the Traveler clears it with Kaeya, Captain of the Cavalry, as part of the Knights' effort to stop the dragon Stormterror.

Geography: It lies in Starfell Valley beside the Thousand Winds Temple. Hilichurls and Pyro slimes hold the approach. Inside are Doors of Resurrection, flamethrower and water-and-spike traps, wind currents and elemental trials leading to the training-ground chambers.

Gameplay notes: the one-time domain "Trial: Scorching Fire and Raging Lightning" is recommended at Adventure Rank 15 with Pyro and Electro, and the player chooses between Hydro, Electro and Pyro trials.

History: The Four Winds were formally established after Vennessa's revolution a thousand years ago, and for roughly five hundred years Mondstadters built temples to them. The Wolf's temple was originally a training ground. After the cataclysm the worship faded and the temples were abandoned. At some point Boreas and his wolves moved west and settled in Wolvendom.

The temple's text says only that the Wolf's spirit still watches over Mondstadt; the Wolf's later home in Wolvendom is described in the Mondstadt entry.

Quests: In "Crash Course" (Prologue Act I), Kaeya meets the Traveler at the Thousand Winds Temple and joins as a trial character in the story domain "Deep Within the Temple of the Wolf". He says the temples must be cleared for the Four Winds, and that Stormterror was once one of them, referring the Traveler to the Acting Grand Master for the story. After Stormterror's crystal is destroyed he praises the Traveler's fighting.

Afterwards Kaeya stays behind alone. A cutscene shows him reasoning that hilichurls could not have organised the ambush themselves; a Hydro Abyss Mage reveals itself and is killed by an unidentified red-haired man who calls the Knights inefficient. Kaeya replies that his involvement makes things more interesting.

Dangers: Hilichurls, Pyro slimes, Hydro and Electro foes, and the temple's flame and water traps.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an abandoned ruin; its story domain is complete and its one-time domain remains enterable.

200.comment: Temple of the Wolf: Wolf of the North
200.content: Canon gives two possible bearers of the Wolf of the North: Boreas (Andrius), the Great Wolf King now a spirit in Wolvendom, and the current Knight of Boreas in the Knights' tradition (Varka). The temple does not decide between them.

201.content:
The Cat's Tail (also: Cat's Tail, Cats Tail): The Cat's Tail is a tavern in Mondstadt City, owned by Margaret and known for its cats and for Diona, its young bartender whose cocktails taste wonderful whatever goes into them. It sits between the Adventurers' Guild post and the Good Hunter restaurant, and is where Mondstadt's Genius Invokation TCG players meet.

It is the rival of Angel's Share, which belongs to the Dawn Winery. Since Diona was hired it has done a roaring trade, though Angel's Share is still said to sell more.

People: Margaret hired Diona for a simple reason: she is cute, despite being too young to drink alcohol herself. Margaret owns several cats, including Prince and Butterfly, and enjoys writing witty replies to messages on the Cat's Tail Message Board, which has become a sort of advice board. After the TCG took off at the tavern, Prince, assisted by a woman named Shuyun, helps patrons who come to play.

Diona, a cat-eared young woman from Springvale, openly hates alcohol and sees herself as the "Wine Industry Slayer", set on inventing the worst drink in the world. Every attempt turns out delicious, to her fury. In a message-board exchange Margaret answered Diluc's wistful note kindly and welcomed him despite their rivalry. A set of regular guests are drawn to the tavern's tables each day, plus a rotating weekly guest who may be a familiar character.

Atmosphere: A relaxed place to put your feet up for an afternoon or evening, with cats on the counter and drinks that are far better than their bartender wants. The official description teases that guests should be careful not to praise the bartender's skills. It also serves pizza, which is Jean's favourite when she has time to order one.

The building has a main room, two smaller rooms and a second floor. After the world quest "A Guest From Liyue" the tavern's invitation board is upgraded, by Tubby using Adeptus arts, into an Invitation Duel Room where invited characters come to duel the player.

History: Before Diona the Dawn Winery's Angel's Share dominated Mondstadt's wine trade. Her arrival made the Cat's Tail a challenger overnight. Elzer, the winery's butler, tried to headhunt her for Angel's Share and was bitten.

The tavern became the TCG hub in 3.3. In the world quest "Come Try Genius Invokation TCG!" the scholar Timaeus tells the Traveler that the community goes there to play, and Margaret, Diona and Shuyun teach the rules and arrange the first duels, including one against Fischl.

Quests: "Come Try Genius Invokation TCG!" (3.3) opens the tavern's interior to the player. "Margaret's Longing" is a quest in which Prince steals Venti's lyre strings. "Master's Day Off" is a quest after which Margaret thanks the Traveler for help with her cat.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tavern is open and the TCG hub of Mondstadt; no later content changes that.

202.content: Margaret is the proud owner of the Cat's Tail, shoulder-length blonde hair, a red and white dress and a brown hat. By day she wanders the fountain plaza. She is a little simplistic at times, quick with jokes, calls Mondstadt "a city of romance", and is fond of her cats.

203.comment: The Cat's Tail: Prince the Cat
203.content: Prince is a black cat belonging to Margaret, who calls him a mischievous little rascal while spoiling him. He loves fish and playing with string and has keen senses. He serves as the tavern's shopkeeper and TCG helper.

key: Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind
204.comment: Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind
204.content:
Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind: Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind is a Domain of Blessing in Windrest Peak, northern Mondstadt, added in version 6.6. Its description calls it a floral realm hidden amid the mountains, seldom visited because it is remote. Its lore blurb recalls Elysium, an ancient city-state whose people believed it, sealed in its coffin, would outlast corruption and flourish like a sacred forest.

Only poetry and blooming flowers remain in the wind; the dream of Elysium, the text says, will not return.

Geography: Set among the mountains of Windrest Peak, a hidden garden-like realm. The blurb places it in the era when the thousand winds could still brush the Temple of Space.

The wiki lists the area only generally; no exact landmark is given.

History: The entrance text ties the place to Elysium, an Arcadian city-state in these mountains. Its people trusted that the sealed city would resist destruction from outside, but, the text says, all things wax and wane and that dream is gone.

Elysium and the Temple of Space are covered in the Mondstadt nation entry and their own entries.

Dangers: Defenders include Mitachurls, a Hydro Hilichurl Rogue, a Stonehide Lawachurl, a Ruin Drake: Earthguard and Domain Keepers. Its ley line disorder rewards Normal and Charged Attacks with a stacking damage bonus.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the domain is open; it was added in 6.6 and no later content changes it.

205.content:
Thousand Winds Temple (also: Ancient Thousand Winds Temple): The Thousand Winds Temple is a ruined temple and amphitheater in Starfell Valley. The Arcadians built it to worship Istaroth, Ruler of Time; later it served both Istaroth and Barbatos, and in the aristocratic age it became an arena where slaves fought for the nobles' amusement. It is also where the future Anemo Archon, then a small wind spirit, was first answered.

The official map text calls it a long-forgotten commemorative site, carved with the maxim that wind brings the seeds of tales and time lets them take root.

Geography: A collection of temple ruins northeast of Mondstadt. Pillars still bear faint elegant carvings. A large sundial east of the Temple of the Wolf carries an inscription about seeds of stories brought by the wind. Hilichurls, slimes and a Cryo Regisvine roam the site, with Ruin Guards and Abyss mages among its tougher inhabitants.

Dandelion Seed grows here. NPCs around the ruins include Patchi the Curious (a researcher), Doolan and Henry Morton.

History: Arcadians built the temple for Istaroth. When Arcadia fell, it was left in ruins. During the Archon War the Gunnhildr Clan settled among the ruins, seeking help against the blizzards of Decarabian and Boreas' conflict, and raised a small shrine to Istaroth. Their prayers were answered by a small wind spirit, who became Barbatos.

Venti has said that as a wind spirit he met Istaroth here by chance and she entrusted him with fragments of her power and authority (told during the limited-time Sunspray Summer Resort event, 5.8). Once he ascended as Anemo Archon, the temple was rebuilt for worship of both gods, and the Sacrificial weapons were used as ceremonial implements in its rites. Istaroth was later forgotten, leaving only Barbatos worshipped.

People: Patchi the Curious (a researcher), Doolan and Henry Morton can be met around the site.

Atmosphere: Weathered stone tiers around a wide floor, wind-bent grass and half-lost carvings: a place that has had three different meanings and kept the marks of all of them.

Dangers: Hilichurl and mitachurl camps, Ruin Guards, Cryo Abyss mages and a Cryo Regisvine.

Status as of 7.1: A ruin as of 7.1, still visited by researchers.

206.comment: Thousand Winds Temple: Istaroth's shrine and Barbatos
206.content: Gunnhildr's clan built a small shrine to Istaroth here and prayed for protection from blizzards. A weak wind spirit answered, the future Barbatos. After his ascension the place honoured both gods; Istaroth's worship faded.

207.comment: Thousand Winds Temple: Istaroth's gift to young Barbatos
207.content: During the Sunspray Summer Resort event (quest A Curtain Call for a Colorful Summer Night!, 5.8), Venti tells the Traveler that, as an Anemo spirit, he once met Istaroth ('Time') by chance at the Thousand Winds Temple and, hearing his wishes, she entrusted him with fragments of her power and authority. This comes from an event quest and is Venti's own account; few know it.

208.content:
Valley of Remembrance (also: Dance of Steel): The Valley of Remembrance is a Domain of Blessing between Dawn Winery and Dragonspine in Mondstadt. Its entrance text says that after a time the continent's people lost track of the past and dug downward to find what they had forgotten; beyond an ancient tree's hollow, yesterday's secrets became today's treasures. It is an altar full of monsters that fear brute force, and clearing it rewards artifacts.

Its trial levels are all titled "Dance of Steel", apparently a nod to its Physical damage bonus.

Geography: Located in Windwail Highland in the Dawn Winery area, toward the slopes of Dragonspine; the entrance blurb mentions the hollow of an ancient tree.

The ley line disorder raises the party's Physical damage, and higher levels weaken enemies' Physical resistance.

History: Canon says nothing specific beyond the entrance blurb: forgotten history, dug up and turned into treasure.

Dangers: Treasure Hoarders of many kinds (Potioneers, Handymen, Pugilists, Gravediggers, Seamen), Fatui Pyro Agents and Electro Cicin Mages.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the domain is open and unchanged since 1.0.

209.content:
Whispering Woods (also: Whispering Forest): The Whispering Woods are dense, deep woods in Starfell Valley, near Starfell Lake and Mondstadt City, cut by a small road. Wind in the leaves sounds like whispers, hence the name. In the Prologue the Traveler first sees Venti, then just a boy, calming the dragon Dvalin here.

Hilichurls and slimes roam the area, and dandelion seeds and small lamp grass grow here.

Geography: A forest at the far end of Starfell Valley, close to Starfell Lake and the city, with a small road running through the trees. The wiki catalogues its own set of points of interest within it.

Starfell Valley is described as stretching from Stormbearer Point to the ends of the Whispering Woods, which makes the woods the valley's wooded edge.

History: The in-game expedition text explains the name: travellers kept mistaking the fluttering sound of wind-blown leaves for whispers, so they began calling the place the Whispering Woods.

Dangers: Hilichurls (ordinary Hilichurls, Fighters and Berserkers) and Hydro and Pyro Slimes.

In the Prologue the area is an early combat test. After the Traveler and Paimon leave the forest, the Knights' Outrider Amber stops them and the three clear a nearby hilichurl camp.

Atmosphere: Dim green shade, leaves rustling in constant gusts and a narrow road, with the sense that the wind itself is murmuring.

Quests: Prologue Act I, "Forest Rendezvous": the Traveler and Paimon saw a dragon fly toward the heart of the forest and followed it. There they came across a boy talking gently to the dragon, telling it not to be afraid and that he was back. When he noticed them, the dragon roared and the boy vanished in a burst of Anemo; the dragon flew away. A crimson crystal was left on a rock, which the Traveler took.

This is the first meeting with Venti and Dvalin, though neither is named yet. The dragon soon becomes "Stormterror" to Mondstadters when it begins to rampage. The soundtrack piece "Reunion in the Whispering Woods" accompanies this cutscene and the later Prologue meeting before Dvalin is purified.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the woods are unchanged; no later story has used them.

210.comment: Whispering Woods: First Sighting of Venti and Dvalin
210.content: In the heart of the Whispering Woods the Traveler and Paimon watched a boy (Venti) speak to a dragon (Dvalin) before the dragon sensed them and both fled, leaving behind a crimson crystal. Nobody yet knew the boy was the Anemo Archon, and Paimon only called him a weirdo.

211.content:
Windrest Peak: Windrest Peak is the northernmost part of Mondstadt, opened in Version 6.5, and revolves around the port town of Dornman Port, one of the continent's major trade hubs. It also holds Millhaven, an idyllic windmill village of windrest-flower fields and fragrance makers, and the Old Sanatorium Site, where a hilltop sanatorium once stood. High above the peak floats the Temple of Space. The weather is clearer and more varied than in the rest of Mondstadt.

Long ago the Arcadian city-state of Elysium stood in these mountains under the Gunnhildr Clan, and the area later became that clan's fief. The Knights of Favonius keep a base at the port.

Geography: Mountain country north of Cider Lake, running down to a harbour. Dornman Port sits on the coast, Millhaven in its fields inland, and the Old Sanatorium Site on a hill above. Local plants include calla lily, dandelion seed, etherwing moth, valberry and windwheel aster. Unlike the south, it has varied clouds and clearer skies.

The Temple of Space is a separate area in the sky above, with its own map tab; the wiki says the mountain breezes here are fierce because, by decree of the temple's owner, no wind may enter it. A Time Trial Challenge lies at ruins just north of Dornman Port. The Knights of Favonius Ruins lie underground beneath the port.

Places: Dornman Port (the harbour, bazaar, taverns and a Knights base); Millhaven; the Old Sanatorium Site; the Knights of Favonius Ruins beneath the port; the Temple of Space overhead; the Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind domain.

Dornman Port has a bulletin board, a ducks-feeding spot and Millhaven has its own bulletin board and a set of Dodoco doodles. The Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind (added in Version 6.6) is a hidden floral domain in the mountains, whose text mourns the "dream of Elysium", the city-state sealed in its coffin.

People: Dornman Port: sailors, merchants and Knights of Favonius, among them Vice Captain Lohen, stationed there. Millhaven: fragrance-makers; a young self-styled Witch Hunter, Prune, has posted a notice on a board. Old Sanatorium Site: the doorman Mann, who oversees demolition and heritage preservation. Henry Morton and Liben are Dornman Port NPCs.

Local legends of the area include the monster Churldric, and a normal boss, The Open-Eyed, roams it.

Governance: Dornman Port belonged to the Gunnhildr Clan as a hereditary fief in the aristocratic era. Today the Knights of Favonius keep order from a base at the port; their Reconnaissance Company patrols the trade road to the capital. Docking legally requires an entry permit.

After Vennessa's rebellion the Gunnhildr Clan, which sided with the people, led the push to abolish hereditary fiefs and likely set an example by handing its own over to Mondstadt.

Culture: A cosmopolitan port that welcomes steady merchant shipping from many nations; known for cargo shipping and flower cultivation, with taverns where sailors drink. Millhaven is peaceful and sweet-scented, its economy tied to windrest flowers and fragrances. Dornman Port has had no church since the late aristocratic era.

Nobody is quite sure how the port got its name. A trade route to Port Ormos in Sumeru has opened, and a company in the port plans to export fruit that others doubt will survive the voyage. A saying about the sanatorium holds that anyone who visits it stays among the enchanted hills for ever.

History: In the age of Great Arcadia, the city-state of Elysium stood in these mountains under the Gunnhildr Clan. After Arcadia fell the Gunnhildrs took refuge in Decarabian's city; once Barbatos scattered the snow they returned north, and the land became their fief and, in time, Dornman Port, with Mondstadt's very first sacred sanctuary to Barbatos. Later, in the dark age of the aristocracy, they threw a bishop sent from the capital out of the sanctuary's tower and tore it down to signal a break with the tyrannical Imunlaukr Clan; the port has had no church since.

During the Cataclysm 500 years ago the port stood on the brink of destruction, and many knights died defending it; their graves lie beneath the city in what is now the Knights of Favonius Ruins, which the wiki calls an ancient battlefield where the Knights fought the Abyss. More recently the Knights' Reconnaissance Company traced a hidden Abyss Order cargo to the port, where it was about to be shipped to Liyue Harbor; the scholar Yanfei, unwitting consultant to the ship, was caught up in it and Eula helped her capture the Abyss operatives nearby.

Atmosphere: Ships and cargo at the port, tavern noise, clouds driven across the hills, and the sweet smell of windrest flowers around Millhaven. Its viewpoint is titled The Harbor Where a Thousand Winds Converge, and the area's own, The Northerly Wind's Soft Hymn.

Dangers: Smuggling and Abyss Order activity at the port, and the wind-swept heights themselves.

The Temple of Space is dangerous in its own right: the Watchers Nihilita and Melanta and various Segment-Domain Keepers enforce the owner's rules inside.

Travel: Reached overland north of Cider Lake or by sea. The port is far from the capital; the Reconnaissance Company patrols the trade road in between, especially during Weinlesefest. The Old Sanatorium Site has a map marker through which the Temple of Space can be entered once the world quest series A Long Day in the Mountains has begun.

Quests: World quest series: A Long Day in the Mountains (6.5), set in Mondstadt and the Temple of Space, which draws on Thomas Mann's novel The Magic Mountain; and the Knights of Favonius Ruins quest Winds Beneath the Tower of Silence.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Windrest Peak is open, busy and calm; no 7.0-7.1 event is recorded in the pages read.

The Temple of Space remains hanging above the peak, and the old sanatorium on the hill has been demolished. The Knights keep a base at the port, where Lohen has been stationed.

212.content: A bustling harbour town north of Cider Lake and one of the continent's major trade hubs, welcoming merchant ships from many nations. Once the Gunnhildr Clan's fief, with Mondstadt's first sanctuary of Barbatos (since torn down, so no church remains). Famous for cargo shipping and flower cultivation. Mona was born here; the Reconnaissance Company patrols the road between port and capital. Some say the port is named for the Thorn King, a ruler lost to history, others for an ancestor of the Gunnhildrs, others for a madman in a crown of thorns.

213.content: A peaceful windmill village known for its fields of windrest flowers and its fragrance products. A notice on the village board by the self-styled Witch Hunter Prune accuses a witch codenamed "A" of bullying; replies tell the writer to go to Jean about a lost pet, and one thinks the target sounds like Alice. Doodles of Dodoco bombs around the village involve Klee.

214.content: A hilltop site where a sanatorium was torn down a few years ago. It had been built on the ruins left when the Temple of Space was lifted into the sky. Its doorman Mann oversees demolition and heritage preservation. Notes left behind show patients swapping a burial plot and offering free tombstone-carving; a gravestone reads "One lifetime doesn't count." The place is the map marker entrance to the Temple of Space, after A Long Day in the Mountains begins.

215.content:
Created by Asmoday, Ruler of Space, as Segment-Domain Tau, an exhibition hall preserving records of fallen civilisations (Hyperborea, Lang-Gan, Delphi Pytho, Ochkanatlan, Remuria and Arcadia) in books, paintings, landscapes and selected individuals called the Uplifted. Long ago it adjoined the temple where Arcadian survivors worshipped Istaroth, "mother of the thousand winds"; after an unknown disaster it was lifted into the sky and hidden, leaving Istaroth's temple behind to decay. Its Watchers Nihilita and Melanta enforce the decree that the temple exist only to preserve, with innovation forbidden. Time stands still inside.

The temple has three exhibition areas: Luyang Academy (painting, inspired by ancient Liyue), the Mahavaipulya Chamber (books) and the Desert Pavilion (modelled on Sumeru's desert temples). The Uplifted go through the Apathic Interval, giving up desire to leave it, and may leave the temple only by building the Path to the Heavens across the Corridor of Nothingness, which costs all their memories and wisdom. Wind is forbidden within, so it lingers in the mountains outside.

216.content:
Windrise: Windrise is a plain of everlasting breeze in Galesong Hill, in Mondstadt's countryside near the sea. A giant oak, the Symbol of Mondstadt's Hero, dominates it. According to legend the tree grew where the hero Vennessa, first Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, ascended to Celestia about a thousand years ago. A Statue of the Seven stands beneath its branches, and locals treat the place with quiet reverence.

Official text calls it a valley of winds in which the oak's shade shelters the statue from rain and wind, as Vennessa once sheltered Mondstadt. The spot is also where Venti, the bard who is the Anemo Archon Barbatos, goes to recover when he is hurt.

Geography: Open grassland on the Galesong Hill side of Mondstadt, facing the sea, with the oak at its centre. Falcon Coast runs east from Windrise to the water, and the underground ruin of the Temple of the Falcon lies within the area. Windwheel asters are the local specialty; there is a fishing point and a ruin torch, and an Elemental Monument stands among the grass.

Windrise and Falcon Coast, together with Cape Oath, enclose the bay east of Mondstadt City; from the drop of Cape Oath's headland the plain and its tree are easy to see.

Places: The Symbol of Mondstadt's Hero, the oak itself, is the heart of the area; the Statue of the Seven beneath it stands in its shade. The Temple of the Falcon is an old ruin said to have been devoted to the Falcon of the West; its depths are windy.

The Temple of the Falcon is entered as a domain and holds a one-time exploration challenge and story-quest areas. Its own description claims it has watched over Windrise for thousands of years, which does not obviously match a hero from about 1,000 years ago, so treat the temple's age as unsettled.

People: Dr. Edith, a historian and folklore researcher, is usually found by the statue by day collecting material for a new book; she loves telling Vennessa's story and is the source of the Windrise oak legend. Chloris runs a small stall selling flowers and berries that Floral Whisper does not stock; she is the elder sister of Flora, who owns that shop. Godwin, a Knight of Favonius, patrols the path near the Temple of the Falcon and, per the wiki, belongs to the elite group under the Grand Master.

Children from Falcon Coast want to come here to play with Dr. Edith (see Falcon Coast). Dr. Edith says she has collected far more stories and ballads about the tree than she could recount quickly.

History: Vennessa, a Muratan gladiator who led the rebellion that ended the Mondstadt aristocracy about 1,000 years ago and founded the Knights of Favonius, is said to have ascended to Celestia at this spot, taking the form of a falcon and becoming the Falcon of the West of the Four Winds. The oak is believed to have grown after her ascension; Dr. Edith says it appeared the same year she left.

In the Prologue, after the Traveler purifies Dvalin's tear, Venti hurries to the tree and says the Abyssal poison he absorbed is easing. Later, when Signora has torn out his Gnosis and Barbara's healing does nothing, he returns to the tree to recover, since a body made with an Archon's power cannot be mended by ordinary means. In a world quest, Dr. Edith asks for oak leaves to study the wind; they turn out to carry Anemo energy.

Atmosphere: Constant gentle wind, long grass and the sound of leaves, with the sea nearby. It feels like a memorial more than a settlement: people come to rest, to read, or to be alone.

Dangers: Mostly mild: hilichurl fighters, shooters and shield guards, and Cryo, Dendro, Hydro and Pyro slimes. A Knight of Favonius patrols the path.

Travel: Reached overland from Mondstadt City; the oak is visible from far off and the Statue of the Seven is a fixed landmark.

Quests: Relevant: the Prologue (Venti recovering at the tree), the Leaves on the Wind world quest, and Lupus Majoris Chapter Act I (6.4).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Windrise is unchanged: a peaceful landmark and memorial.

Nothing newer is recorded here; the Prologue-era scenes at the oak are its main canon, plus Varka's return in 6.4 (see the entry below).

217.content: At the end of Lonely Warrior (Lupus Majoris Chapter Act I, 6.4), after Varka is guided out of the ley lines by the thoughts of those who care for him, he opens his eyes at Windrise with the Knights and the Traveler gathered round him, and tells them it has been a long time.

218.comment: Windrise: Vennessa's Ascension and the Oak
218.content: Legend holds that Vennessa, the first Grand Master, was recognised by the gods for her deeds and ascended to Celestia at Windrise, taking a falcon's form. The oak is believed to have sprung up there afterwards. It is not proven, and surviving accounts of her later life disagree. The tree also has some link to the Anemo Archon's power: Venti rests beneath it to heal.

219.content:
Windwail Highland: Windwail Highland is the rustic southwestern part of Mondstadt, a country of clear springs, orchards and lush forest. It holds Springvale, a sleepy hunting village built over a spring; the Dawn Winery, the chief winery of Mondstadt, owned by the Ragnvindr family and now by Diluc; and Wolvendom, a dark forest ruled by the wolf-god Boreas and his pack, which the locals avoid.

Enemy activity is low in the orchards and high in Wolvendom, where even fearless hunters seldom venture.

Geography: Gentle hills, clear springs, orchards and forest in the southwest of Mondstadt; deeper into the highland the trees thicken into Wolvendom. The Dawn Winery lies between Springvale and the Stone Gate to Liyue, beside a lake that supplies its water. Local plants include calla lily, dandelion seed, philanemo mushroom, small lamp grass, windwheel aster and wolfhook.

Springvale faces the lake that surrounds the city. The winery is a two-storey manor on a small hill, with the vineyard circling it in rows and a few storage sheds and single-storey buildings around it. Springvale's spring is in fact melted snow and ice from Dragonspine.

Places: Springvale (dirt streets, one-storey tan houses with blue-tiled roofs, a windmill above the spring); the Dawn Winery and its manor; Wolvendom with the Wolf of the North challenge arena.

Wolvendom has an Elemental Monument and a Time Trial Challenge. The Dawn Winery has a Statue of the Seven; its sign carries the words "Whence the flow of daylight comes" above the name and "Forget not whence thou came" below (the wiki transcribes the first as "dalight").

People: Springvale: hunters such as Draff, head of the hunters, Allan and Jotun; the cook Brook, the bard Myweiss, and others. Dawn Winery: Diluc, the owner; Adelinde, head housemaid; the winemaker Connor, the warehouse manager Ernest, the farmer Tunner and maids Hillie and Moco. Wolvendom: Boreas and his pack; an NPC named Ross the Quick; and the wolf-raised boy Razor lives in the forest.

The Executive Chairman of the Mondstadt Wine Guild, Elzer, says the winery is so successful it effectively represents the whole of Mondstadt's wine trade. Several delivery staff (Fritz, Ben, Magar) and the worker Hartman are also named, along with the staff of Angel's Share, Diluc's tavern in the city.

Governance: No formal authority is shown: Springvale's hunters are led by their head; the Dawn Winery is private property of its owner, the Ragnvindr family; Wolvendom is the territory of Boreas and the pack.

Culture: Springvale has a long history of hunting, sweet spring water and a legend of a kind spirit in the waters; most residents are hunters who supply fresh meat to Mondstadt's large restaurants, and its rustic charm attracts tourists. The Dawn Winery is almost a place of pilgrimage for lovers of wine. A board in the village praises mushrooms.

The winery sells part of each year's output in Mondstadt and the rest along the trade route south of the city, and its wines are popular across Teyvat. It is rumoured to use Cryo slimes to keep its wine cellar cool. Wolves' howling can be heard from far away at night.

History: The legend of Springvale: a mother brought her gravely ill son to an empty well, where a fairy filled the well with life-saving water. The miracle drew people until a village grew over the spring. The Ragnvindr Clan has owned the Dawn Winery since Ragnvindr, about a thousand years ago, and Diluc inherited it four years before the story began, after his father Crepus died.

Wolvendom's name is archaic; in the original Chinese it means "fiefdom of running wolves", suggesting that Boreas is a lord rather than a pack leader. Boreas once mistook the first Field Tiller, wandering through the forest, for a challenger and fought it until it fled to Old Mondstadt. Rifthounds began to appear around Wolvendom as of Version 2.4, hinted by Razor's quest The Meaning of Lupical.

Atmosphere: In the day, sweet orchards, vineyards, tipsy taverns and the smell of grapes. The forest of Wolvendom is silent and dark, and at night wolves can be heard howling from far away.

Dangers: Wolvendom's wolves, hilichurls and, later, rifthounds; the unfriendly forest after dark. The Wolf of the North challenge pits fighters against Lupus Boreas, Dominator of Wolves.

The orchards and winery are peaceful by comparison.

Travel: Springvale lies south of Mondstadt City. The Dawn Winery lies between Springvale and the Stone Gate to Liyue; the winery's goods are sold along the trade route south of the city.
