Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Windwail Highland is quiet. Diluc runs the winery and Boreas still holds Wolvendom; none of the pages read records a change to the area in 7.0-7.1 content.

Diluc, who left the Knights after his father's death, has declined an invitation from Varka to return (see Mondstadt).

220.content: A peaceful hunting village south of Mondstadt City, built over a natural spring beneath its single windmill. Most residents are hunters who supply fresh meat to Mondstadt's restaurants. Legend says a fairy filled an empty well with life-saving water to cure a dying boy; in fact the spring is melted snow from Dragonspine, though an Oceanid from Fontaine really does live in it.

221.content: Mondstadt's chief winery and the Ragnvindr family estate, specialising in dandelion wine. It is a two-storey manor on a hill with vineyards around it, southwest of the city, owned by the Ragnvindrs for about a thousand years. Diluc inherited it four years before the story began, after the untimely death of his father Crepus. It is also the base of the taverns, such as Angel's Share, that the family runs.

222.content: A deep, dark and silent forest ruled by Boreas, the Wolf of the North of the Four Winds, who also appears as Andrius, with his wolf pack. Locals avoid it; the wolf-raised boy Razor lives there. Even bold hunters do not enter lightly. A challenge arena in the forest lets the Traveler fight Lupus Boreas, Dominator of Wolves.

223.content:
With Wind Comes Glory: With Wind Comes Glory is a popular souvenir shop in Mondstadt City, run by Marjorie. Adventurers can pawn precious items there for Anemo Sigils and spend the Sigils on rare goods.

Its map description calls it a popular souvenir shop and a place for able adventurers to pawn treasures, with Marjorie at their service.

Places: A shopfront with Marjorie standing just outside it. By day a music box tune plays from inside, louder the closer you stand.

Beyond souvenirs she runs a curiosities section selling gadgets for Mora, among them a Windblume Festival balloon, a Windsong Lyre and a Wind-Blessed Harpastum. In the souvenir section Anemo Sigils buy ascension materials, Mora and rarer items.

People: Marjorie is Cyrus's daughter and Iris's niece. She opened the shop to share the stories behind the treasures her father found on his adventures. She now buys treasures from adventurers and resells them as souvenirs, and orders specialised gear for them on request.

She has orange hair and eyes, a gray shirt and a dark blue skirt. Her idle lines invite customers to look around and pass on gossip about the strange wanderer near Wolvendom, who is Razor; during the Of Ballads and Brews event she says he has been seen in Springvale.

Culture: The shop treats keepsakes as stories: Marjorie's aim is to share the tales behind her father's finds. Her counter trades in Anemo Sigils rather than Mora for its rarer souvenirs.

Atmosphere: A cheerful, curio-filled shop with a music box tinkling in the daylight.

Travel: In the market district of Mondstadt City.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

224.content:
Wolvendom: Wolvendom is a deep, dark forest in Windwail Highland, Mondstadt, so silent that it chills the spine. It is the domain of Boreas, also called Andrius, the Wolf of the North of the Four Winds, and his wolf pack. Locals avoid it, and not even fearless hunters enter lightly. The boy Razor, raised by the wolves, lives here.

Boreas' physical body died long ago and now only his spirit holds the forest. In his arena there he can manifest a temporary form of ice and wind to test challengers, and he takes in wolf packs and orphaned infants as the pack's leader.

Geography: A forested part of Windwail Highland. A Teleport Waypoint and a beach facing Cider Lake lie at its edge, and Boreas' arena sits deeper in. An Elemental Monument and a time-trial challenge are found here. Local plants include calla lilies, dandelion seeds, small lamp grass and wolfhook, a plant used to treat wounded wolves.

Official text describes the howling of the wolves at night as carrying a long way. Springvale villagers readily blame the pack when wolves raid, and attacks were reported at Drunkard Gorge as well as Springvale in Razor's story quest.

People: Boreas leads the pack, which includes Pale-Furred Wolves. Razor, a boy raised by the pack, lives among them; Boreas has told him plainly that he is human, not a wolf. Ross the Quick, a traveller, can be found on the beach by the waypoint facing Cider Lake.

Varka, the Grand Master of the Knights, earned Boreas' favour by repeatedly challenging him and, as Knight of Boreas, later took Razor under his wing, teaching him human speech and swordplay. The Knights' tradition of a Knight of Boreas dates back to the wolf's early days as one of the Four Winds.

History: Boreas began as an ordinary wolf from Snezhnaya whose pack met Koitar at Amsvartnir in the far north; contact with her unknowingly blessed him with speech and divine power, and he called her his mother. He moved south, warred with Decarabian, decided he was unfit to be Archon and went back to Nod-Krai to sleep. About a thousand years later he split his soul so a part could accompany the Wandering Knight to Mondstadt; seeing it flourish, he let his body die and poured his power into the ley lines. The spirit that remains watches the land from Wolvendom.

In Chapter I Act IV (Dishonorable Trial) the Traveler found Boreas restrained by an Abyss Herald, which was trying to corrupt him as it had Dvalin; once the herald fell, Boreas explained that a Field Tiller had once blundered in and that he had taken it for a challenger, wounding it. Later, in Razor's story quest, outside riftwolves led by a black wolf were attacking villages, Boreas tested Razor and the Traveler, and told Razor not to join his pack's war since he is human; the follow-up world quest shows the pack joining the fight alongside Razor against the dark wolves.

Atmosphere: A forest of heavy shade and unnatural quiet, broken only by distant howls. It feels watched; visitors are on the wolves' terms.

Dangers: Wolves hold the area, and outsiders face Boreas' challenge. Hilichurls, Abyss Mages, Mitachurls, Anemo and Hydro Samachurls, slimes and Cryo Whopperflowers are common. Rockfond Rifthound Whelps have been seen here since version 2.4, first hinted at in Razor's quest.

In his arena Boreas takes the form of a large bluish wolf, Lupus Boreas, Dominator of Wolves. As a gameplay note, after Razor's story quest this fight is a recurring weekly challenge. The form cannot use his full strength.

Travel: Reached overland from Mondstadt City or Springvale; the waypoint on the shore is the usual way in.

Quests: Related: Chapter I Act IV (Dishonorable Trial), Lupus Minor Chapter Act I (The Meaning of Lupical), With Lupical... (Witch's Homework), and the Lupus Majoris Chapter (6.4).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the pack and Boreas' spirit still hold Wolvendom; Razor lives there.

The Wild Hunt attack seen in 6.4 was fended off and no newer event is recorded here.

225.comment: Wolvendom: Boreas' Arena and the Wolf of the North
225.content: Boreas appears in a temporary ice-and-wind wolf form to challenge those who ask. He tests conviction, as he did with Razor and the Traveler. His physical body is gone and this form cannot use his full power.

226.content:
Wyrmrest Valley: Wyrmrest Valley is a steep valley on Dragonspine, Mondstadt, where the black dragon Durin fell about 500 years ago. His skull, ribcage and heart lie there, and the life force seeping from his core has dyed the silver snow scarlet. It is cold, dangerous and eerie, and the Fatui have been interested in it.

Durin was an Abyssal dragon created by Rhinedottir. Dvalin brought him down in the cataclysm after he ravaged Mondstadt. His poisoned blood later helped drive Dvalin to become Stormterror.

Geography: A snowy ravine on Dragonspine whose slopes are stained red in places. Features: Ancient Rime, Ruin Braziers, Scarlet Quartz and Warming Seelie; a Teleport Waypoint lies at its northern edge, near where patrols station. The wiki notes the skull faces west-northwest, towards where Celestia floats.

Official text names the dragon's heart, still beating beneath the valley, as a source of warmth: it energises Strange Teeth into Empowered Dragonteeth. Dragon blood has reached Dragonspine's ley lines, and the Frostbearing Tree revived. Scarlet Quartz seems to be a gemstone formed from Durin's remains and carries his blood toxins.

People: Esther, an environmentalist, studies Dragonspine's terrain and gives out Frostshield Potions. Tommy, an adventurer, and Riese, a Knight of Favonius, are met at the border of the valley on patrol. The Dragonspine Adventurer Camp, where Orban and Iris are based, lies elsewhere on the mountain.

In The Festering Fang, Orban at the camp has the Traveler gather Strange Teeth, one of which lies beside the heart.

History: Durin was summoned by Rhinedottir as one of her miraculous creations. He is said to have had a gentle heart and to have seen his rampage as a long dream. Dvalin pierced his neck above Vindagnyr; he fell into this valley, giving the mountain the name Dragonspine.

The Fatui sought to use Durin's heart in the world quest The Festering Fang; the Traveler blocked them. Dvalin, worn and poisoned by Durin's blood, slept in Decarabian's tower until the Abyss Order deceived him.

Atmosphere: Freezing and silent, with red stains on pale snow and the sense of a vast thing lying under the earth.

Dangers: Extreme cold needs warmth or cold-resistance. Fatui Skirmishers of several elements and Cryo Cicin Mages patrol.

Travel: Reached by climbing Dragonspine from the camp.

Quests: The Festering Fang (world quest), The Gardener (Paralogism, Interlude Chapter Act IV).

Status as of 7.1: Durin's core is drained and inert as of 7.1; the dragon is replaced by the human Durin.

227.content: Before Paralogism the heart's vitality could change Strange Teeth into Empowered Dragonteeth and warm the valley. Albedo removed its core; it is now inert but still warm.
